question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

About 5,760 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) were aged 50 or over with 20 or more years of service at the August 2026 snapshot, about 21% of the 27,650 on strength. That is the pool that could become retirement-eligible within five years, not a forecast of how many will leave. By age: 50-54 has 2,483, 55-59 has 2,130, 60-64 has 850, and 65 or over has 297.

The query applied no retirement eligibility rules, so treat the pool as an upper bound on near-term retirements. It used published fields only, so no estimated figures are involved. Late reports can still shift the counts slightly.

I read "could retire" as officers aged 50 and over with 20 or more years of service; if you meant a different age or service cut, or actual retirement separations, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.age_bracket,
    workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
), detail AS (
  SELECT
    base.age_bracket,
    CASE
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years < 1 THEN 'Under 1 year'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 1 AND base.length_of_service_years < 5 THEN '1 to 4 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 5 AND base.length_of_service_years < 10 THEN '5 to 9 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 10 AND base.length_of_service_years < 15 THEN '10 to 14 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 15 AND base.length_of_service_years < 20 THEN '15 to 19 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 20 AND base.length_of_service_years < 25 THEN '20 to 24 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 25 AND base.length_of_service_years < 30 THEN '25 to 29 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 30 THEN '30+ years'
    END AS length_of_service_bracket,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount
  FROM base
  WHERE base.age_bracket IS NOT NULL
    AND base.length_of_service_years IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    base.age_bracket,
    CASE
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years < 1 THEN 'Under 1 year'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 1 AND base.length_of_service_years < 5 THEN '1 to 4 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 5 AND base.length_of_service_years < 10 THEN '5 to 9 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 10 AND base.length_of_service_years < 15 THEN '10 to 14 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 15 AND base.length_of_service_years < 20 THEN '15 to 19 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 20 AND base.length_of_service_years < 25 THEN '20 to 24 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 25 AND base.length_of_service_years < 30 THEN '25 to 29 years'
      WHEN base.length_of_service_years >= 30 THEN '30+ years'
    END
), total AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_headcount
  FROM base
  WHERE base.age_bracket IS NOT NULL
    AND base.length_of_service_years IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  detail.age_bracket,
  detail.length_of_service_bracket,
  detail.headcount,
  total.total_headcount
FROM detail
CROSS JOIN total
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS age_bracket,
  'TOTAL' AS length_of_service_bracket,
  total.total_headcount AS headcount,
  total.total_headcount
FROM total
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN age_bracket = 'TOTAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
  age_bracket,
  CASE length_of_service_bracket
    WHEN 'Under 1 year' THEN 1
    WHEN '1 to 4 years' THEN 2
    WHEN '5 to 9 years' THEN 3
    WHEN '10 to 14 years' THEN 4
    WHEN '15 to 19 years' THEN 5
    WHEN '20 to 24 years' THEN 6
    WHEN '25 to 29 years' THEN 7
    WHEN '30+ years' THEN 8
    WHEN 'TOTAL' THEN 9
    ELSE 10
  END
```

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory

TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, series 1802) had 1,041 separations in October and November 2025: 541 in October and 500 in November. Of those, 702 were quits (372 in October and 330 in November). The OPM data does not show the 1,110 figure; the gap is 69 separations, and I cannot tell from the records which scope produced that number. Late reports can still be added, so these counts may tick up slightly. Four of the 1,041 came through the 2025 deferred resignation program, all in October.

I read this as TSA screeners' separations in all categories, by effective month, for October and November 2025. If you meant all TSA occupations, I can run that for the same two months.

```sql
WITH `base` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    CASE
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      WHEN `separation_category` ILIKE 'RETIREMENT%' THEN 'RETIREMENT'
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'TERMINATION' THEN 'TERMINATION'
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT'
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 'REDUCTION IN FORCE'
      ELSE 'OTHER SEPARATION'
    END AS `separation_bucket`,
    CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS `drp_flag`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
    AND `occupational_series_code` IS NOT NULL
    AND `separation_category` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802'
    AND `effective_month` IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
), `detail` AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(`effective_month` AS STRING) AS `period`,
    `separation_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    SUM(`drp_flag`) AS `drp_separation_count`
  FROM `base`
  GROUP BY `effective_month`, `separation_bucket`
), `month_totals` AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(`effective_month` AS STRING) AS `period`,
    'TOTAL' AS `separation_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    SUM(`drp_flag`) AS `drp_separation_count`
  FROM `base`
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
), `combined_detail` AS (
  SELECT
    '2025-10 and 2025-11 combined' AS `period`,
    `separation_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    SUM(`drp_flag`) AS `drp_separation_count`
  FROM `base`
  GROUP BY `separation_bucket`
), `combined_total` AS (
  SELECT
    '2025-10 and 2025-11 combined' AS `period`,
    'TOTAL' AS `separation_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    SUM(`drp_flag`) AS `drp_separation_count`
  FROM `base`
)
SELECT `period`, `separation_bucket`, `separation_count`, `drp_separation_count`
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM `detail`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM `month_totals`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM `combined_detail`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM `combined_total`
) `x`
ORDER BY
  CASE
    WHEN `period` = '2025-10-01' THEN 1
    WHEN `period` = '2025-11-01' THEN 2
    WHEN `period` = '2025-10 and 2025-11 combined' THEN 3
    ELSE 4
  END,
  CASE
    WHEN `separation_bucket` = 'QUIT' THEN 1
    WHEN `separation_bucket` = 'RETIREMENT' THEN 2
    WHEN `separation_bucket` = 'TERMINATION' THEN 3
    WHEN `separation_bucket` = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 4
    WHEN `separation_bucket` = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 5
    WHEN `separation_bucket` = 'OTHER SEPARATION' THEN 6
    WHEN `separation_bucket` = 'TOTAL' THEN 7
    ELSE 8
  END
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory
OPM records show 94 FEMA accessions (component HSCB, all occupational series) effective October 2025 through May 2026, 40 fewer than GAO's 134. Accessions are recorded by effective month only, so the mid-May cutoff cannot be applied: the May figure of 76 is the full month of May. The monthly counts are October 1, November 8, December 1, January 5, February 0, March 2, April 1, and May 76, which sum to 94. Later OPM files can add accessions, so this count will rise slightly. I cannot tell from the data why GAO's count differs. It may use a different definition of a hire or a different cutoff, and I have not verified GAO's method.

I read "hired" as accession records effective October 2025 to May 2026 for FEMA; if you meant the plan variance for FEMA, or accessions only through May 15, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(accession.effective_month) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE 'BY_EFFECTIVE_MONTH' END AS row_type,
  accession.effective_month,
  COUNT(*) AS accession_count,
  'monthly' AS effective_date_granularity
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession` AS accession
WHERE accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSCB'
  AND accession.effective_month IS NOT NULL
  AND accession.effective_month >= DATE('2025-10-01')
  AND accession.effective_month <= DATE('2026-05-15')
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((accession.effective_month), ())
ORDER BY CASE WHEN GROUPING(accession.effective_month) = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, accession.effective_month
```

question_text: Month by month, how many CBP Officers did we hire from September 2025 to August 2026?
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, HSBD, series 1895) logged 2,456 accessions from September 2025 to August 2026. The monthly counts are below, and the total is the sum of the twelve months.

| Month (effective) | Accessions |
|---|---|
| September 2025 | 224 |
| October 2025 | 80 |
| November 2025 | 236 |
| December 2025 | 159 |
| January 2026 | 232 |
| February 2026 | 166 |
| March 2026 | 243 |
| April 2026 | 159 |
| May 2026 | 319 |
| June 2026 | 160 |
| July 2026 | 242 |
| August 2026 | 236 |

Every accession row carries an imputed location and pay, filled in from job postings because OPM redacted them. The counts themselves do not depend on those fields, but any location or pay breakdown from these rows would be estimated. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months (July and August 2026) will grow.

I read "hired" as accession actions by effective month; if you meant the plan-quarter view or separations, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT
    accession.effective_month,
    accession.location_imputed,
    accession.pay_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.accession AS accession
  WHERE accession.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND accession.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND accession.effective_month >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND accession.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    filtered.effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS accession_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN filtered.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS location_imputed_true_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN filtered.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pay_imputed_true_rows,
    MAX(CASE WHEN filtered.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS any_location_imputed_true,
    MAX(CASE WHEN filtered.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS any_pay_imputed_true
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY filtered.effective_month
), total AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS accession_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN filtered.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS location_imputed_true_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN filtered.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pay_imputed_true_rows,
    MAX(CASE WHEN filtered.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS any_location_imputed_true,
    MAX(CASE WHEN filtered.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS any_pay_imputed_true
  FROM filtered
)
SELECT
  monthly.effective_month,
  monthly.accession_count,
  monthly.location_imputed_true_rows,
  monthly.pay_imputed_true_rows,
  monthly.any_location_imputed_true,
  monthly.any_pay_imputed_true
FROM monthly

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, the largest concentrations of CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) are in Washington, District of Columbia (1,920), Sterling, Virginia (751), Ashburn, Virginia (678), El Paso, Texas (561), and Detroit, Michigan (440). Across the 189 city and state locations, the total is 27,650 officers. Every one of these locations is estimated: OPM redacted the duty station, so each city was filled in from job postings, which show where DHS hires rather than where officers sit. The masking test does not cover CBP. For FEMA and CISA, the drawn state matched the true state 11.7% and 28.2% of the time. The test flatters the method for CBP, whose staff are spread across hundreds of ports, so treat this ranking as a rough distribution, not a count of where officers work.

I read "which cities" as the full CBP Officer cell in the latest snapshot, August 2026. If you meant the open quarter, FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025), say so and I will run the December 2025 snapshot.

```sql
WITH city_counts AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.duty_station_city AS city,
    workforce_snapshot.duty_station_state AS state,
    workforce_snapshot.location_imputed,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.duty_station_city IS NOT NULL
    AND workforce_snapshot.duty_station_state IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    workforce_snapshot.duty_station_city,
    workforce_snapshot.duty_station_state,
    workforce_snapshot.location_imputed
)
SELECT
  city_counts.city,
  city_counts.state,
  city_counts.headcount,
  city_counts.location_imputed,
  SUM(city_counts.headcount) OVER () AS total_headcount
FROM city_counts
ORDER BY city_counts.headcount DESC, city_counts.city ASC, city_counts.state ASC, city_counts.location_imputed ASC;
```

question_text: Add up the first three quarters of FY2026: how far behind plan is each component on hiring?
answer_text:
Verified

Across the twelve components, DHS accessioned 17,370 against 15,064 planned hires over FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (October 2025 to June 2026), 2,306 (15.3%) ahead of plan. Eight components are behind, led by Protective-type cells such as S&T, CISA and FEMA, which are each about 92 to 94% short; CBP, ICE, Secret Service and FLETC are ahead.

| Component | Planned | Accessions | Variance | Variance % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Science and Technology (HSFA) | 18 | 1 | -17 | -94.4% |
| Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (HSCA) | 303 | 18 | -285 | -94.1% |
| FEMA (HSCB) | 2,043 | 147 | -1,896 | -92.8% |
| Office of the Inspector General (HSAE) | 36 | 5 | -31 | -86.1% |
| Coast Guard civilian (HSAC) | 567 | 198 | -369 | -65.1% |
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 441 | 228 | -213 | -48.3% |
| TSA (HSBC) | 2,368 | 1,336 | -1,032 | -43.6% |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 1,203 | 1,053 | -150 | -12.5% |
| CBP (HSBD) | 4,182 | 5,734 | +1,552 | +37.1% |
| Secret Service (HSAD) | 627 | 884 | +257 | +41.0% |
| FLETC (HSBE) | 90 | 193 | +103 | +114.4% |
| ICE (HSBB) | 3,186 | 7,573 | +4,387 | +137.7% |

Late OPM files keep adding accessions, so the shortfalls will narrow somewhat. ICE's FY2026 Q1 figure (6,185 accessions against 1,062 planned) drives much of the surplus, so check it before quoting. The CISA second-quarter figure came from the DHS total less the other eleven components, because that one call failed twice; reconcile it before quoting. I read "behind plan" as accessions minus planned hires summed over the three quarters; if you meant one quarter or separations, say so.

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory

Higher-grade CBP Officer postings did not stay open longer. Across the 469 CBP Officer announcements (series 1895, CBP) opened from September 2025 to October 2026, grades 12 to 15 had median advertised windows of 6 days, while grade 5 had a median of 30 days and grade 9 a median of 28. Grade 13 has one outlier that stayed open 181 days. The grade 5 and grade 9 groups are small (14 and 22 postings), so those medians are less firm than the grade 12 to 15 figures.

| Minimum grade | Postings | Average days open | Median days open |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | 6 | 13.3 | 13 |
| 5 | 14 | 29.3 | 30 |
| 9 | 22 | 22.4 | 28 |
| 11 | 1 | 6.0 | 6 |
| 12 | 57 | 7.7 | 6 |
| 13 | 211 | 7.4 | 6 |
| 14 | 126 | 5.8 | 6 |
| 15 | 32 | 6.4 | 6 |

These durations are the advertised open-to-close windows, not the time until someone was hired; postings are not linked to hires in the data, so time to fill cannot be measured. I read this as the advertised window for all CBP Officer postings opened in that range, grouped by minimum grade; if you meant time to fill, or postings for another occupation, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered_postings` AS (
  SELECT
    `minimum_grade`,
    datediff(`close_date`, `open_date`) AS `duration_days`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` ILIKE '%HSBD%'
    AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `close_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `minimum_grade` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `open_date` <= DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND (
      array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1895')
      OR `series` = '1895'
    )
), `by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `minimum_grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `number_of_postings`,
    AVG(`duration_days`) AS `average_duration_days`,
    percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY `duration_days`) AS `median_duration_days`,
    MIN(`duration_days`) AS `minimum_duration_days`,
    MAX(`duration_days`) AS `maximum_duration_days`
  FROM `filtered_postings`
  GROUP BY `minimum_grade`
), `overall` AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS `total_number_of_postings`,
    AVG(`duration_days`) AS `overall_average_duration_days`
  FROM `filtered_postings`
)
SELECT
  `by_grade`.`minimum_grade`,
  `by_grade`.`number_of_postings`,
  `by_grade`.`average_duration_days`,
  `by_grade`.`median_duration_days`,
  `by_grade`.`minimum_duration_days`,
  `by_grade`.`maximum_duration_days`,
  `overall`.`total_number_of_postings`,
  `overall`.`overall_average_duration_days`
FROM `by_grade`
CROSS JOIN `overall`
ORDER BY CAST(`by_grade`.`minimum_grade` AS INT) ASC, `by_grade`.`minimum_grade` ASC
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) retired 586 times in the twelve effective months from September 2025 through August 2026, and December 2025 was the peak month with 152 (26% of the total). None of these retirements came through the 2025 deferred resignation program. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months (June to August 2026) will grow.

| Effective month | Retirements |
|---|---|
| September 2025 | 54 |
| October 2025 | 36 |
| November 2025 | 24 |
| December 2025 | 152 |
| January 2026 | 44 |
| February 2026 | 26 |
| March 2026 | 31 |
| April 2026 | 45 |
| May 2026 | 52 |
| June 2026 | 46 |
| July 2026 | 45 |
| August 2026 | 31 |
| **Total** | **586** |

The monthly figures add to the total of 586. I read "in the year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026, counting all three retirement categories together (voluntary, early out, and other). If you meant a single retirement category, or the calendar year 2025 only, say so.

```sql
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `retirement_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `drp_retirement_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'N' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `non_drp_retirement_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `separation_category` IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'RETIREMENT - OTHER')
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT `effective_month`, `retirement_count`, `drp_retirement_count`, `non_drp_retirement_count`
FROM (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    `retirement_count`,
    `drp_retirement_count`,
    `non_drp_retirement_count`,
    0 AS `sort_key`
  FROM monthly
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS `effective_month`,
    SUM(`retirement_count`) AS `retirement_count`,
    SUM(`drp_retirement_count`) AS `drp_retirement_count`,
    SUM(`non_drp_retirement_count`) AS `non_drp_retirement_count`,
    1 AS `sort_key`
  FROM monthly
) t
ORDER BY `sort_key`, `effective_month`
```

question_text: How many CBP Officers who left this year had less than one year of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory
138 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) separated with less than one year of service from January to August 2026, out of 591 separations in those months. By category, that is 63 other separations, 59 quits, 14 terminations (expired appointment or other), and 2 transfers out to another individual position, which sum to 138. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly.

I read "this year" as calendar 2026 to date (January to August 2026); if you meant the trailing twelve months to August 2026, say so and I will rerun it.

```sql
WITH `base` AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
),
`under_one` AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM `base`
  WHERE `length_of_service_years` < 1
),
`under_one_by_category` AS (
  SELECT
    `separation_category`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`
  FROM `under_one`
  WHERE `separation_category` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `separation_category`
)
SELECT
  'under_1_year_total' AS `result_type`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `separation_category`,
  COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`
FROM `under_one`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'all_separations_total' AS `result_type`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `separation_category`,
  COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`
FROM `base`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'under_1_year_by_category' AS `result_type`,
  `separation_category`,
  `separation_count`
FROM `under_one_by_category`
ORDER BY `result_type`, `separation_count` DESC, `separation_category`

I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026 and "senior executives" as the Senior Executive Service pay plan; if you meant calendar 2026 or the count of executives on hand, say so.

```sql
SELECT

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers do not leave at a higher rate simply because they are higher-graded. In the trailing twelve months to August 2026, the rate is highest in the lowest grades and at grade 15, and sits near 3 to 4% across grades 09 to 14.

| Grade | Headcount, Sep 2025 to Aug 2026 | Separations | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | 36 to 28 | 7 | 21.9% |
| 05 | 412 to 898 | 67 | 10.2% |
| 07 | 863 to 1,234 | 81 | 7.7% |
| 09 | 1,429 to 1,661 | 61 | 3.9% |
| 11 | 1,125 to 1,270 | 8 | 0.7% |
| 12 | 17,520 to 17,130 | 550 | 3.2% |
| 13 | 4,251 to 4,375 | 136 | 3.2% |
| 14 | 834 to 866 | 32 | 3.8% |
| 15 | 174 to 188 | 12 | 6.6% |
| All grades | 26,644 to 27,650 | 954 | 3.5% |

Grades 00, 05, 07 and 15 are small or thin, so their rates are noisy; grade 12 alone carries 550 of the 954 separations. The 2025 deferred resignation program flags no separations in this window, so the rate with and without that wave is the same. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly. The rate is separations divided by the average of the September 2025 and August 2026 headcounts. My first pass used an August 2025 start snapshot that the records do not hold and returned zero starting headcount, so I reran it with September 2025; the table above is the corrected run.

I read "higher-graded" as the pay grade on the OPM record and "leaving" as the trailing twelve-month separation rate to August 2026. If you meant a count of separations or grades grouped into bands, say so.

```sql
WITH sep_by_grade AS (
  SELECT
    separation.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS separations_excluding_drp
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.effective_month >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND separation.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY separation.grade
),
start_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_start
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
end_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_end
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.grade, start_hc.grade, end_hc.grade) AS grade,
    COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) AS headcount_start,
    COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0) AS headcount_end,
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations, 0) AS separations,
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations_excluding_drp, 0) AS separations_excluding_drp
  FROM sep_by_grade
  FULL OUTER JOIN start_hc
    ON sep_by_grade.grade = start_hc.grade
  FULL OUTER JOIN end_hc
    ON COALESCE(sep_by_grade.grade, start_hc.grade) = end_hc.grade
),
final_rows AS (
  SELECT
    base.grade AS grade,
    base.headcount_start AS headcount_start,
    base.headcount_end AS headcount_end,
    base.separations AS separations,
    CASE
      WHEN (base.headcount_start + base.headcount_end) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE 100 * try_divide(base.separations, (try_divide((base.headcount_start + base.headcount_end),2.0)))
    END AS rate,
    base.separations_excluding_drp AS separations_excluding_drp,
    CASE
      WHEN (base.headcount_start + base.headcount_end) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE 100 * try_divide(base.separations_excluding_drp, (try_divide((base.headcount_start + base.headcount_end),2.0)))
    END AS rate_excluding_drp
  FROM base

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'TOTAL' AS grade,
    SUM(base.headcount_start) AS headcount_start,
    SUM(base.headcount_end) AS headcount_end,
    SUM(base.separations) AS separations,
    CASE
      WHEN (SUM(base.headcount_start) + SUM(base.headcount_end)) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE 100 * try_divide(SUM(base.separations), (try_divide((SUM(base.headcount_start) + SUM(base.headcount_end)),2.0)))
    END AS rate,
    SUM(base.separations_excluding_drp) AS separations_excluding_drp,
    CASE
      WHEN (SUM(base.headcount_start) + SUM(base.headcount_end)) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE 100 * try_divide(SUM(base.separations_excluding_drp), (try_divide((SUM(base.headcount_start) + SUM(base.headcount_end)),2.0)))
    END AS rate_excluding_drp
  FROM base
)
SELECT
  final_rows.grade AS grade,
  final_rows.headcount_start AS headcount_start,
  final_rows.headcount_end AS headcount_end,
  final_rows.separations AS separations,
  final_rows.rate AS rate,

FROM final_rows
ORDER BY CASE WHEN final_rows.grade = 'TOTAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, final_rows.grade ASC

params.question: For CBP Officers (component HSBD, occupational series 1895), compute the trailing twelve-month separation rate to August 2026 by grade. Use effective months from 2025-09-01 through 2026-08-01 for separations. For each grade, rate = separations in that grade / average of headcount at the 2025-08-01 snapshot and headcount at the 2026-08-01 snapshot for that grade. Return one row per grade with: grade, headcount_start (2025-08-01), headcount_end (2026-08-01), separations, rate, separations excluding the 2025 deferred resignation program wave, and rate excluding that wave. Order by grade ascending. Include the total row across all grades as well.

For CBP Officers (component HSBD, occupational series 1895), compute the trailing twelve-month separation rate to August 2026 by grade. Separations are those with effective_month from 2025-09-01 through 2026-08-01. Headcount_start is the workforce snapshot at 2025-09-01 (the earliest snapshot available), and headcount_end is the snapshot at 2026-08-01, both by grade. Rate = separations in that grade / ((headcount_start + headcount_end) / 2). Return one row per grade with: grade, headcount_start, headcount_end, separations, rate, separations excluding rows flagged as 2025 deferred resignation program (DRP) separations, and rate excluding DRP. Order by grade ascending, and include a TOTAL row across all grades.

genie_sql:
WITH sep_by_grade AS (
  SELECT
    separation.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS separations_excluding_drp
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.effective_month >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND separation.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY separation.grade
),
start_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_start
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
end_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_end
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.grade, start_hc.grade, end_hc.grade) AS grade,
    COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) AS headcount_start,
    COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0) AS headcount_end,
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations, 0) AS separations,
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations_excluding_drp, 0) AS separations_excluding_drp
  FROM sep_by_grade
  FULL OUTER JOIN start_hc
    ON sep_by_grade.grade = start_hc.grade
  FULL OUTER JOIN end_hc
    ON COALESCE(sep_by_grade.grade, start_hc.grade) = end_hc.grade
),
final_rows AS (
  SELECT
    base.grade AS grade,
    base.headcount_start AS headcount_start,
    base.headcount_end AS headcount_end,
    base.separations AS separations,
    CASE
      WHEN (base.headcount_start + base.headcount_end) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE 100 * try_divide(base.separations, (try_divide((base.headcount_start + base.headcount_end),2.0)))
    END AS rate,
    base.separations_excluding_drp AS separations_excluding_drp,
    CASE
      WHEN (base.headcount_start + base.headcount_end) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE 100 * try_divide(base.separations_excluding_drp, (try_divide((base.headcount_start + base.headcount_end),2.0)))
    END AS rate_excluding_drp
  FROM base

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'TOTAL' AS grade,
    SUM(base.headcount_start) AS headcount_start,
    SUM(base.headcount_end) AS headcount_end,
    SUM(base.separations) AS separations,
    CASE
      WHEN (SUM(base.headcount_start) + SUM(base.headcount_end)) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE 100 * try_divide(SUM(base.separations), (try_divide((SUM(base.headcount_start) + SUM(base.headcount_end)),2.0)))
    END AS rate,
    SUM(base.separations_excluding_drp) AS separations_excluding_drp,
    CASE
      WHEN (SUM(base.headcount_start) + SUM(base.headcount_end)) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE 100 * try_divide(SUM(base.separations_excluding_drp), (try_divide((SUM(base.headcount_start) + SUM(base.headcount_end)),2.0)))
    END AS rate_excluding_drp
  FROM base
)
SELECT
  final_rows.grade AS grade,
  final_rows.headcount_start AS headcount_start,
  final_rows.headcount_end AS headcount_end,
  final_rows.separations AS separations,
  final_rows.rate AS rate,
  final_rows.separations_excluding_drp AS separations_excluding_drp,
  final_rows.rate_excluding_drp AS rate_excluding_drp
FROM final_rows
ORDER BY CASE WHEN final_rows.grade = 'TOTAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, final_rows.grade ASC

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

On the August 2026 snapshot, about 3,277 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) are aged 55 or over with 20 or more years of service, the core group who could retire within five years. Adding the 2,483 aged 50 to 54 with 20 or more years, who reach 55 within the window, gives about 5,760. Those two figures are 11.9% and 20.8% of the 27,650 CBP Officers on the snapshot.

| Age bracket | 20+ years service | 10 to 20 years service |
|---|---|---|
| 50-54 | 2,483 | 900 |
| 55-59 | 2,130 | 378 |
| 60-64 | 850 | 190 |
| 65 or more | 297 | 50 |

The records do not hold retirement eligibility rules, so the cut-offs are a proxy built from age and service only. Actual departures depend on take-up, and the 10-to-20-year group adds more people as they pass 20 years. The tool's summary text gave a grand total of 29,650, but its own rows sum to 27,650 (I added them, and the age and service totals agree). The rows carry estimated location and pay fields, but these counts do not depend on them. I read "could retire" as age 55 or over with 20 or more years' service, with the 50 to 54 group as the five-year edge; if you meant the plan's exact eligibility rules, or actual retirement separations, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%20-24%' THEN '20-24'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%25-29%' THEN '25-29'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%30-34%' THEN '30-34'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%35-39%' THEN '35-39'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%40-44%' THEN '40-44'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%45-49%' THEN '45-49'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%50-54%' THEN '50-54'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%55-59%' THEN '55-59'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%60-64%' THEN '60-64'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%65%' THEN '65 or more'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS `age_bucket`,
    CASE
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20 or more'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS `service_bucket`,
    COALESCE(`location_imputed`, FALSE) AS `location_imputed`,
    COALESCE(`pay_imputed`, FALSE) AS `pay_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
), filtered AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM base
  WHERE `age_bucket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(`age_bucket`, 'Total') AS `age_bucket`,
  COALESCE(`service_bucket`, 'Total') AS `service_bucket`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `location_imputed_headcount`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `pay_imputed_headcount`
FROM filtered
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((`age_bucket`, `service_bucket`), (`age_bucket`), (`service_bucket`), ())
ORDER BY
  CASE COALESCE(`age_bucket`, 'Total')
    WHEN '20-24' THEN 1
    WHEN '25-29' THEN 2
    WHEN '30-34' THEN 3
    WHEN '35-39' THEN 4
    WHEN '40-44' THEN 5
    WHEN '45-49' THEN 6
    WHEN '50-54' THEN 7
    WHEN '55-59' THEN 8
    WHEN '60-64' THEN 9
    WHEN '65 or more' THEN 10
    WHEN 'Total' THEN 11
    ELSE 12
  END,
  CASE COALESCE(`service_bucket`, 'Total')
    WHEN 'under 1' THEN 1
    WHEN '1-3' THEN 2
    WHEN '3-5' THEN 3
    WHEN '5-10' THEN 4
    WHEN '10-20' THEN 5
    WHEN '20 or more' THEN 6
    WHEN 'Total' THEN 7
    ELSE 8
  END;
```

FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency) missed its FY2026 Q1 hiring plan by the most in headcount: 10 accessions against 681 planned, a shortfall of 671 (98.5%) in October to December 2025. TSA (Transportation Security Administration) was next at 310 short, and USCIS (Citizenship and Immigration Services) at 201 short. ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) overshot its plan by the most, with 6,185 accessions against 1,062 planned.

| USCIS (HSAB) | 401 | 200 | -201 | -50.1% |
| Coast Guard civilian (HSAC) | 189 | 76 | -113 | -59.8% |

| CBP (HSBD) | 1,257 | 1,385 | +128 | +10.2% |

The plan is the staffing plan, and these counts are right-censored: late OPM reports keep adding accessions to October to December 2025, so the shortfalls will narrow somewhat. question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory

OPM records show 1,041 separations of TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, series 1802) with effective dates in October and November 2025: 541 in October and 500 in November. That is 69 fewer than the 1,110 reported to Congress, and I cannot reconcile the gap from these records. Of the 1,041, 702 were quits (372 in October, 330 in November), about 67% of separations. Quits are matched exactly, so that count is sound. The query's other category buckets do not add up to the totals (for example, transfers and terminations were not separated out), so quote only the totals and quits. Late reports can still add a few separations for these months.

I read this as all separations of TSA screeners with effective months in October and November 2025; if you meant only quits or a twelve-month rate, say so.

```sql
WITH `base` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    CASE
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      WHEN `separation_category` ILIKE 'RETIREMENT%' THEN `separation_category`
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'TERMINATION' THEN 'TERMINATION'
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT'
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 'REDUCTION IN FORCE'
      ELSE 'OTHER SEPARATION'
    END AS `category_bucket`,
    CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS `drp_flag`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
    AND `occupational_series_code` IS NOT NULL
    AND `separation_category` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802'
    AND `effective_month` IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
), `monthly` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `total_separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'QUIT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `quit_separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_flag` = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `drp_flagged_separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'QUIT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `quit_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `retirement_voluntary_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `retirement_early_out_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'TERMINATION' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `termination_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `transfer_out_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `reduction_in_force_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'OTHER SEPARATION' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `other_separation_count`
  FROM `base`
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
), `combined` AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `total_separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'QUIT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `quit_separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_flag` = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `drp_flagged_separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'QUIT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `quit_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `retirement_voluntary_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `retirement_early_out_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'TERMINATION' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `termination_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `transfer_out_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `reduction_in_force_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `category_bucket` = 'OTHER SEPARATION' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `other_separation_count`
  FROM `base`
)
SELECT
  CAST(`effective_month` AS STRING) AS `month_label`,
  `total_separations`,
  `quit_separations`,
  `drp_flagged_separations`,
  `quit_count`,
  `retirement_voluntary_count`,
  `retirement_early_out_count`,
  `termination_count`,
  `transfer_out_count`,
  `reduction_in_force_count`,
  `other_separation_count`
FROM `monthly`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'BOTH_MONTHS' AS `month_label`,
  `total_separations`,
  `quit_separations`,
  `drp_flagged_separations`,
  `quit_count`,
  `retirement_voluntary_count`,
  `retirement_early_out_count`,
  `termination_count`,
  `transfer_out_count`,
  `reduction_in_force_count`,
  `other_separation_count`
FROM `combined`
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `month_label` = '2025-10-01' THEN 1 WHEN `month_label` = '2025-11-01' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory

OPM accession records show 94 FEMA accessions (component HSCB, all occupational series) with effective months from October 2025 through May 2026, against GAO's 134. That is 40 fewer, or about 70 percent of GAO's figure. OPM dates are monthly, so the mid-May cutoff cannot be applied; the count includes all of May 2026. By month: October 2025 1, November 8, December 1, January 2026 5, February 0, March 2, April 1, May 76. Over four-fifths of the count falls in May, so that month deserves a check. Late OPM files keep adding accessions, so the count will rise. Some rows carry estimated location and pay (November 2025 and May 2026), filled in from job postings. The gap may come from GAO counting a different action type, such as transfers in, which this count includes.

I read "hired" as all accessions (new hires, transfers in, and SES) effective October 2025 through May 2026; if you meant new hires only, say so and I will narrow it by accession category.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    `location_imputed`,
    `pay_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSCB'
    AND `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-05-15'
)
SELECT
  CAST('TOTAL' AS STRING) AS `period`,
  CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS `effective_month`,
  COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`,
  MAX(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `any_location_imputed_true`,
  MAX(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `any_pay_imputed_true`
FROM `filtered`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  CAST('MONTH' AS STRING) AS `period`,
  `effective_month`,
  COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`,
  MAX(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `any_location_imputed_true`,
  MAX(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `any_pay_imputed_true`
FROM `filtered`
GROUP BY `effective_month`
ORDER BY `period`, `effective_month`
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory
As of the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, 1802) averaged $74,762.38 in annual basic pay across 46,913 employees, and CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) averaged $104,655.83 across 27,650. CBP Officers averaged $29,893.45 more, about 40% above the TSA screener figure.
Pay for about 90% of TSA screener rows (42,225 of 46,913) and for all CBP Officer rows is estimated from job postings, because OPM redacted it, so treat both averages as estimates.
I read "average salary" as the mean annual basic pay in the August 2026 snapshot, unweighted by grade; if you meant a different snapshot or a median, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_annual_basic_pay`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `imputed_pay_row_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
  AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND `occupational_series_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND ((`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802')
    OR (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'))
GROUP BY
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`
ORDER BY `agency_subelement_code`, `occupational_series_code`
```

These city locations are all estimated, not published by OPM: they were filled in from job postings, which show where DHS hires rather than where officers sit. The masking test that measures how reliable this method is has not been run for this answer; I can pull it if you need it to quote. question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory

889 USAJOBS postings listed Border Patrol Agent (series 1896) among their series, counting multi-series postings, with an open date between September 1, 2025 and October 31, 2026, across all of DHS. Postings are counted once each by control number. Because the count is by open date, postings that opened before September 2025 are excluded even if they were open during the window.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT `control_number`) AS `distinct_posting_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
WHERE `open_date` BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-01' AND DATE '2026-10-31'
  AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1896')
```

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. In the USAJOBS postings for CBP Officers (1895) opened from September 2025 to October 2026, the higher-grade announcements closed faster, not slower. Grades 12 to 15 averaged 5.8 to 7.7 days open, while grades 5 and 9 averaged 29.3 and 22.4 days. Grade 13 has the most postings (211), and grade 9 has 22 and grade 5 has 14, so the two slow groups are small.

These are the planned open windows (open date to close date), not how long a posting stayed live before it was filled or cancelled. Postings filled early are not in the data, so the figures are an upper bound on time open. The query's imputed-location and imputed-pay flags were set to constant false in the generated query, so I cannot confirm from this result that no posting is estimated.

I read "stay open longer" as the average days between open and close dates by grade; if you meant time to fill or the count still open on a date, say so.

```sql
WITH postings AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(job_posting.minimum_grade, job_posting.maximum_grade) AS grade,
    DATEDIFF(job_posting.close_date, job_posting.open_date) AS days_open,
    CAST(false AS BOOLEAN) AS location_imputed,
    CAST(false AS BOOLEAN) AS pay_imputed
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE job_posting.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND job_posting.open_date >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND job_posting.open_date <= DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND job_posting.open_date IS NOT NULL
    AND job_posting.close_date IS NOT NULL
    AND COALESCE(job_posting.minimum_grade, job_posting.maximum_grade) IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      array_contains(job_posting.occupational_series_codes, '1895')
      OR job_posting.series = '1895'
    )
)
SELECT
  postings.grade,
  COUNT(*) AS posting_count,
  AVG(postings.days_open) AS avg_days_open,
  percentile_approx(postings.days_open, 0.5) AS median_days_open,
  MAX(CASE WHEN postings.location_imputed THEN true ELSE false END) AS any_location_imputed_true,
  MAX(CASE WHEN postings.pay_imputed THEN true ELSE false END) AS any_pay_imputed_true
FROM postings
GROUP BY postings.grade
ORDER BY postings.grade
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) retired 586 times in the twelve months from September 2025 to August 2026, peaking in December 2025 (152) and running at 24 to 54 a month in every other month. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months, especially August 2026, will grow. I did not split out the 2025 deferred resignation program wave, so I cannot say how much of the September and December peaks it accounts for; a one-off query can split it. The data also holds three retirements from earlier years, all in single digits by month.

I read "the year" as the twelve months September 2025 to August 2026, counting all three retirement categories; if you meant the pattern across all years in the data, or early-out versus voluntary retirements separately, say so.

```sql
WITH `all_months` AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT `effective_month`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
),
`monthly_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `retirement_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `separation_category` IN (
      'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY',
      'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT',
      'RETIREMENT - OTHER'
    )
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
),
`monthly_output` AS (
  SELECT
    `all_months`.`effective_month` AS `effective_month`,
    COALESCE(`monthly_counts`.`retirement_count`, 0) AS `retirement_count`
  FROM `all_months`
  LEFT JOIN `monthly_counts`
    ON `all_months`.`effective_month` = `monthly_counts`.`effective_month`
)
SELECT
  `effective_month`,
  `retirement_count`
FROM `monthly_output`
UNION ALL
SELECT

question_text: Which DHS components lost the most senior executives this year?
answer_text:
Exploratory

DHS Headquarters lost the most senior executives over the trailing twelve months to August 2026 (57 separations), followed by FEMA (44), ICE (37), CBP (31), and USCIS (30). Across all of DHS there were 273 senior executive separations, and TSA recorded none.

| Component (code) | Senior executive separations |
|---|---|
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 57 |
| FEMA (HSCB) | 44 |
| ICE (HSBB) | 37 |
| CBP (HSBD) | 31 |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 30 |
| CISA (HSCA) | 27 |
| U.S. Secret Service (HSAD) | 23 |
| Science and Technology Directorate (HSFA) | 8 |
| U.S. Coast Guard (HSAC) | 7 |
| FLETC (HSBE) | 4 |
| Domestic Nuclear Detection Office (HSDA) | 3 |
| Office of the Inspector General (HSAE) | 2 |
| TSA (HSBC) | 0 |

Of the 273, 124 were voluntary retirements, 50 early-out retirements, 56 quits, and 43 other categories. Several components' senior executive records carry estimated location or pay (DHS Headquarters, ICE, CBP, USCIS, Secret Service, Coast Guard, FLETC, and the Inspector General); the counts themselves do not depend on those fields. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will rise slightly. These are counts, not rates, and the figures include the 2025 deferred resignation wave. I read "this year" as the twelve effective months September 2025 to August 2026 and "senior executives" as the Senior Executive Service pay plan (ES); if you meant the fiscal year to date (October 2025 to August 2026) or a rate per senior executive, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered_sep` AS (
  SELECT
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    `agency_subelement`,
    `separation_category`,
    `location_imputed`,
    `pay_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `pay_plan_code` = 'ES'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
),
`by_component` AS (
  SELECT
    c.`agency_subelement_code`,
    c.`agency_subelement`,
    COUNT(f.`agency_subelement_code`) AS `separation_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.`separation_category` = 'QUIT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `quit_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.`separation_category` = 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `retirement_voluntary_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.`separation_category` = 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `retirement_early_out_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.`separation_category` = 'TERMINATION' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `termination_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.`separation_category` = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `transfer_out_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.`separation_category` IS NOT NULL AND f.`separation_category` NOT IN ('QUIT', 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'TERMINATION', 'TRANSFER OUT') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `other_category_count`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN f.`location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS `any_location_imputed`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN f.`pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS `any_pay_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`component` c
  LEFT JOIN `filtered_sep` f
    ON c.`agency_subelement_code` = f.`agency_subelement_code`
  WHERE c.`agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
    AND c.`agency_subelement` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.`agency_subelement_code`, c.`agency_subelement`
),
`total_row` AS (
  SELECT
    'ALL' AS `agency_subelement_code`,
    'All components' AS `agency_subelement`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `separation_category` = 'QUIT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `quit_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `separation_category` = 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `retirement_voluntary_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `separation_category` = 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `retirement_early_out_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `separation_category` = 'TERMINATION' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `termination_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `separation_category` = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `transfer_out_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `separation_category` IS NOT NULL AND `separation_category` NOT IN ('QUIT', 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'TERMINATION', 'TRANSFER OUT') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `other_category_count`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS `any_location_imputed`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS `any_pay_imputed`
  FROM `filtered_sep`
)
SELECT *
FROM (
  SELECT
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    `agency_subelement`,
    `separation_count`,
    `quit_count`,
    `retirement_voluntary_count`,
    `retirement_early_out_count`,
    `termination_count`,
    `transfer_out_count`,
    `other_category_count`,
    `any_location_imputed`,
    `any_pay_imputed`,
    0 AS `sort_total`
  FROM `by_component`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    `agency_subelement`,
    `separation_count`,
    `quit_count`,
    `retirement_voluntary_count`,
    `retirement_early_out_count`,
    `termination_count`,
    `transfer_out_count`,
    `other_category_count`,
    `any_location_imputed`,
    `any_pay_imputed`,
    1 AS `sort_total`
  FROM `total_row`
) q
ORDER BY `sort_total`, `separation_count` DESC, `agency_subelement_code`
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

Higher grades are not leaving CBP Officer (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) positions faster than mid-grades. In the trailing twelve months to August 2026, grades 12 to 14 separated at about 3.2% to 3.8%, while the lowest grades left fastest: 10.2% at grade 05 and 7.7% at grade 07. Grade 15 is higher at 6.6%, but it rests on 12 separations against about 181 average staff.

| Grade | Separations | Average headcount | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 05 | 67 | 655 | 10.2% |
| 07 | 81 | 1,049 | 7.7% |
| 09 | 61 | 1,545 | 3.9% |
| 11 | 8 | 1,198 | 0.7% |
| 12 | 550 | 17,325 | 3.2% |
| 13 | 136 | 4,313 | 3.2% |
| 14 | 32 | 850 | 3.8% |
| 15 | 12 | 181 | 6.6% |

Grade 00 (7 separations on about 32 average staff, 21.9%) is too small to read. The 2025 deferred resignation wave shows no separations for these officers in this window, so the rate with and without it is the same. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly.

I read "higher-graded" as grade 12 and above, and "lower grades" as 05 to 09; if you meant separation counts by grade, or a different grade cut, say so.

```sql
WITH sep_by_grade AS (
  SELECT
    separation.grade,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS drp_separations
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.effective_month >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND separation.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY separation.grade
),
start_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_start
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
end_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_end
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
all_grades AS (
  SELECT sep_by_grade.grade FROM sep_by_grade
  UNION
  SELECT start_hc.grade FROM start_hc
  UNION
  SELECT end_hc.grade FROM end_hc
)
SELECT
  all_grades.grade,
  COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations, 0) AS separations,
  COALESCE(sep_by_grade.drp_separations, 0) AS drp_separations,
  COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) AS headcount_start,
  COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0) AS headcount_end,
  100 * try_divide(
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations, 0),
    try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0)),2.0)
  ) AS separation_rate,
  100 * try_divide(
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations, 0) - COALESCE(sep_by_grade.drp_separations, 0),
    try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0)),2.0)
  ) AS separation_rate_excluding_drp,
  CASE
    WHEN (start_hc.grade IS NOT NULL OR end_hc.grade IS NOT NULL) AND sep_by_grade.grade IS NOT NULL THEN 'snapshot_and_separation'
    WHEN (start_hc.grade IS NOT NULL OR end_hc.grade IS NOT NULL) AND sep_by_grade.grade IS NULL THEN 'snapshot'
    WHEN (start_hc.grade IS NULL AND end_hc.grade IS NULL) AND sep_by_grade.grade IS NOT NULL THEN 'separation'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS row_source
FROM all_grades
LEFT JOIN sep_by_grade
  ON all_grades.grade = sep_by_grade.grade
LEFT JOIN start_hc
  ON all_grades.grade = start_hc.grade
LEFT JOIN end_hc
  ON all_grades.grade = end_hc.grade
ORDER BY all_grades.grade
```

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

About 5,760 CBP Officers (HSBD, 1895) could reach retirement age within five years, as of the August 2026 snapshot. That is 3,277 already aged 55 and over with 20 or more years of service, plus 2,483 aged 50 to 54 with 20 or more years who reach 55 within the window. The 5,760 is an upper bound, about 21% of the 27,650 officers in the cell. The records I could reach do not show retirement plan coverage, so these are age and service groupings, not confirmed eligibility.

| Age bracket | 20+ years of service | Role in the count |
|---|---|---|
| 50-54 | 2,483 | Reach 55 within five years |
| 55-59 | 2,130 | Already 55 or over |
| 60-64 | 850 | Already 55 or over |
| 65 or more | 297 | Already 55 or over |

Late reports keep arriving, so these headcounts are as of the snapshot and carry no separation adjustment. I read this as officers aged 50 and over with 20 or more years of service, counted in the August 2026 headcount; if you meant a different service threshold or the separation counts for retirements, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.age_bracket,
    CASE
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 1 THEN 'under 1'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 1 AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 3 AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 5 AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 10 AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 20 THEN '20 and over'
    END AS service_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%under 20%' THEN 1
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%20-24%' THEN 2
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%25-29%' THEN 3
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%30-34%' THEN 4
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%35-39%' THEN 5
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%40-44%' THEN 6
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%45-49%' THEN 7
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%50-54%' THEN 8
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%55-59%' THEN 9
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%60-64%' THEN 10
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.age_bracket ILIKE '%65%' THEN 11
      ELSE 99
    END AS age_sort
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.age_bracket IS NOT NULL
    AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years IS NOT NULL
), by_age AS (
  SELECT
    base.age_bracket,
    base.age_sort,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.service_bucket = 'under 1' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS under_1,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.service_bucket = '1-3' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `1_3`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.service_bucket = '3-5' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `3_5`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.service_bucket = '5-10' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `5_10`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.service_bucket = '10-20' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `10_20`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.service_bucket = '20 and over' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `20_and_over`,
    COUNT(*) AS total
  FROM base
  GROUP BY base.age_bracket, base.age_sort
), final_rows AS (
  SELECT
    by_age.age_bracket,
    by_age.age_sort,
    by_age.under_1,
    by_age.`1_3`,
    by_age.`3_5`,
    by_age.`5_10`,
    by_age.`10_20`,
    by_age.`20_and_over`,
    by_age.total
  FROM by_age
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'Total' AS age_bracket,
    999 AS age_sort,
    SUM(by_age.under_1) AS under_1,
    SUM(by_age.`1_3`) AS `1_3`,
    SUM(by_age.`3_5`) AS `3_5`,
    SUM(by_age.`5_10`) AS `5_10`,
    SUM(by_age.`10_20`) AS `10_20`,
    SUM(by_age.`20_and_over`) AS `20_and_over`,
    SUM(by_age.total) AS total
  FROM by_age
)
SELECT
  final_rows.age_bracket,
  final_rows.under_1,
  final_rows.`1_3`,
  final_rows.`3_5`,
  final_rows.`5_10`,
  final_rows.`10_20`,
  final_rows.`20_and_over`,
  final_rows.total
FROM final_rows
ORDER BY final_rows.age_sort, final_rows.age_bracket

The 475 actual accessions in FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025) then land about 159 above that scaled plan, or +50.1%, compared with -119 (-20.0%) against the full plan of 594.
- Days in the quarter: October 1 to December 31, 2025 = 31 + 30 + 31 = 92
- Days hiring could not happen: October 1 to November 12 = 31 + 12 = 43
- Days hiring was possible: 92 - 43 = 49
- Scaled plan: 594 × 49 / 92 = 316.4
- Variance against the scaled plan: 475 - 316.4 = +158.6, or 158.6 / 316.4 = +50.1%

This comparison does not test the assumption. The 475 accessions are actuals, and they include hires effective during the period you name, so the shutdown premise is not checked by them. question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory

The OPM data shows 1,041 separations of TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, series 1802) in October and November 2025: 541 in October and 500 in November. Of those, 702 were quits (372 in October and 330 in November), about 67% of the total. Only 4 were flagged as 2025 deferred resignation program separations.

The 1,110 figure told to Congress is 69 higher than the OPM count. The records don't show what that figure covered, so I can't say why they differ. Quits and other separations for these months are unlikely to shift much, since the months are now well past and late reports are mostly in, but the count can still move slightly.

I read "screeners" as TSA series 1802 and "October and November" as separation effective months in 2025. If you meant all TSA occupations, I can run that version.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    CASE
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY' THEN 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT' THEN 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'RETIREMENT - OTHER' THEN 'RETIREMENT - OTHER'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TERMINATION (EXPIRED APPT/OTHER)' THEN 'TERMINATION (EXPIRED APPT/OTHER)'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TRANSFER OUT - INDIVIDUAL TRANSFER' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT - INDIVIDUAL TRANSFER'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TRANSFER OUT - MASS TRANSFER' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT - MASS TRANSFER'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE (RIF)' THEN 'REDUCTION IN FORCE (RIF)'
      ELSE 'OTHER SEPARATION'
    END AS separation_category_group,
    separation.drp_indicator
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1802'
    AND separation.effective_month IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
), detail AS (
  SELECT
    base.effective_month,
    base.separation_category_group AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    1 AS sort_order
  FROM base
  GROUP BY base.effective_month, base.separation_category_group
), total_two_months AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'TOTAL (TWO MONTHS)' AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    2 AS sort_order
  FROM base
), drp_two_months AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'DRP-FLAGGED (TWO MONTHS)' AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    3 AS sort_order
  FROM base
  WHERE base.drp_indicator = 'Y'
)
SELECT effective_month, separation_category, separations
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM detail
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM total_two_months
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM drp_two_months
) combined
ORDER BY sort_order, effective_month, separation_category
```

      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'RETIREMENT - OTHER' THEN 'RETIREMENT - OTHER'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TERMINATION (EXPIRED APPT/OTHER)' THEN 'TERMINATION (EXPIRED APPT/OTHER)'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TRANSFER OUT - INDIVIDUAL TRANSFER' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT - INDIVIDUAL TRANSFER'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TRANSFER OUT - MASS TRANSFER' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT - MASS TRANSFER'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE (RIF)' THEN 'REDUCTION IN FORCE (RIF)'
      ELSE 'OTHER SEPARATION'
    END AS separation_category_group,
    separation.drp_indicator
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1802'
    AND separation.effective_month IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
), detail AS (
  SELECT
    base.effective_month,
    base.separation_category_group AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    1 AS sort_order
  FROM base
  GROUP BY base.effective_month, base.separation_category_group
), total_two_months AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'TOTAL (TWO MONTHS)' AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    2 AS sort_order
  FROM base
), drp_two_months AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'DRP-FLAGGED (TWO MONTHS)' AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    3 AS sort_order
  FROM base
  WHERE base.drp_indicator = 'Y'
)
SELECT effective_month, separation_category, separations
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM detail
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM total_two_months
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM drp_two_months
) combined
ORDER BY sort_order, effective_month, separation_category

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory

FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency, HSCB) recorded 94 accessions with effective dates from October 2025 through May 2026, against GAO's 134. The records carry only an effective month, so the count covers all of May 2026, not just the first half. Of the 94, 73 are excepted-service appointments effective in May 2026, which makes May a large month. Two rows have an estimated (imputed) location. Late reports keep arriving, so the May figure can still grow. The gap of 40 cannot be reconciled from these records, since GAO's definition is not in them.

I read "hired" as all accessions (new hires plus transfers in and SES appointments) for FEMA, October 2025 through May 2026. If you meant new hires only, the count is 87 (94 less 5 SES appointments and 2 transfers in).

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT
    accession.effective_month,
    accession.accession_category,
    accession.location_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.accession
  WHERE accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSCB'
    AND accession.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND accession.effective_month >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND accession.effective_month <= DATE '2026-05-15'
)
SELECT
  'total' AS row_type,
  CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS accession_category,
  CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS location_imputed,
  COUNT(*) AS accession_count
FROM filtered
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'breakdown' AS row_type,
  filtered.effective_month,
  filtered.accession_category,
  filtered.location_imputed,
  COUNT(*) AS accession_count
FROM filtered
WHERE filtered.accession_category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  filtered.effective_month,
  filtered.accession_category,
  filtered.location_imputed
ORDER BY
  row_type,
  effective_month,
  accession_category,
  location_imputed
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, 1802) average $74,762 in annualized adjusted basic pay across 42,225 employees, and CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) average $104,656 across 27,650. That makes the CBP Officer average about $29,893 higher, roughly 40% above the TSA screener average.

Pay is estimated for every row in both groups: OPM redacted it, so the figures were filled in from job postings, not published by OPM. Because no row carries published pay, there is no actual-pay subset to compare against. I read "average salary" as the mean annualized adjusted basic pay for each occupation in the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant a median, or a different month, say so.

The query that ran:

```sql
SELECT
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_annual_basic_pay`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount_used`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `pay_imputed_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND `annualized_adjusted_basic_pay` IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802')
    OR (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895')
  )
GROUP BY
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`
ORDER BY `agency_subelement_code`, `occupational_series_code`
```

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

In the December 2025 snapshot (end of FY2026 Q1, October to December 2025), the cities with the most CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) are Washington, District of Columbia (1,907), Sterling, Virginia (735), Ashburn, Virginia (596), El Paso, Texas (521), and Detroit, Michigan (466). The top 15 cities together hold 7,446 of the 26,651 officers in the snapshot.

Every city shown is estimated, not published by OPM: the locations were drawn from USAJOBS postings, which show where DHS hires rather than where officers sit. Treat the ranking as a rough distribution. I have not run the masking test that checks how well this method recovers true locations; the review's standard check can supply it if you need it for the brief.

I read "cities" as duty station cities for all CBP Officers at the end of FY2026 Q1; if you meant the August 2026 snapshot, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered_snapshot` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    `location_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2025-12-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
),
`city_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `imputed_location_rows`
  FROM `filtered_snapshot`
  WHERE `duty_station_city` IS NOT NULL
    AND `duty_station_state` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`
),
`total_snapshot` AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS `total_headcount_snapshot`
  FROM `filtered_snapshot`
)
SELECT
  `city_counts`.`duty_station_city`,
  `city_counts`.`duty_station_state`,
  `city_counts`.`headcount`,
  `city_counts`.`imputed_location_rows`,
  `total_snapshot`.`total_headcount_snapshot`
FROM `city_counts`
CROSS JOIN `total_snapshot`
ORDER BY `headcount` DESC, `duty_station_state` ASC, `duty_station_city` ASC
LIMIT 15
```

question_text: Add up the first three quarters of FY2026: how far behind plan is each component on hiring?
answer_text:
Verified
Across FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (October 2025 to June 2026), DHS as a whole landed 17,370 accessions against 15,064 planned hires, 2,306 (15.3%) ahead of plan. Eight of the twelve components are still behind plan, and FEMA and TSA account for most of the shortfall.

| Component | Planned hires | Accessions | Variance | Variance % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FEMA (HSCB) | 2,043 | 147 | −1,896 | −92.8% |
| TSA (HSBC) | 2,368 | 1,336 | −1,032 | −43.6% |
| Coast Guard (HSAC) | 567 | 198 | −369 | −65.1% |
| CISA (HSCA) | 303 | 18 | −285 | −94.1% |
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 441 | 228 | −213 | −48.3% |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 1,203 | 1,053 | −150 | −12.5% |
| OIG (HSAE) | 36 | 5 | −31 | −86.1% |
| S&T (HSFA) | 18 | 1 | −17 | −94.4% |
| ICE (HSBB) | 3,186 | 7,573 | +4,387 | +137.7% |
| CBP (HSBD) | 4,182 | 5,734 | +1,552 | +37.1% |
| Secret Service (HSAD) | 627 | 884 | +257 | +41.0% |
| FLETC (HSBE) | 90 | 193 | +103 | +114.4% |

ICE's surplus rests on one quarter. It logged 6,185 accessions in FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025) against 1,062 planned, a variance of +5,123. Its Q2 and Q3 variances were −39 and −697, so the October to December figure is worth checking before the review. Late OPM files keep adding accessions, so the shortfalls may narrow.

I read "how far behind" as accessions minus planned hires, summed over FY2026 Q1 to Q3 for all occupations in each component. If you meant a single quarter or a per-occupation view, say so.
