question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. Across CBP Officer postings opened September 2025 to October 2026, higher-grade postings generally had shorter announced windows, not longer. Postings with a minimum grade of 13 averaged 7.4 days open (median 6, 211 postings), and grade 14 averaged 5.8 days (median 6, 126 postings). The longest windows were at lower grades: minimum grade 5 averaged 29.3 days (median 30, 14 postings) and minimum grade 9 averaged 22.4 days (median 28, 22 postings), though those groups are small.

This measures the window between each posting's open and close dates, not how long a posting actually stayed open before it was filled or cancelled, so it is an announced-window measure. I read "higher grade" as the minimum grade on the posting and "stay open" as the announced open-to-close days, across all CBP Officer postings opened in that period. Grouping by maximum grade shows the same pattern. If you meant postings still open on a given date, or the actual time to fill, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered_postings` AS (
  SELECT
    `minimum_grade`,
    `maximum_grade`,
    DATEDIFF(`close_date`, `open_date`) AS `days_open`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `open_date` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `open_date` <= DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `close_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND ARRAY_CONTAINS(`occupational_series_codes`, '1895')
), `by_min_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    'minimum_grade' AS `grade_group_type`,
    `minimum_grade` AS `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `posting_count`,
    AVG(`days_open`) AS `avg_days_open`,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY `days_open`) AS `median_days_open`,
    CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS `location_imputed`,
    CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS `pay_imputed`
  FROM `filtered_postings`
  WHERE `minimum_grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `minimum_grade`
), `by_max_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    'maximum_grade' AS `grade_group_type`,
    `maximum_grade` AS `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `posting_count`,
    AVG(`days_open`) AS `avg_days_open`,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY `days_open`) AS `median_days_open`,
    CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS `location_imputed`,
    CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS `pay_imputed`
  FROM `filtered_postings`
  WHERE `maximum_grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `maximum_grade`
)
SELECT *
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM `by_min_grade`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM `by_max_grade`
) `u`
ORDER BY `grade_group_type`, CAST(`grade` AS INT) ASC, `grade` ASC;
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) had 586 retirements from September 2025 through August 2026. The peak was December 2025 with 152, about a quarter of the year's total, and the lowest month was November 2025 with 24.

| Effective month | Retirements |
|---|---|
| Sep 2025 | 54 |
| Oct 2025 | 36 |
| Nov 2025 | 24 |
| Dec 2025 | 152 |
| Jan 2026 | 44 |
| Feb 2026 | 26 |
| Mar 2026 | 31 |
| Apr 2026 | 45 |
| May 2026 | 52 |
| Jun 2026 | 46 |
| Jul 2026 | 45 |
| Aug 2026 | 31 |

The counts do not depend on location or pay, but the rows behind them carry estimated (imputed) location and pay fields in every month, so any location or pay breakdown of these people would be estimated. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months (July and August 2026) will grow. The retirement count includes all three retirement categories (voluntary, early out, other). I read "retire" as those three categories counted by effective month over the trailing twelve months; if you meant the retirement rate, or a single retirement type, say so.

```sql
WITH month_spine AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS effective_month
),
filtered AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    separation.location_imputed,
    separation.pay_imputed
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation` AS separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.effective_month >= TO_DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND separation.effective_month <= TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND separation.separation_category IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'RETIREMENT - OTHER')
),
monthly AS (
  SELECT
    month_spine.effective_month,
    COUNT(filtered.effective_month) AS retirement_separations,
    COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN filtered.location_imputed = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) = 1 AS any_location_imputed,
    COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN filtered.pay_imputed = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) = 1 AS any_pay_imputed
  FROM month_spine
  LEFT JOIN filtered
    ON month_spine.effective_month = filtered.effective_month
  GROUP BY month_spine.effective_month
),
summary AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(monthly.retirement_separations) AS total_retirement_separations,
    MAX(CASE WHEN monthly.any_location_imputed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS any_location_imputed_any_month,
    MAX(CASE WHEN monthly.any_pay_imputed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS any_pay_imputed_any_month
  FROM monthly
)
SELECT
  monthly.effective_month,
  monthly.retirement_separations,
  summary.total_retirement_separations,
  monthly.any_location_imputed,
  monthly.any_pay_imputed,
  summary.any_location_imputed_any_month,
  summary.any_pay_imputed_any_month
FROM monthly
CROSS JOIN summary
ORDER BY monthly.effective_month
```

question_text: Which DHS components lost the most senior executives this year?
answer_text:
Exploratory

DHS Headquarters lost the most senior executives (Senior Executive Service, pay plan ES) over the twelve months September 2025 to August 2026, with 57 separations, followed by FEMA (44) and ICE (37). Across DHS there were 273 senior executive separations in that window, and 62 came through the 2025 deferred resignation program (DRP), which is concentrated at FEMA (23 of 44) and DHS Headquarters (15 of 57). Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly.

| Component | Senior executive separations | Of which DRP |
|---|---|---|
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 57 | 15 |
| FEMA (HSCB) | 44 | 23 |
| ICE (HSBB) | 37 | 0 |
| CBP (HSBD) | 31 | 0 |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 30 | 9 |
| CISA (HSCA) | 27 | 7 |
| Secret Service (HSAD) | 23 | 0 |
| Science and Technology Directorate (HSFA) | 8 | 5 |
| Coast Guard (HSAC) | 7 | 1 |
| FLETC (HSBE) | 4 | 0 |
| Domestic Nuclear Detection Office (HSDA) | 3 | 1 |
| Office of the Inspector General (HSAE) | 2 | 1 |
| TSA (HSBC) | 0 | 0 |

These are counts, not rates; the senior executive headcounts by component were not pulled, so a rate ranking could differ. A first pass returned zeros everywhere because of a component-name matching problem, so the table uses the second pass, whose rows sum to the 273 total. I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026 and "senior executives" as pay plan ES; if you meant calendar 2026 or separation rates, say so.

```sql
SELECT *
FROM (
  SELECT
    'pay_plan' AS section,
    separation.pay_plan_code,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS agency_subelement_code,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.pay_plan_code = 'ES' AND separation.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS drp_yes_count
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
  GROUP BY separation.pay_plan_code

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'es_by_component' AS section,
    separation.pay_plan_code,
    separation.agency_subelement_code,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS drp_yes_count
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND separation.pay_plan_code = 'ES'
  GROUP BY separation.pay_plan_code, separation.agency_subelement_code

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'es_by_grade' AS section,
    separation.pay_plan_code,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS agency_subelement_code,
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No, not in a straight line. Across the trailing twelve months to August 2026, CBP Officers in the middle grades (12 and 13, most of the cell) separated at about 3.2%, and the lowest grades left fastest. Grade 15 (6.6%) is above the cell's overall 3.5%, but it is small, with 12 separations. Grade 14 (3.8%) is close to the overall rate.

| Grade | Separations | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| 00 (36 at start, 28 at end) | 7 | 21.9% |
| 05 | 67 | 10.2% |
| 07 | 81 | 7.7% |
| 09 | 61 | 3.9% |
| 11 | 8 | 0.7% |
| 12 | 550 | 3.2% |
| 13 | 136 | 3.2% |
| 14 | 32 | 3.8% |
| 15 | 12 | 6.6% |
| All grades | 954 | 3.5% |

The rate for each grade is its separations divided by the average of its headcount in September 2025 and August 2026. The query returned the same figures with and without the 2025 deferred resignation program in every grade, so it found no program separations in this cell. Confirm that before you quote the rates. Late reports keep arriving, so recent counts will grow.

I read "higher-graded" as the grade field for each grade on record, with the rate over the trailing twelve months to August 2026. If you meant a grade band (for example, GS-14 and above) or the count of separations, say so.

```sql
WITH `start_headcount` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_start`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`end_headcount` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_end`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`separations` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(`drp_indicator`, 'N') <> 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`grades` AS (
  SELECT `grade` FROM `start_headcount`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `end_headcount`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `separations`
),
`by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `g`.`grade` AS `grade`,
    COALESCE(`sh`.`headcount_start`, 0) AS `headcount_start`,
    COALESCE(`eh`.`headcount_end`, 0) AS `headcount_end`,
    COALESCE(`s`.`separations`, 0) AS `separations`,
    COALESCE(`s`.`separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program`, 0) AS `separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program`
  FROM `grades` `g`
  LEFT JOIN `start_headcount` `sh`
    ON `g`.`grade` = `sh`.`grade`
  LEFT JOIN `end_headcount` `eh`
    ON `g`.`grade` = `eh`.`grade`
  LEFT JOIN `separations` `s`
    ON `g`.`grade` = `s`.`grade`
)
SELECT
  `grade`,
  `headcount_start`,
  `headcount_end`,
  `separations`,
  CASE
    WHEN (`headcount_start` + `headcount_end`) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(`separations`,(try_divide((`headcount_start` + `headcount_end`),2.0)))
  END AS `rate`,
  `separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program`,
  CASE
    WHEN (`headcount_start` + `headcount_end`) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(`separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program`,(try_divide((`headcount_start` + `headcount_end`),2.0)))
  END AS `rate_excluding_deferred_resignation_program`
FROM (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    `headcount_start`,
    `headcount_end`,
    `separations`,
    `separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program`
  FROM `by_grade`

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'ALL' AS `grade`,
    SUM(`headcount_start`) AS `headcount_start`,
    SUM(`headcount_end`) AS `headcount_end`,
    SUM(`separations`) AS `separations`,
    SUM(`separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program`) AS `separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program`
  FROM `by_grade`
) `final`
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `grade` = 'ALL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, `grade`
```

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, about 5,463 of the 27,299 CBP Officers (20%) already meet a retirement-eligibility proxy of age 50 with 20 years of service. By August 2031 that rises to between 7,708 and 11,053 (28% to 40%). These are eligibility counts, not forecasts of who will retire. Late reports keep arriving, so the August 2026 counts can shift slightly.

| Group (August 2026 headcount) | Officers |
|---|---|
| Eligible now: ages 50-54, 55-59, 60-64 with 20+ years | 5,463 |
| Become eligible by 2031 (certain): ages 45-49 with 20+ years | 2,245 |
| May become eligible by 2031: ages 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64 with 10-20 years | 0 to 3,345 |

The 10-20 year band cannot be split at the 15-year point, so the upper figure assumes every officer in that band reaches 20 years by 2031. The age 50 and 20-year threshold is my assumption, not a figure from the data; confirm the CBP retirement rule before quoting it. I summed the cross-tab rows to get the 27,299 total, and no officers appear in the 65 or more bracket.

I read this as retirement eligibility for CBP Officers at the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant actual retirement separations over the past year, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS ( SELECT `age_bracket`, CASE WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20 and over' END AS `service_bucket` FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot` WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01' AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895' AND `age_bracket` IN ('20-24', '25-29', '30-34', '35-39', '40-44', '45-49', '50-54', '55-59', '60-64', '65 or more') AND `age_bracket` IS NOT NULL AND `length_of_service_years` IS NOT NULL ) SELECT `age_bracket`, `service_bucket`, COUNT(*) AS `headcount`, COUNT(*) AS `total_headcount` FROM `filtered` WHERE `service_bucket` IS NOT NULL GROUP BY `age_bracket`, `service_bucket` ORDER BY CASE `age_bracket` WHEN '20-24' THEN 1 WHEN '25-29' THEN 2 WHEN '30-34' THEN 3 WHEN '35-39' THEN 4 WHEN '40-44' THEN 5 WHEN '45-49' THEN 6 WHEN '50-54' THEN 7 WHEN '55-59' THEN 8 WHEN '60-64' THEN 9 WHEN '65 or more' THEN 10 ELSE 99 END, CASE `service_bucket` WHEN 'under 1' THEN 1 WHEN '1-3' THEN 2 WHEN '3-5' THEN 3 WHEN '5-10' THEN 4 WHEN '10-20' THEN 5 WHEN '20 and over' THEN 6 ELSE 99 END
```

- Scaled plan: 594 × 49 / 92 = 316.4 hires
- Variance against the scaled plan: 475 - 316.4 = +158.6, or 158.6 / 316.4 = +50.1%

Later OPM files can add accessions, so the actual figure will rise. Accessions by month for October to December 2025 are the better test of the assumption; a one-off query can pull them. question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory

TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration (TSA), series 1802) had 1,041 separations effective October and November 2025 in the OPM data, of which 702 were quits (67%). October had 541 separations, 372 of them quits; November had 500, 330 of them quits. That is 69 fewer than the 1,110 TSA reported, and the records do not show why the two figures differ. Later OPM files can add separations, so these counts may rise slightly. Only 4 of the 1,041 carry the deferred resignation program flag, all in October. The separation categories show how people left, not why.

I read "left during the shutdown" as separations effective October and November 2025 for TSA screeners; if you meant all TSA occupations or a different window, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    CASE
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      WHEN separation.separation_category ILIKE '%RETIREMENT%' THEN 'RETIREMENT'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TERMINATION' THEN 'TERMINATION'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 'REDUCTION IN FORCE'
      ELSE 'OTHER SEPARATION'
    END AS separation_bucket,
    separation.drp_indicator
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1802'
    AND separation.effective_month IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
    AND separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.separation_category IS NOT NULL
),
monthly AS (
  SELECT
    base.effective_month,
    base.separation_bucket,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS drp_flagged_separations
  FROM base
  GROUP BY base.effective_month, base.separation_bucket
),
totals AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_separations_two_months,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.separation_bucket = 'QUIT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_quit_separations_two_months,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_drp_flagged_two_months
  FROM base
)
SELECT
  monthly.effective_month,
  monthly.separation_bucket,
  monthly.separations,
  monthly.drp_flagged_separations,
  totals.total_separations_two_months,
  totals.total_quit_separations_two_months,
  totals.total_drp_flagged_two_months
FROM monthly
CROSS JOIN totals
ORDER BY
  monthly.effective_month,
  CASE monthly.separation_bucket
    WHEN 'QUIT' THEN 1
    WHEN 'RETIREMENT' THEN 2
    WHEN 'TERMINATION' THEN 3
    WHEN 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 4
    WHEN 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 5
    WHEN 'OTHER SEPARATION' THEN 6
    ELSE 7
  END
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory
OPM records show 94 accession actions for FEMA (HSCB) across all occupational series, effective October 2025 through May 2026. That is 40 fewer than GAO's 134, or 70% of GAO's figure. OPM holds only monthly effective dates, so the count covers all of May 2026 (76 of the 94) and cannot be cut at mid-May. Through April the count is 18, so the OPM figure through mid-May falls between 18 and 94. Late reports keep arriving, so the count will grow.

By effective month: 2025-10: 1; 2025-11: 8; 2025-12: 1; 2026-01: 5; 2026-02: 0; 2026-03: 2; 2026-04: 1; 2026-05: 76. These sum to 94.

I read "hired" as all accession actions (new hires, transfers in, and SES appointments) for FEMA in every series, counted by effective month. If GAO counted only new hires, or a different window, say so and I can rerun that category.

```sql
WITH filtered_accessions AS (
  SELECT
    accession.effective_month
  FROM workforce.semantic.accession
  WHERE accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSCB'
    AND accession.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND accession.effective_month >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND accession.effective_month <= DATE '2026-05-15'
), monthly_counts AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_FORMAT(accession.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM') AS effective_month_yyyy_mm,
    COUNT(*) AS accession_actions
  FROM filtered_accessions AS accession
  GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(accession.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM')
), total_count AS (
  SELECT
    'TOTAL' AS effective_month_yyyy_mm,
    COUNT(*) AS accession_actions
  FROM filtered_accessions
)
SELECT
  'total' AS row_type,
  total_count.effective_month_yyyy_mm,
  total_count.accession_actions
FROM total_count
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'month' AS row_type,
  monthly_counts.effective_month_yyyy_mm,
  monthly_counts.accession_actions
FROM monthly_counts
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN row_type = 'total' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
  effective_month_yyyy_mm
```

question_text: Month by month, how many CBP Officers did we hire from September 2025 to August 2026?
answer_text:
Exploratory
CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, HSBD, series 1895) had 2,456 accessions from September 2025 to August 2026, by effective month: 224, 80, 236, 159, 232, 166, 243, 159, 319, 160, 242 and 236 (September through August). The low was 80 in October 2025 and the high was 319 in May 2026. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months (June to August 2026) will grow. I read "hired" as accession actions counted by effective month, all accession categories included; if you meant new hires only, or the plan's quarterly view, say so.

```sql
WITH `months` AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS `effective_month`
),
`counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= TO_DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
),
`monthly` AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_FORMAT(`months`.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `month`,
    COALESCE(`counts`.`accession_count`, 0) AS `accession_count`,
    `months`.`effective_month` AS `sort_month`
  FROM `months`
  LEFT JOIN `counts`
    ON `months`.`effective_month` = `counts`.`effective_month`
)
SELECT `month`, `accession_count`
FROM (
  SELECT `month`, `accession_count`, `sort_month`, 0 AS `sort_order`
  FROM `monthly`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'TOTAL' AS `month`, SUM(`accession_count`) AS `accession_count`, CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS `sort_month`, 1 AS `sort_order`
  FROM `monthly`
) `final`
ORDER BY `sort_order`, `sort_month`
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory
TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, 1802) averaged $74,762.38 in annual basic pay on the August 2026 snapshot across 46,913 staff, against $104,655.83 for CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) across 27,650 staff. That is $29,893.45 more per year for CBP Officers, about 40% above TSA screeners.
Pay is estimated: OPM redacted it, so the figures were filled in from job postings. 42,225 of the 46,913 TSA screener rows (90%) and all 27,650 CBP Officer rows are estimated, so treat both averages as estimates.
I read "salary" as average annual basic pay on the August 2026 snapshot, the latest; if you meant a different month or a measure such as median pay, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_annual_basic_pay`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `imputed_pay_row_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND `occupational_series_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND ((`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802')
    OR (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'))
GROUP BY
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`
ORDER BY `agency_subelement_code`, `occupational_series_code`
```

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory
Washington, District of Columbia has the most CBP Officers at 1,920 in the August 2026 snapshot, followed by Sterling, Virginia (751) and Ashburn, Virginia (678). The top 25 cities hold 10,220 of the 27,650 CBP Officers (about 37%). All of these locations are estimated: OPM redacted them, so each city was filled in from job postings, which show where DHS hires rather than where officers sit. The review's masking test covers FEMA and CISA, not CBP. For those two, the drawn state matched the true state 11.7% of the time (FEMA) and 28.2% (CISA), and the method flatters CBP because its staff spread across many more ports and airports. Treat the city ranking as a distribution estimate, not a count of where officers are posted.

I read "most" as headcount by duty station city in the August 2026 snapshot, the latest; if you meant the FY2026 Q1 snapshot or separations by city, say so.

```sql
WITH `base` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    `location_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
),
`city_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `location_imputed_rows`
  FROM `base`
  WHERE `duty_station_city` IS NOT NULL
    AND `duty_station_state` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `duty_station_city`, `duty_station_state`
),
`top_25` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    `headcount`,
    `location_imputed_rows`,
    0 AS `sort_bucket`
  FROM `city_counts`
  ORDER BY `headcount` DESC, `duty_station_city` ASC, `duty_station_state` ASC
  LIMIT 25
),
`total_row` AS (
  SELECT
    'ALL' AS `duty_station_city`,
    'ALL' AS `duty_station_state`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `location_imputed_rows`,
    1 AS `sort_bucket`
  FROM `base`
)
SELECT
  `duty_station_city`,
  `duty_station_state`,
  `headcount`,
  `location_imputed_rows`
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM `top_25`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM `total_row`
) `combined`
ORDER BY `sort_bucket` ASC, `headcount` DESC, `duty_station_city` ASC, `duty_station_state` ASC
```

question_text: Add up the first three quarters of FY2026: how far behind plan is each component on hiring?
answer_text:
Verified

Across all of DHS, FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (October 2025 to June 2026) landed 17,370 accessions against 15,064 planned hires, a variance of +2,306 (+15.3%). The gap is uneven: FEMA, TSA, and the Coast Guard fell furthest short, while ICE and CBP ran well ahead.

| Component | Planned hires | Actual accessions | Variance (hires) | Variance, % of plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FEMA (HSCB) | 2,043 | 147 | -1,896 | -92.8% |
| TSA (HSBC) | 2,368 | 1,336 | -1,032 | -43.6% |
| U.S. Coast Guard (HSAC) | 567 | 198 | -369 | -65.1% |
| CISA (HSCA) | 303 | 18 | -285 | -94.1% |
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 441 | 228 | -213 | -48.3% |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 1,203 | 1,053 | -150 | -12.5% |
| OIG (HSAE) | 36 | 5 | -31 | -86.1% |
| S&T (HSFA) | 18 | 1 | -17 | -94.4% |
| FLETC (HSBE) | 90 | 193 | +103 | +114.4% |
| Secret Service (HSAD) | 627 | 884 | +257 | +41.0% |
| CBP (HSBD) | 4,182 | 5,734 | +1,552 | +37.1% |
| ICE (HSBB) | 3,186 | 7,573 | +4,387 | +137.7% |

Two cells were not returned for one quarter each (CISA for October to December 2025... no: CISA for January to March 2026, and S&T for October to December 2025). Their missing actuals are the all-DHS quarterly totals minus the other ten components, so those two figures are derived, not read directly. ICE's October to December 2025 accessions (6,185) are far above its later quarters (1,023 and 365) and drive most of its surplus. Late OPM reports keep adding accessions, so every shortfall will narrow. I read "behind plan" as accessions minus planned hires summed over the three quarters and all occupations in each component; if you want one quarter or the percentage alone, say so.

question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory

889 USAJOBS announcements listed Border Patrol Agent series 1896 among their series, across all DHS components, with an open date from September 1, 2025 to October 31, 2026. Each announcement is counted once, including those that list several series. This counts postings, not hires or openings, and the figure is a one-off count rather than one of the review's standard calculations.

I read this as announcements opened in that window, counted by open date, across all components; if you meant postings open on a single date, or a count by component, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered_postings AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `control_number`,
    `announcement_number`,
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    `agency_subelement`,
    `open_date`,
    `close_date`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-01' AND DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1896')
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS `distinct_posting_count`,
  `control_number`,
  `announcement_number`,
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `open_date`,
  `close_date`
FROM filtered_postings
ORDER BY `open_date`, `control_number`, `announcement_number`
```

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. Across the 469 CBP Officer postings opened from September 2025 to October 2026, the higher-grade postings had shorter announced windows, not longer. Grades 7 and 9 (27 postings) had a median of 30 days, while grades 12 to 15 (235 postings) had a median of 6 days. Grade 13, the largest group with 210 postings, averaged 7.3 days. Grade 00 (6 postings) averaged 13.3 days.

Duration here is the announced window (close date minus open date), not how long a posting stayed open in practice or how long it took to fill. I read "stay open longer" as that announced window by maximum grade; if you meant time to actual closure, or the number of postings open on a given date, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `maximum_grade` AS `grade`,
  COUNT(*) AS `posting_count`,
  AVG(DATEDIFF(`close_date`, `open_date`)) AS `avg_duration_days`,
  PERCENTILE_APPROX(DATEDIFF(`close_date`, `open_date`), 0.5) AS `median_duration_days`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
  AND `maximum_grade` IS NOT NULL
  AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
  AND `close_date` IS NOT NULL
  AND `open_date` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
  AND `open_date` <= DATE '2026-10-31'
  AND ARRAY_CONTAINS(`occupational_series_codes`, '1895')
GROUP BY `maximum_grade`
ORDER BY `maximum_grade` ASC
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (CBP, 1895) had 586 retirements in the twelve effective months September 2025 to August 2026. December 2025 was the peak at 152, about a quarter of the year's total, and the lowest month was November 2025 at 24. Late reports keep arriving, so the recent months, especially August 2026, will grow slightly. The one-off query does not separate out deferred resignation program separations, so I cannot say how much of the December peak came from that wave.

| Month | Retirements |
|---|---|
| 2025-09 | 54 |
| 2025-10 | 36 |
| 2025-11 | 24 |
| 2025-12 | 152 |
| 2026-01 | 44 |
| 2026-02 | 26 |
| 2026-03 | 31 |
| 2026-04 | 45 |
| 2026-05 | 52 |
| 2026-06 | 46 |
| 2026-07 | 45 |
| 2026-08 | 31 |

I read this as all three retirement categories (voluntary, early out, other) for CBP Officers by effective month over September 2025 to August 2026; if you meant the trailing twelve-month retirement rate or only the open quarter, say so.

```sql
WITH months AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS effective_month
), retirements AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS retirement_count
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.separation_category IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'RETIREMENT - OTHER')
    AND separation.effective_month BETWEEN TO_DATE('2025-09-01') AND TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
  GROUP BY separation.effective_month
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    months.effective_month,
    DATE_FORMAT(months.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM') AS effective_month_label,
    COALESCE(retirements.retirement_count, 0) AS retirement_count
  FROM months
  LEFT JOIN retirements
    ON months.effective_month = retirements.effective_month
)
SELECT
  monthly.effective_month_label AS effective_month,
  monthly.retirement_count,
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

Higher-graded CBP Officers (grades 13 to 15) did not leave at a clearly higher rate over the trailing twelve months to August 2026: combined they separated at 3.4% (180 separations on a mean headcount of 5,344), against 3.5% for grades 5 to 12 (767 on 21,771). The highest rates sit at the lower grades, 5 (10.2%) and 7 (7.7%), and grade 15 reads 6.6% on only 12 separations. Across all grades the rate is 3.5% (954 separations on a mean headcount of 27,147). No separations in this window are flagged as 2025 deferred resignation program, so the rate is the same with or without that wave. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly, and the grade 0 and grade 15 cells are too small for firm conclusions.

I read "higher-graded" as grades 13 to 15 against grades 5 to 12 (grade 0 is in neither group), over the trailing twelve months to August 2026; if you meant a different grade cut or a count of separations, say so.

```sql
WITH `sep_by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separations_all`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS `separations_excluding_drp`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`start_hc_by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `start_headcount`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`end_hc_by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `end_headcount`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`grades` AS (
  SELECT `grade` FROM `sep_by_grade`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `start_hc_by_grade`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `end_hc_by_grade`
),
`detail` AS (
  SELECT
    `g`.`grade` AS `grade`,
    COALESCE(`s`.`separations_all`, 0) AS `separations_all`,
    COALESCE(`s`.`separations_excluding_drp`, 0) AS `separations_excluding_drp`,
    COALESCE(`sh`.`start_headcount`, 0) AS `start_headcount`,
    COALESCE(`eh`.`end_headcount`, 0) AS `end_headcount`,
    try_divide((COALESCE(`sh`.`start_headcount`, 0) + COALESCE(`eh`.`end_headcount`, 0)),2.0) AS `mean_headcount`
  FROM `grades` `g`
  LEFT JOIN `sep_by_grade` `s`
    ON `g`.`grade` = `s`.`grade`
  LEFT JOIN `start_hc_by_grade` `sh`
    ON `g`.`grade` = `sh`.`grade`
  LEFT JOIN `end_hc_by_grade` `eh`
    ON `g`.`grade` = `eh`.`grade`
)
SELECT
  `grade`,
  `separations_all`,
  `separations_excluding_drp`,
  `start_headcount`,
  `end_headcount`,
  `mean_headcount`,
  CASE WHEN `mean_headcount` = 0 THEN NULL ELSE try_divide(`separations_all`,`mean_headcount`) END AS `rate_all`,
  CASE WHEN `mean_headcount` = 0 THEN NULL ELSE try_divide(`separations_excluding_drp`,`mean_headcount`) END AS `rate_excluding_drp`
FROM (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    `separations_all`,
    `separations_excluding_drp`,
    `start_headcount`,
    `end_headcount`,
    `mean_headcount`,
    0 AS `sort_key`
  FROM `detail`

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'TOTAL' AS `grade`,
    SUM(`separations_all`) AS `separations_all`,
    SUM(`separations_excluding_drp`) AS `separations_excluding_drp`,
    SUM(`start_headcount`) AS `start_headcount`,
    SUM(`end_headcount`) AS `end_headcount`,
    try_divide((SUM(`start_headcount`) + SUM(`end_headcount`)),2.0) AS `mean_headcount`,
    1 AS `sort_key`
  FROM `detail`
) `x`
ORDER BY `sort_key`, `grade`
```

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

Of the 27,299 CBP Officers on the August 2026 snapshot, 7,034 are aged 50 to 64, and 5,463 of them have 20 or more years of service. Those aged 50 to 64 are the people who reach age 55 or older within five years. The breakdown is 2,483 aged 50-54, 2,130 aged 55-59, and 850 aged 60-64, each with 20 or more years of service. The records hold no retirement eligibility rules or retirement intent, so these are the exposure pool, not a forecast. The query returned no one aged 65 or more. Its summary text gave 24,146 employees, but its rows sum to 27,299, so I used the rows.

I read "could retire" as employees whose age and service put them in the retirement-age pool within five years, on the August 2026 snapshot. If you meant recorded retirements (the three retirement categories) over the past year, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bracket`,
    CASE
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20 and over'
    END AS `length_of_service_bucket`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `age_bracket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `length_of_service_years` IS NOT NULL
    AND `age_bracket` IN (
      '20-24','25-29','30-34','35-39','40-44','45-49','50-54','55-59','60-64','65 or more'
    )
), cells AS (
  SELECT
    'CELL' AS `section`,
    `age_bracket`,
    `length_of_service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`
  FROM base
  WHERE `length_of_service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `age_bracket`, `length_of_service_bucket`
), age_totals AS (
  SELECT
    'AGE_TOTAL' AS `section`,
    `age_bracket`,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `length_of_service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`
  FROM base
  WHERE `length_of_service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `age_bracket`
), los_totals AS (
  SELECT
    'LOS_TOTAL' AS `section`,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `age_bracket`,
    `length_of_service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`
  FROM base
  WHERE `length_of_service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `length_of_service_bucket`
)
SELECT
  `section`,
  `age_bracket`,
  `length_of_service_bucket`,
  `headcount`
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM cells
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM age_totals
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM los_totals
) u
ORDER BY
  CASE `section`
    WHEN 'CELL' THEN 1
    WHEN 'AGE_TOTAL' THEN 2
    WHEN 'LOS_TOTAL' THEN 3
    ELSE 4
  END,
  CASE `age_bracket`
    WHEN '20-24' THEN 1
    WHEN '25-29' THEN 2
    WHEN '30-34' THEN 3
    WHEN '35-39' THEN 4
    WHEN '40-44' THEN 5
    WHEN '45-49' THEN 6
    WHEN '50-54' THEN 7
    WHEN '55-59' THEN 8
    WHEN '60-64' THEN 9
    WHEN '65 or more' THEN 10
    ELSE 11
  END,
  CASE `length_of_service_bucket`
    WHEN 'under 1' THEN 1
    WHEN '1-3' THEN 2
    WHEN '3-5' THEN 3
    WHEN '5-10' THEN 4
    WHEN '10-20' THEN 5
    WHEN '20 and over' THEN 6
    ELSE 7
  END
```

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory
The OPM data shows 1,041 separations of TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, series 1802) in October and November 2025 combined, not 1,110. Of those, 702 were quits and 339 were other categories.

The 1,041 is 69 fewer than TSA's figure. Both months are well past, so late reports should add little, though about 0.8% of records are later restated. The 2025 deferred resignation program accounts for only 2 separations in each group. I read "screeners" as the 1802 series in TSA and "left" as all separation categories; if you meant all TSA occupations, or only the 1,110 you were given, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `category_group`,
  SUM(`separation_count`) OVER () AS `total_separations_two_months_combined`,
  `separation_count`,
  `drp_separation_count`
FROM (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      ELSE 'ALL OTHER CATEGORIES'
    END AS `category_group`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `drp_separation_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802'
  GROUP BY
    CASE
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      ELSE 'ALL OTHER CATEGORIES'
    END
) t
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `category_group` = 'QUIT' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory

OPM records show 94 FEMA (HSCB) accessions effective October 2025 through mid-May 2026, all occupations. That is 40 fewer than GAO's 134, so OPM counts about 70% of GAO's figure (94 ÷ 134 = 0.70). Accession records are dated by month, so the May figure covers all of May (76 accessions), not only the first half. Later OPM files can still add accessions for these months. Three of the 94 rows carry estimated locations; the count is unaffected.

By month: October 2025, 1; November, 8; December, 1; January 2026, 5; February, 0; March, 2; April, 1; May, 76. The total is 94.

I read this as all FEMA accessions effective October 2025 to May 2026, across all accession categories. If you meant new hires only, or a single occupational series, say so and I can split it by category.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    `location_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSCB'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-05-15'
),
`summary` AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS `total_count_in_window`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `location_imputed_count_in_window`,
    CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN true ELSE false END AS `any_location_imputed`
  FROM `filtered`
),
`monthly` AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_FORMAT(`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month_yyyy_mm`,
    COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`
  FROM `filtered`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS `row_type`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `effective_month`,
  CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS `accession_count`,
  `total_count_in_window`,
  `any_location_imputed`,
  `location_imputed_count_in_window`
FROM `summary`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'MONTH' AS `row_type`,
  `effective_month_yyyy_mm` AS `effective_month`,
  `accession_count`,
  CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS `total_count_in_window`,
  CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS `any_location_imputed`,
  CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS `location_imputed_count_in_window`
FROM `monthly`
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `row_type` = 'TOTAL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, `effective_month`
```

answer_text:
Exploratory
CBP Officers (CBP, 1895) had 2,456 accessions from September 2025 to August 2026, ranging from 80 in October 2025 to 319 in May 2026.

| Month | Accessions |
|---|---|
| 2025-09 | 224 |

| 2025-11 | 236 |
| 2025-12 | 159 |
| 2026-01 | 232 |
| 2026-02 | 166 |
| 2026-03 | 243 |
| 2026-04 | 159 |
| 2026-05 | 319 |
| 2026-06 | 160 |
| 2026-07 | 242 |
| 2026-08 | 236 |

The monthly figures add to the 2,456 total. Late OPM reports keep arriving, so the most recent months (July and August 2026) will grow. I read "hired" as all accessions effective in each month, including transfers in; if you meant new hires only, say so and I will split them out.

```sql
WITH months AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS effective_month
), monthly_counts AS (
  SELECT
    accession.effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS accession_count
  FROM workforce.semantic.accession
  WHERE accession.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND accession.effective_month BETWEEN TO_DATE('2025-09-01') AND TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND accession.occupational_series_code = '1895'
  GROUP BY accession.effective_month
)
SELECT month, accession_count
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE_FORMAT(months.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
    COALESCE(monthly_counts.accession_count, 0) AS accession_count,
    months.effective_month AS sort_month,
    0 AS sort_group
  FROM months
  LEFT JOIN monthly_counts
    ON months.effective_month = monthly_counts.effective_month

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'TOTAL' AS month,
    SUM(COALESCE(monthly_counts.accession_count, 0)) AS accession_count,
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS sort_month,
    1 AS sort_group
  FROM months
  LEFT JOIN monthly_counts
    ON months.effective_month = monthly_counts.effective_month
) q
ORDER BY q.sort_group, q.sort_month
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory
Across the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, series 1802) averaged $74,762 in annual basic pay on 46,913 staff, about $29,893 (40.0%) below CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895), who averaged $104,656 on 27,650 staff.
Both averages are estimated: pay was imputed from job postings for 42,225 of the TSA rows (90%) and for all 27,650 CBP rows, so quote them as estimates rather than OPM-published pay. The figures are annual basic pay, not total earnings with overtime or locality.
I read "salary" as average annual basic pay for the August 2026 snapshot, the latest month, since no period was named; if you meant a different snapshot or total compensation, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code,
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series,
  COUNT(*) AS headcount,
  AVG(workforce_snapshot.annualized_adjusted_basic_pay) AS average_annual_basic_pay,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN true ELSE false END AS any_pay_imputed,
  SUM(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS imputed_row_count
FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND (
    (workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC' AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1802')
    OR (workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD' AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895')
  )
GROUP BY
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code,
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series
ORDER BY workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code, workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code
```

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory
CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) are most concentrated in Washington, District of Columbia (1,920), then Sterling, Virginia (751) and Ashburn, Virginia (678), across 189 duty-station cities and 27,650 officers in the August 2026 snapshot. The city figures are estimated: all 27,650 rows have an imputed location, filled from USAJOBS postings, so they show where CBP hiring is advertised rather than where officers sit. The masking test covered only FEMA and CISA (state match 0.12 and 0.28), and it flatters the method for CBP, whose staff spread across many ports. I read this as the August 2026 snapshot for all CBP Officers; if you meant FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025) or the state-level view, say so.

```sql
WITH city_counts AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `location_imputed_rows`

    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'

FROM city_counts
```

question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory
889 USAJOBS postings listed Border Patrol Agent (series 1896) among their series, across all of DHS, with an open date from September 1, 2025 to October 31, 2026. Counting each posting once, including postings that list several series, the monthly counts run from 43 (December 2025) to 92 (August 2026). I counted by open date and across all components, since the question named no component. If you meant postings that close in the window, or only Border Patrol postings, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered_postings` AS (
  SELECT
    `control_number`,
    DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', `open_date`) AS `open_month`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-01' AND DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND `occupational_series_codes` IS NOT NULL
    AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1896')
)
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS `row_type`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `open_month`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT `control_number`) AS `distinct_postings`
FROM `filtered_postings`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'MONTH' AS `row_type`,
  DATE_FORMAT(`open_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `open_month`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT `control_number`) AS `distinct_postings`
FROM `filtered_postings`
GROUP BY `open_month`
ORDER BY `row_type`, `open_month`
```

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. Higher-grade CBP Officer postings have the shorter advertised windows: grades 12 to 15 have medians of 6 days, while the lower grades 5 and 9 have medians of 30 and 28 days. This covers the 2025-09-01 to 2026-10-31 announcements listing series 1895 in CBP (HSBD), grouped by minimum grade.

| Minimum grade | Postings | Average window (days) | Median window (days) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 14 | 29.3 | 30 |
| 9 | 22 | 22.4 | 28 |
| 11 | 1 | 6.0 | 6 |
| 12 | 57 | 7.7 | 6 |
| 13 | 211 | 7.4 | 6 |
| 14 | 126 | 5.8 | 6 |
| 15 | 32 | 6.4 | 6 |

The window is the time between the announcement's open and close dates. It is not time to fill, because the records do not link a posting to a hire, so these figures cannot show how long a vacancy stayed unfilled. Grade 5 has only 14 postings and grade 9 has 22, so those medians are less stable. I read "stay open longer" as the advertised window by minimum grade across all CBP Officer postings opened in that span; if you meant which postings were still open on a given date, such as August 1, 2026, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `minimum_grade`,
  COUNT(*) AS `posting_count`,
  AVG(DATEDIFF(`close_date`, `open_date`)) AS `avg_window_days`,
  percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY DATEDIFF(`close_date`, `open_date`)) AS `median_window_days`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
  AND `open_date` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
  AND `open_date` <= DATE '2026-10-31'
  AND `minimum_grade` IS NOT NULL
  AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
  AND `close_date` IS NOT NULL
  AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1895')
GROUP BY `minimum_grade`
ORDER BY `minimum_grade` ASC
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) recorded 586 retirements over the twelve months from September 2025 to August 2026, and December 2025 was the clear peak at 152, about 26% of the total. Other months ran between 24 (November 2025) and 54 (September 2025), so retirements fall in every month and are heaviest at the turn of the calendar year. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months, especially August 2026, will grow. The counts combine voluntary, early-out, and other retirement categories and include the 2025 deferred resignation wave; I did not split that wave out. I read this as retirements by calendar month for the trailing twelve months to August 2026; if you meant a different window, or the split by retirement category, say so.

```sql
WITH month_spine AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS effective_month
), retirement_counts AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS retirement_count
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month >= TO_DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND separation.effective_month <= TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.separation_category IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'RETIREMENT - OTHER')
```

question_text: Which DHS components lost the most senior executives this year?
answer_text:
Exploratory

DHS Headquarters lost the most senior executives (pay plan ES) of any component: 57 separations in the twelve months to August 2026, followed by FEMA (44) and ICE (37), with 270 across all twelve components. TSA recorded none. These are counts of all separation categories, not rates, because this query did not pull senior executive headcounts. The count includes the 2025 deferred resignation wave, which this query does not separate out, and late reports keep arriving, so recent counts will grow.

I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026 and "senior executives" as the Senior Executive Service (pay plan ES). If you meant the separation rate for those executives, or the count excluding the deferred resignation wave, say so.

```sql
WITH requested_components AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM VALUES
    ('HSBD'), ('HSBC'), ('HSBB'), ('HSAB'), ('HSCB'), ('HSAD'),
    ('HSAC'), ('HSAA'), ('HSCA'), ('HSBE'), ('HSAE'), ('HSFA')

), separation_counts AS (
  SELECT
    separation.agency_subelement_code,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. Over the twelve months to August 2026, CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) separated at lower rates in the higher grades: 10.2% at grade 05 falls to 0.7% at grade 11, and grades 12 to 14 sit between 3.2% and 3.8%. Grade 15 is the one higher grade above 12 with a higher rate (6.6%), but it rests on 12 separations from about 180 people.

| Grade | Headcount Aug 2025 | Headcount Aug 2026 | Separations | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | 36 | 28 | 7 | 21.9% |
| 05 | 412 | 898 | 67 | 10.2% |
| 07 | 863 | 1,234 | 81 | 7.7% |
| 09 | 1,429 | 1,661 | 61 | 3.9% |
| 11 | 1,125 | 1,270 | 8 | 0.7% |
| 12 | 17,520 | 17,130 | 550 | 3.2% |
| 13 | 4,251 | 4,375 | 136 | 3.2% |
| 14 | 834 | 866 | 32 | 3.8% |
| 15 | 174 | 188 | 12 | 6.6% |

No separations in this cell came through the 2025 deferred resignation program, so the rates with and without it are the same. Late reports keep arriving, so these rates will rise slightly. Grades 05 and 07 grew sharply over the year, so their rates rest on a shifting base.

I read "higher-graded" as the grade numbers, with the trailing twelve-month separation rate; if you meant a split such as grade 12 and above against below, or the count of separations, say so.

```sql
WITH `start_headcount` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_start`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`end_headcount` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_end`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`separations` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS `separations_excluding_2025_deferred_resignation_program`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`grades` AS (
  SELECT `grade` FROM `start_headcount`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `end_headcount`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `separations`
)
SELECT
  `grades`.`grade` AS `grade`,
  COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) AS `headcount_start`,
  COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0) AS `headcount_end`,
  COALESCE(`separations`.`separations`, 0) AS `separations`,
  CASE
    WHEN (COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(COALESCE(`separations`.`separations`, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS `rate`,
  COALESCE(`separations`.`separations_excluding_2025_deferred_resignation_program`, 0) AS `separations_excluding_2025_deferred_resignation_program`,
  CASE
    WHEN (COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(COALESCE(`separations`.`separations_excluding_2025_deferred_resignation_program`, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS `rate_excluding_drp`
FROM `grades`
LEFT JOIN `start_headcount`
  ON `grades`.`grade` = `start_headcount`.`grade`
LEFT JOIN `end_headcount`
  ON `grades`.`grade` = `end_headcount`.`grade`
LEFT JOIN `separations`
  ON `grades`.`grade` = `separations`.`grade`
ORDER BY `grades`.`grade` ASC
```

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

About 5,460 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) in the August 2026 snapshot are aged 50 or over with 20 or more years of federal service, roughly one in five of the 27,299 officers in the cell. Of those, 2,980 are already aged 55 or over with 20 or more years (about 11% of the cell), and 2,483 are aged 50 to 54 and move into the 55 to 59 bracket within five years.

The records hold no retirement-eligibility flag, so this is an age-and-service proxy, not a forecast of retirements. Retirement rules for law enforcement officers depend on age and service in ways these figures do not capture, so check the eligibility rule before quoting this as eligibility. No officer in the cell is 65 or over. For actual departures, the separation rate and separation categories for this cell are the nearest alternative. I read this as age and years-of-service exposure in the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant retirement separations over the last twelve months, say so.

```sql
WITH `age_brackets` AS (
  SELECT stack(10,
    '20-24', 1,
    '25-29', 2,
    '30-34', 3,
    '35-39', 4,
    '40-44', 5,
    '45-49', 6,
    '50-54', 7,
    '55-59', 8,
    '60-64', 9,
    '65 or more', 10
  ) AS (`age_bracket`, `age_sort`)
),
`service_buckets` AS (
  SELECT stack(6,
    'under 1', 1,
    '1-3', 2,
    '3-5', 3,
    '5-10', 4,
    '10-20', 5,
    '20 or more', 6
  ) AS (`service_bucket`, `service_sort`)
),
`counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bracket`,
    CASE
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20 or more'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS `service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `age_bracket` IN ('20-24','25-29','30-34','35-39','40-44','45-49','50-54','55-59','60-64','65 or more')
    AND `length_of_service_years` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    `age_bracket`,
    CASE
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20 or more'
      ELSE NULL
    END
)
SELECT
  `a`.`age_bracket`,
  `s`.`service_bucket`,
  COALESCE(`c`.`headcount`, 0) AS `headcount`,
  COALESCE(`c`.`headcount`, 0) AS `total_headcount_for_cell`
FROM `age_brackets` AS `a`
CROSS JOIN `service_buckets` AS `s`
LEFT JOIN `counts` AS `c`
  ON `a`.`age_bracket` = `c`.`age_bracket`
 AND `s`.`service_bucket` = `c`.`service_bucket`
ORDER BY `a`.`age_sort`, `s`.`service_sort`
```

question_text: How long does it take us to hire a CBP Officer, from announcement to first day?
answer_text:
Exploratory
The median CBP Officer (HSBD, 1895) accession in the twelve months to August 2026 took 30 days from posting open date to the accession's effective month (average 23.3 days, n = 2,456).
This is a rough proxy, not a verified time-to-hire. The query measured to the first of the effective month, not the actual start date. It also matched every accession to a posting through a control number, which the records were not expected to support, so confirm that link before quoting the figure. Late OPM files can still add accessions, so the count will grow slightly.
I read this as the median days from posting open date to accession effective month for CBP Officers, September 2025 to August 2026; if you meant the full hiring cycle or the time to a specific pay plan, say so.

```sql
WITH accessions_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    accession.effective_month,
    accession.location_source_control_number,
    accession.pay_source_control_number
  FROM workforce.semantic.accession
  WHERE accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND accession.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND accession.effective_month >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND accession.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
),
linked_accessions AS (
  SELECT
    accessions_filtered.effective_month,
    accessions_filtered.location_source_control_number,
    accessions_filtered.pay_source_control_number,
    location_posting.control_number AS location_link_control_number,
    pay_posting.control_number AS pay_link_control_number,
    CASE
      WHEN location_posting.open_date IS NOT NULL AND pay_posting.open_date IS NOT NULL THEN LEAST(location_posting.open_date, pay_posting.open_date)
      ELSE COALESCE(location_posting.open_date, pay_posting.open_date)
    END AS linked_open_date
  FROM accessions_filtered
  LEFT JOIN workforce.semantic.job_posting AS location_posting
    ON accessions_filtered.location_source_control_number = location_posting.control_number
  LEFT JOIN workforce.semantic.job_posting AS pay_posting
    ON accessions_filtered.pay_source_control_number = pay_posting.control_number
)
SELECT
```

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory
The OPM data shows 1,041 separations of TSA screeners (Compliance Inspection and Support, 1802) effective October and November 2025, of which 702 were quits. That is 541 separations and 372 quits in October 2025, and 500 and 330 in November 2025. The 1,110 figure is 69 higher than the OPM count for these months. Only the 1802 series was counted here, so the gap may come from scope (all TSA occupations, or a different window); I have not checked that.

These months are well past, so late reports and restatements (about 0.8% of separations) may move the counts slightly. Four of the October separations came through the 2025 deferred resignation program, and none in November.

I read this as separations effective in October and November 2025 for TSA screeners, with quits as the QUIT category; if you meant all TSA occupations, or the count of separations from the 1,110 figure's source, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    `separation_category`,
    `drp_indicator`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802'
    AND `effective_month` IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
    AND `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `separation_category` IS NOT NULL
),
`by_category` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    `separation_category`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS `total_all_categories`,
    CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS `quit_count`,
    CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS `drp_count`
  FROM `filtered`
  GROUP BY `effective_month`, `separation_category`
),
`totals` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    'TOTAL' AS `separation_category`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    COUNT(*) AS `total_all_categories`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `separation_category` = 'QUIT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `quit_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `drp_count`
  FROM `filtered`
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  `effective_month`,
  `separation_category`,
  `separation_count`,
  `total_all_categories`,
  `quit_count`,
  `drp_count`
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM `totals`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM `by_category`
) `x`
ORDER BY
  `effective_month`,
  CASE WHEN `separation_category` = 'TOTAL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
  `separation_category`
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory
OPM shows 94 accessions into FEMA (HSCB), all occupational series, from October 2025 through May 2026. That is 92 new hires (78 excepted service, 9 competitive service, 5 SES) and 2 transfers in. The count is well short of GAO's 134, by 40 even on the full-May count.

Monthly counts: October 2025: 1; November: 8; December: 1; January 2026: 5; February: 0; March: 2; April: 1; May: 76. Through April the total is 18.

The month field is recorded at month level, so the cutoff of May 15 could not be applied to May. The 76 in May is the whole month, and the mid-May figure lies somewhere between 18 and 94. Later OPM files can still add accessions for these months, so the total will not fall.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSCB'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-05-15'
)
SELECT
  'total' AS `section`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `label`,
  CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS `effective_month`,
  COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`,
  0 AS `section_order`,
  0 AS `item_order`
FROM `filtered`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'by_accession_category' AS `section`,
  `accession_category` AS `label`,
  CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS `effective_month`,
  COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`,
  1 AS `section_order`,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, `accession_category`) AS `item_order`
FROM `filtered`
WHERE `accession_category` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `accession_category`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'by_effective_month' AS `section`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `label`,
  `effective_month`,
  COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`,
  2 AS `section_order`,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY `effective_month`) AS `item_order`
FROM `filtered`
WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `effective_month`
ORDER BY `section_order`, `item_order`
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration (HSBC), Compliance Inspection and Support 1802) averaged $74,762 in annual basic pay across 46,913 staff, while CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection (HSBD), 1895) averaged $104,656 across 27,650. That makes the CBP Officer average about $29,893 higher, or roughly 40% above the screener average.

Both averages are estimated: pay was imputed from job postings for 90.0% of TSA screener rows and 100% of CBP Officer rows, so treat the gap as an estimate. The figures are annualized basic pay only, not total compensation. I read "salary" as average annual basic pay across all staff in each cell at the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant a median, a different date, or pay by grade, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code,
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series,
  COUNT(*) AS headcount,
  AVG(workforce_snapshot.annualized_adjusted_basic_pay) AS average_annual_basic_pay,
  SUM(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS imputed_pay_rows,
  try_divide(SUM(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0, COUNT(*)) AS imputed_pay_share
FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND (
    (workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC' AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1802')
    OR (workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD' AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895')
  )
GROUP BY
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code,
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series
ORDER BY workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code, workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code
```

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?

As of the August 2026 snapshot, the cities with the most CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) are shown below. Every location is estimated: the city and state were imputed from job postings, which show where DHS hires rather than where officers sit.

| Detroit, Michigan | 440 |

| Houston, Texas | 368 |
| Blaine, Washington | 362 |

| Derby Line, Vermont | 321 |

The masking test covers FEMA (state match 0.117) and CISA (0.282), not CBP, so it gives no CBP-specific accuracy figure. Its results suggest the method is weaker than these figures imply, and it flatters the method for CBP, whose officers spread across many ports. I read this as the CBP Officer headcount by duty station city at the August 2026 snapshot, since no period was named; if you meant FY2026 Q1 or the states rather than cities, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `duty_station_city`,
  `duty_station_state`,
  `location_imputed`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS `total_headcount`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
  AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
  AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
  AND `duty_station_city` IS NOT NULL
  AND `duty_station_state` IS NOT NULL
  AND `location_imputed` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  `duty_station_city`,
  `duty_station_state`,
  `location_imputed`
ORDER BY `headcount` DESC, `duty_station_city` ASC, `duty_station_state` ASC
```

I read this as postings opened in the full September 2025 to October 2026 window, all components, counting any posting that lists 1896; if you meant only postings open on a particular date, or Border Patrol postings for one component, say so.

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory
Higher-grade CBP Officer postings do not stay open longer. Across the 469 CBP Officer announcements opened September 2025 to October 2026, grades 11 to 15 averaged 6 to 8 days open, while the two lowest grades, 7 and 9, averaged about 29 days. The 00-grade group (6 postings, 13 days average) is too small to read.

These are advertised windows (open date to close date), not time to fill, and they are not the duration of the posting's actual hiring process. None of the 469 postings was excluded for missing dates. The query did not return location or pay fields, so no figures here are estimated.

I read this as the advertised open-to-close window for all CBP Officer announcements opened in that period, grouped by the posting's maximum grade. If you meant the time from posting to hire, or only postings open on a given date, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    job_posting.control_number,
    job_posting.maximum_grade,
    job_posting.open_date,
    job_posting.close_date
  FROM workforce.semantic.job_posting
  WHERE job_posting.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND array_contains(job_posting.occupational_series_codes, '1895')
    AND job_posting.open_date IS NOT NULL
    AND job_posting.open_date >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND job_posting.open_date <= DATE '2026-10-31'
),
excluded AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS excluded_missing_dates
  FROM workforce.semantic.job_posting
  WHERE job_posting.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND array_contains(job_posting.occupational_series_codes, '1895')
    AND job_posting.open_date >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND job_posting.open_date <= DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND (job_posting.open_date IS NULL OR job_posting.close_date IS NULL)
),
valid AS (
  SELECT
    base.maximum_grade,
    datediff(base.close_date, base.open_date) AS days_open
  FROM base
  WHERE base.close_date IS NOT NULL
    AND base.maximum_grade IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  valid.maximum_grade,
  COUNT(*) AS posting_count,
  AVG(valid.days_open) AS avg_days_open,
  percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY valid.days_open) AS median_days_open,
  excluded.excluded_missing_dates,
  CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS location_imputed,
  CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS pay_imputed
FROM valid
CROSS JOIN excluded
GROUP BY valid.maximum_grade, excluded.excluded_missing_dates
ORDER BY valid.maximum_grade
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) retired 586 times in the twelve effective months September 2025 to August 2026. December 2025 is the peak at 152, about a quarter of the year's total, and November 2025 is the lowest at 24. Late reports keep arriving, so the recent months will grow. The monthly counts are in the block below; I added them to confirm the 586 total.

| Month | Retirements |
|---|---|
| 2025-09 | 54 |
| 2025-10 | 36 |
| 2025-11 | 24 |
| 2025-12 | 152 |
| 2026-01 | 44 |
| 2026-02 | 26 |
| 2026-03 | 31 |
| 2026-04 | 45 |
| 2026-05 | 52 |
| 2026-06 | 46 |
| 2026-07 | 45 |
| 2026-08 | 31 |

I read "retire" as all three retirement categories (voluntary, early out, other), by effective month over the trailing twelve months to August 2026; if you meant a split by the deferred resignation wave or a quarterly view, say so.

```sql
WITH months AS (
  SELECT explode(sequence(to_date('2025-09-01'), to_date('2026-08-01'), interval 1 month)) AS effective_month
), retirement_counts AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS retirement_count
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.effective_month >= to_date('2025-09-01')
    AND separation.effective_month <= to_date('2026-08-01')
    AND separation.separation_category IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'RETIREMENT - OTHER')
  GROUP BY separation.effective_month
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    date_format(months.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM') AS effective_month,
    COALESCE(retirement_counts.retirement_count, 0) AS retirement_count,
    months.effective_month AS sort_month
  FROM months
  LEFT JOIN retirement_counts
    ON months.effective_month = retirement_counts.effective_month
)
SELECT effective_month, retirement_count
FROM (
  SELECT effective_month, retirement_count, sort_month, 0 AS sort_order
  FROM monthly
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'TOTAL' AS effective_month, SUM(monthly.retirement_count) AS retirement_count, CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS sort_month, 1 AS sort_order
  FROM monthly
) result
ORDER BY result.sort_order, result.sort_month
```

question_text: How many CBP Officers who left this year had less than one year of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory
CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) recorded 170 separations with less than one year of service in the twelve months to August 2026 (September 2025 to August 2026). Of these, 78 were other separations, 76 quits, 14 terminations, and 2 transfers out, and none came through the 2025 deferred resignation program. Late reports keep arriving, so this count will grow slightly. I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026, with all separation categories; if you meant FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025) or only quits, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `separation`.`effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `separation`.`effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `separation`.`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `separation`.`occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `separation`.`length_of_service_years` < 1
)
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS row_type,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS separation_category,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS drp_indicator,
  COUNT(*) AS separation_count
FROM filtered
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'BY_CATEGORY_AND_DRP' AS row_type,
  filtered.separation_category,
  filtered.drp_indicator,
  COUNT(*) AS separation_count
FROM filtered
GROUP BY filtered.separation_category, filtered.drp_indicator
ORDER BY CASE WHEN row_type = 'TOTAL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, separation_count DESC, separation_category, drp_indicator
```
