question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) recorded 586 retirements in the twelve months from September 2025 to August 2026. December 2025 was the peak at 152, about a quarter of the total, and November 2025 was the low at 24. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months will grow. Every row's duty-station location is estimated from job postings, not published by OPM; the monthly counts themselves do not depend on location.

| Month | Retirements |
|---|---|
| 2025-09 | 54 |
| 2025-10 | 36 |
| 2025-11 | 24 |
| 2025-12 | 152 |
| 2026-01 | 44 |
| 2026-02 | 26 |
| 2026-03 | 31 |
| 2026-04 | 45 |
| 2026-05 | 52 |
| 2026-06 | 46 |
| 2026-07 | 45 |
| 2026-08 | 31 |

I read this as all three retirement categories (voluntary, early out, other) for the twelve effective months ending August 2026, counted by effective month; if you meant a different window or only one retirement category, say so.

```sql
WITH month_spine AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS effective_month
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS retirement_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS imputed_location_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.location_imputed = false THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS non_imputed_location_rows
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation AS separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.effective_month >= TO_DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND separation.effective_month <= TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND separation.separation_category IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'RETIREMENT - OTHER')
  GROUP BY separation.effective_month
), monthly_filled AS (
  SELECT
    month_spine.effective_month,
    COALESCE(monthly.retirement_count, 0) AS retirement_count,
    COALESCE(monthly.imputed_location_rows, 0) AS imputed_location_rows,
    COALESCE(monthly.non_imputed_location_rows, 0) AS non_imputed_location_rows,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(monthly.imputed_location_rows, 0) > 0 AND COALESCE(monthly.non_imputed_location_rows, 0) = 0 THEN 'all_imputed'
      WHEN COALESCE(monthly.imputed_location_rows, 0) > 0 AND COALESCE(monthly.non_imputed_location_rows, 0) > 0 THEN 'mixed'
      ELSE 'none_imputed'
    END AS location_imputed_status
  FROM month_spine
  LEFT JOIN monthly
    ON month_spine.effective_month = monthly.effective_month
)
SELECT
  DATE_FORMAT(monthly_filled.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM') AS effective_month,
  monthly_filled.retirement_count,
  monthly_filled.imputed_location_rows,
  monthly_filled.non_imputed_location_rows,
  monthly_filled.location_imputed_status,
  SUM(monthly_filled.retirement_count) OVER () AS twelve_month_total
FROM monthly_filled
ORDER BY monthly_filled.effective_month
```

question_text: How many CBP Officers who left this year had less than one year of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory
138 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) separated with less than one year of service from January to August 2026, out of 591 CBP Officer separations in the same months. Of the 138, 63 were OTHER SEPARATION, 59 QUIT, 14 TERMINATION (EXPIRED APPT/OTHER), and 2 TRANSFER OUT - INDIVIDUAL TRANSFER (the four add to 138). Late reports keep arriving, so this count will grow. I read "this year" as calendar 2026 to date (January to August 2026); if you meant the trailing twelve months to August 2026, say so and I will rerun it on that window.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT
    `separation_category`,
    `length_of_service_years`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
),
`totals` AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `lt_one_year_separations_count`,
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

Higher grades are not leaving at a higher rate, at least not across the board. For CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895), the separation rate for the twelve months to August 2026 is highest at grades 00 and 05 and falls to about 3 percent at grades 12 and 13. Grades 14 and 15 are slightly above 12 and 13, but on small counts.

| Grade | Separations | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| 00 | 7 | 0.219 |
| 05 | 67 | 0.102 |
| 07 | 81 | 0.077 |
| 09 | 61 | 0.039 |
| 11 | 8 | 0.007 |
| 12 | 550 | 0.032 |
| 13 | 136 | 0.032 |
| 14 | 32 | 0.038 |
| 15 | 12 | 0.066 |

The rate excluding the 2025 deferred resignation wave matches the overall rate in every grade for this window. Grade 00 has only 36 people at the start, so its rate is noisy. Grade and location are read from each snapshot, so promotions move people between grade rows. Grade 05 grew from 412 to 898 over the year, which makes its rate less clean. The location and pay fields for these rows are estimated, not published by OPM. Late reports keep arriving, so these separation counts will grow.

I read this as the trailing twelve-month separation rate by grade for CBP Officers to August 2026; if you meant the raw counts or a different window, say so.

The query that ran:

```sql
WITH sep AS (
  SELECT
    separation.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.drp_indicator <> 'Y' OR separation.drp_indicator IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS separations_excluding_drp,
    MAX(CASE WHEN separation.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sep_location_imputed_any,
    MAX(CASE WHEN separation.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sep_pay_imputed_any
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.effective_month BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-01' AND DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND separation.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY separation.grade
),
start_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS start_headcount,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS start_location_imputed_any,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS start_pay_imputed_any
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
end_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS end_headcount,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS end_location_imputed_any,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS end_pay_imputed_any
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(sep.grade, start_hc.grade, end_hc.grade) AS grade,
  COALESCE(sep.separations, 0) AS separations,
  COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) AS start_headcount,
  COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0) AS end_headcount,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(1.0 * COALESCE(sep.separations, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS rate,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(1.0 * COALESCE(sep.separations_excluding_drp, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS rate_excluding_drp,
  CASE
    WHEN GREATEST(
      COALESCE(sep.sep_location_imputed_any, 0),
      COALESCE(start_hc.start_location_imputed_any, 0),
      COALESCE(end_hc.end_location_imputed_any, 0)
    ) = 1 THEN true ELSE false
  END AS any_location_imputed_synthetic,
  CASE
    WHEN GREATEST(
      COALESCE(sep.sep_pay_imputed_any, 0),
      COALESCE(start_hc.start_pay_imputed_any, 0),
      COALESCE(end_hc.end_pay_imputed_any, 0)
    ) = 1 THEN true ELSE false
  END AS any_pay_imputed_synthetic
FROM sep
FULL OUTER JOIN start_hc
  ON sep.grade = start_hc.grade
FULL OUTER JOIN end_hc
  ON COALESCE(sep.grade, start_hc.grade) = end_hc.grade
WHERE COALESCE(sep.grade, start_hc.grade, end_hc.grade) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY grade
```

    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(sep.grade, start_hc.grade, end_hc.grade) AS grade,
  COALESCE(sep.separations, 0) AS separations,
  COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) AS start_headcount,
  COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0) AS end_headcount,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(1.0 * COALESCE(sep.separations, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS rate,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(1.0 * COALESCE(sep.separations_excluding_drp, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.start_headcount, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.end_headcount, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS rate_excluding_drp,
  CASE
    WHEN GREATEST(
      COALESCE(sep.sep_location_imputed_any, 0),
      COALESCE(start_hc.start_location_imputed_any, 0),
      COALESCE(end_hc.end_location_imputed_any, 0)
    ) = 1 THEN true ELSE false
  END AS any_location_imputed_synthetic,
  CASE
    WHEN GREATEST(
      COALESCE(sep.sep_pay_imputed_any, 0),
      COALESCE(start_hc.start_pay_imputed_any, 0),
      COALESCE(end_hc.end_pay_imputed_any, 0)
    ) = 1 THEN true ELSE false
  END AS any_pay_imputed_synthetic
FROM sep
FULL OUTER JOIN start_hc
  ON sep.grade = start_hc.grade
FULL OUTER JOIN end_hc
  ON COALESCE(sep.grade, start_hc.grade) = end_hc.grade
WHERE COALESCE(sep.grade, start_hc.grade, end_hc.grade) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY grade
label: Exploratory

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, 5,760 of the 27,650 CBP Officers (about 21%) are aged 50 or over with 20 or more years of federal service: 2,483 aged 50-54, 2,130 aged 55-59, 850 aged 60-64, and 297 aged 65 or more. This is exposure, not a forecast, since it does not model departures for other reasons. A further 2,245 officers aged 45-49 already have 20 or more years and would reach age 50 within the five-year window. The age and service figures are published, but the query's rows carry location and pay flags marked imputed for all 27,650 rows, so any location or pay figure for these officers is estimated from job postings.

I read "could retire" as the proxy of age 50 or over with 20 or more years of service, which I have not checked against OPM retirement rules. If you want the retirements actually recorded, the separation categories for the trailing twelve months are the nearest alternative.

```sql
WITH `base_all` AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bracket`,
    `length_of_service_years`,
    `location_imputed`,
    `pay_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
),
`imputation_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `location_imputed_true_rows`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `pay_imputed_true_rows`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = TRUE OR `pay_imputed` = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `either_imputed_true_rows`
  FROM `base_all`
),
`base` AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bracket`,
    CASE
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20 or more'
    END AS `service_bucket`
  FROM `base_all`
  WHERE `age_bracket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `length_of_service_years` IS NOT NULL
),
`crosstab` AS (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN GROUPING(`age_bracket`) = 1 THEN 'Total' ELSE `age_bracket` END AS `age_bracket`,
    CASE WHEN GROUPING(`service_bucket`) = 1 THEN 'Total' ELSE `service_bucket` END AS `service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
    CASE
      WHEN GROUPING(`age_bracket`) = 1 THEN 999
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '20-24' THEN 1
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '25-29' THEN 2
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '30-34' THEN 3
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '35-39' THEN 4
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '40-44' THEN 5
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '45-49' THEN 6
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '50-54' THEN 7
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '55-59' THEN 8
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '60-64' THEN 9
      WHEN `age_bracket` = '65 or more' THEN 10
      ELSE 998
    END AS `age_sort`,
    CASE
      WHEN GROUPING(`service_bucket`) = 1 THEN 999
      WHEN `service_bucket` = 'under 1' THEN 1
      WHEN `service_bucket` = '1-3' THEN 2
      WHEN `service_bucket` = '3-5' THEN 3
      WHEN `service_bucket` = '5-10' THEN 4
      WHEN `service_bucket` = '10-20' THEN 5
      WHEN `service_bucket` = '20 or more' THEN 6
      ELSE 998
    END AS `service_sort`
  FROM `base`
  GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((`age_bracket`, `service_bucket`), (`age_bracket`), (`service_bucket`), ())
)
SELECT
  `age_bracket`,
  `service_bucket`,
  `headcount`,
  `location_imputed_true_rows`,
  `pay_imputed_true_rows`,
  `either_imputed_true_rows`
FROM `crosstab`
CROSS JOIN `imputation_counts`
ORDER BY `age_sort`, `service_sort`
```

Assuming, as you state, that no one could be onboarded from October 1 to November 12, 2025, the plan scaled to the days hiring was possible is about 316 hires. The 475 actual accessions would then land 159 hires above that scaled plan (+50.1%), compared with 119 hires below the full plan of 594 (-20.0%).

- Days in the quarter: October 1 to December 31, 2025 = 31 + 30 + 31 = 92
- Days hiring could not happen: October 1 to November 12 = 31 + 12 = 43
- Days hiring was possible: 92 - 43 = 49
- Scaled plan: 594 x 49 / 92 = 316.4
- Variance against the scaled plan: 475 - 316.4 = +158.6 hires, or 158.6 / 316.4 = +50.1%

This comparison does not show the shutdown explains the earlier shortfall. Accessions in the data are counted by effective month, so the 475 are a count of actual accessions and would not be reduced by the assumption. question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory

The OPM data shows 1,041 TSA screener (1802) separations in October and November 2025, not 1,110, and 702 of them (67%) were quits: 372 in October and 330 in November. The category counts sum to the 1,041 total, so nothing is missing from the breakdown. The other separations were 182 "other separation," 126 voluntary retirements, 21 transfers out, and 10 other retirements. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts can still grow slightly. I cannot tell from the data what population the 1,110 figure covers, so the gap of 69 may reflect a different count rather than a different set of records.

I read this as TSA screeners (series 1802 within TSA) separations by effective month for October and November 2025. If you meant all TSA occupations, say so and I will rerun it.

```sql
WITH `base` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    `separation_category`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `effective_month` BETWEEN DATE('2025-10-01') AND DATE('2025-11-30')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802'
),
`category_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      WHEN `separation_category` = 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY' THEN 'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY'
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory

OPM records show 94 FEMA (HSCB) accessions effective from October 2025 through mid-May 2026, all occupational series. That is 40 fewer than GAO's 134, or about 30% below it. Most of the 94 fall in May 2026 (76), and late OPM files will add accessions, so this count will grow. The new-hire split returned zero, which doesn't match the totals, so I have left it out.

I read "hired" as all accessions in the window, not new hires only; if you meant new hires, say so. The GAO figure may also use a different definition of hire.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    `accession_category`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSCB'
    AND `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-05-15'
),
`monthly` AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', `effective_month`) AS `month_start`,
    COUNT(*) AS `total_accessions`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `accession_category` IN ('NEW HIRE - COMPETITIVE SERVICE', 'NEW HIRE - EXCEPTED SERVICE') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `new_hire_accessions`
  FROM `filtered`
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', `effective_month`)
)
SELECT
  DATE_FORMAT(`month_start`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month`,
  `total_accessions`,
  `new_hire_accessions`
FROM `monthly`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS `effective_month`,
  COUNT(*) AS `total_accessions`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `accession_category` IN ('NEW HIRE - COMPETITIVE SERVICE', 'NEW HIRE - EXCEPTED SERVICE') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `new_hire_accessions`
FROM `filtered`
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `effective_month` = 'TOTAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, `effective_month`
```

question_text: Month by month, how many CBP Officers did we hire from September 2025 to August 2026?
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) recorded 2,456 new-hire accessions from September 2025 to August 2026, the twelve months in the table below.

| Month | New hires |
|---|---|
| 2025-09 | 224 |
| 2025-10 | 80 |
| 2025-11 | 236 |
| 2025-12 | 159 |
| 2026-01 | 232 |
| 2026-02 | 166 |
| 2026-03 | 243 |
| 2026-04 | 159 |
| 2026-05 | 319 |
| 2026-06 | 160 |
| 2026-07 | 242 |
| 2026-08 | 236 |

The lowest month was October 2025 (80) and the highest May 2026 (319). The total is the sum of the twelve months. Late OPM files keep adding accessions, so the most recent months, July and August 2026, will grow. I read "hire" as new-hire accessions; transfers in and other accession categories are excluded. If you meant all accessions, say so and I will rerun it.

```sql
WITH `months` AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS `effective_month`
), `counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= TO_DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `accession_category` ILIKE '%NEW HIRE%'
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  DATE_FORMAT(`months`.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month`,
  COALESCE(`counts`.`accession_count`, 0) AS `accession_count`
FROM `months`
LEFT JOIN `counts`
  ON `months`.`effective_month` = `counts`.`effective_month`
ORDER BY `months`.`effective_month`
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

The average annualized basic pay of TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration (HSBC), series 1802) was $74,762 in the August 2026 snapshot, against $104,656 for CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection (HSBD), series 1895), about $29,893 or 40% higher. Pay for 42,225 of the 46,913 TSA screeners (90%) and all 27,650 CBP Officers is estimated from job postings, not published by OPM, so treat both averages as estimates. These are simple averages across all rows in each cell, with no filter by pay plan or grade.

I read this as average annual basic pay for the August 2026 snapshot, since you named no period; if you meant a different snapshot or the median, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `agency_subelement_code` AS `component_code`,
  `agency_subelement` AS `component`,
  `occupational_series_code` AS `series_code`,
  `occupational_series` AS `series`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_annual_basic_pay`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `pay_imputed_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND ((`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802')
    OR (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'))
GROUP BY
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`
ORDER BY `agency_subelement_code`, `occupational_series_code`
```

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, Washington, District of Columbia has the most CBP Officers (1,920), followed by Sterling, Virginia (751) and Ashburn, Virginia (678). The ten largest cities hold 6,114 of the 27,650 CBP Officers, about 22 percent.

| Rank | City, State | Headcount (estimated) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Washington, District of Columbia | 1,920 |
| 2 | Sterling, Virginia | 751 |
| 3 | Ashburn, Virginia | 678 |
| 4 | El Paso, Texas | 561 |
| 5 | Detroit, Michigan | 440 |
| 6 | New Orleans, Louisiana | 375 |
| 7 | Houston, Texas | 368 |
| 8 | Blaine, Washington | 362 |
| 9 | Miami, Florida | 338 |
| 10 | Derby Line, Vermont | 321 |

Every row's duty station is estimated, because OPM redacted it and the city was drawn from USAJOBS postings, which show where DHS hires rather than where officers sit. The masking test covered only FEMA and CISA, where the drawn state matched the true state 11.7% and 28.2% of the time; it flatters the method for CBP, so treat these city counts as a distribution estimate. I read this as CBP Officer headcount at the August 2026 snapshot, the latest; if you meant the FY2026 Q1 position or another occupation, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `duty_station_city`,
  `duty_station_state`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `imputed_location_rows`,
  SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS `total_headcount`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
  AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
  AND `duty_station_city` IS NOT NULL
  AND `duty_station_state` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  `duty_station_city`,
  `duty_station_state`
ORDER BY
  `headcount` DESC,
  `duty_station_city` ASC,
  `duty_station_state` ASC
```

question_text: Add up the first three quarters of FY2026: how far behind plan is each component on hiring?
answer_text:
Verified
Across FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (October 2025 to June 2026), DHS as a whole landed 17,370 accessions against a plan of 15,064 hires, a variance of +2,306 (+15.3%). Within that total, seven components are behind plan, led by FEMA (−1,896) and TSA (−1,032). Three component-quarters did not come back from the review's calculations after retries, so FLETC, the Office of the Inspector General, and Science and Technology carry partial sums, flagged below.

| Component | Planned hires | Actual accessions | Variance (hires) | Variance % of plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FEMA (HSCB) | 2,043 | 147 | −1,896 | −92.8% |
| TSA (HSBC) | 2,368 | 1,336 | −1,032 | −43.6% |
| Coast Guard civilian (HSAC) | 567 | 198 | −369 | −65.1% |
| CISA (HSCA) | 303 | 18 | −285 | −94.1% |
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 441 | 228 | −213 | −48.3% |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 1,203 | 1,053 | −150 | −12.5% |
| OIG (HSAE), Q1 and Q3 only | 24 | 2 | −22 | −91.7% |
| S&T (HSFA), Q2 and Q3 only | 12 | 0 | −12 | −100.0% |
| CBP (HSBD) | 4,182 | 5,734 | +1,552 | +37.1% |
| ICE (HSBB) | 3,186 | 7,573 | +4,387 | +137.7% |
| Secret Service (HSAD) | 627 | 884 | +257 | +41.0% |
| FLETC (HSBE), Q2 and Q3 only | 60 | 86 | +26 | +43.3% |

The gap between the DHS total and the twelve rows is the missing quarters. FLETC Q1, OIG Q2 and S&T Q1 together had 48 planned hires and 111 accessions (+63), so the DHS total is complete but their individual splits are not. ICE's Q1 figure (6,185 accessions against about 1,000 in each later quarter) drives its surplus and the DHS total; it is worth checking before quoting. Later OPM files add accessions, so every shortfall will narrow somewhat. I read "behind plan" as the hires variance summed over the three quarters for each component; if you meant the quarter-by-quarter percentage, say so.

question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory
889 USAJOBS postings listed Border Patrol Agent (series 1896) among their series, with announcement open dates from September 1, 2025 through October 31, 2026. All 889 are Customs and Border Protection (CBP) postings, and the count includes postings that also list other series.

I read this as all DHS postings opened in that window that list 1896 anywhere in their series; if you meant only postings open on a single date, or only the CBP Officer series, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered_postings` AS (
  SELECT
    `control_number`,
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    `agency_subelement`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE `control_number` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `open_date` <= DATE('2026-10-31')
    AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1896')
)
SELECT
  'ALL DHS' AS `scope`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `agency_subelement_code`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `agency_subelement`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT `control_number`) AS `distinct_posting_count`
FROM `filtered_postings`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'COMPONENT' AS `scope`,
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT `control_number`) AS `distinct_posting_count`
FROM `filtered_postings`
WHERE `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND `agency_subelement` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `agency_subelement_code`, `agency_subelement`
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `scope` = 'ALL DHS' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, `distinct_posting_count` DESC, `agency_subelement` ASC
```

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory

The data does not support the idea: higher-grade CBP Officer postings close sooner, not later. Across the 469 postings for CBP Officers (series 1895) opened from September 2025 to October 2026, grades 12 to 15 averaged 6 to 8 days between open and close (medians of 6 days), while grades 5 and 9 averaged 22 to 29 days. Grades 5 and 9 have only 14 and 22 postings, so those averages are noisy.

This measures the advertised window (open date to close date), not how long a vacancy stayed unfilled. The data does not link a posting to the hire it produced, so time-to-fill is not available. I read "stay open longer" as the advertised window by minimum grade across all postings opened in that period; if you meant postings open on a single date, or time to fill, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered_postings` AS (
  SELECT
    `minimum_grade`,
    DATEDIFF(`close_date`, `open_date`) AS `days_open`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1895')
    AND `open_date` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `open_date` <= DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND `minimum_grade` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `close_date` IS NOT NULL
),
`totals` AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS `total_postings_across_all_grades`
  FROM `filtered_postings`
)
SELECT
  `fp`.`minimum_grade`,
  COUNT(*) AS `number_of_postings`,
  AVG(`fp`.`days_open`) AS `avg_days_between_open_and_close`,
  percentile(`fp`.`days_open`, 0.5) AS `median_days_between_open_and_close`,
  `t`.`total_postings_across_all_grades`
FROM `filtered_postings` AS `fp`
CROSS JOIN `totals` AS `t`
GROUP BY `fp`.`minimum_grade`, `t`.`total_postings_across_all_grades`
ORDER BY TRY_CAST(`fp`.`minimum_grade` AS INT), `fp`.`minimum_grade`
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) retired most in December 2025, with 152 retirements, against a monthly range of 24 to 54 in the other months of the twelve months to August 2026. Retirements are the three voluntary, early-out, and other retirement categories combined, by effective month, from September 2025 to August 2026 (586 in total). Late reports keep arriving, so the recent months will grow. The count does not separate out the 2025 deferred resignation wave, so I cannot say whether the December spike belongs to it.

| Effective month | CBP Officer retirements |
|---|---|
| 2025-09 | 54 |
| 2025-10 | 36 |
| 2025-11 | 24 |
| 2025-12 | 152 |
| 2026-01 | 44 |
| 2026-02 | 26 |
| 2026-03 | 31 |
| 2026-04 | 45 |
| 2026-05 | 52 |
| 2026-06 | 46 |
| 2026-07 | 45 |
| 2026-08 | 31 |

The query that ran:

```sql
WITH `months` AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS `effective_month`
), `retirements` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `retirement_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= TO_DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `separation_category` IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'RETIREMENT - OTHER')
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  DATE_FORMAT(`months`.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month`,
  COALESCE(`retirements`.`retirement_count`, 0) AS `retirement_count`
FROM `months`
LEFT JOIN `retirements`
  ON `months`.`effective_month` = `retirements`.`effective_month`
ORDER BY `months`.`effective_month` ASC;
```

I read this as retirement counts by month for CBP Officers over the twelve months to August 2026; if you meant the share of separations that are retirements, or the split with the deferred resignation wave, say so.

question_text: How many CBP Officers who left this year had less than one year of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

170 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) separated with less than one year of service in the twelve months to August 2026, out of 954 CBP Officer separations in that period (about 18%).

All 954 rows carry estimated (imputed) duty-station location and pay, because OPM redacted them, so treat any location or pay breakdown as an estimate. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow. I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026; if you meant the fiscal year to date (October 2025 to August 2026), say so and I will rerun it for that window.

```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS `total_cbp_officer_separations`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `separations_under_1_year_service`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `rows_with_location_imputed`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `rows_with_pay_imputed`,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN true ELSE false END AS `any_location_imputed`,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN true ELSE false END AS `any_pay_imputed`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
  AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
  AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
  AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-08-01'
```

question_text: Which DHS components lost the most senior executives this year?
answer_text:
Exploratory

DHS Headquarters (HSAA) lost the most senior executives (Senior Executive Service, pay plan ES) in the twelve months to August 2026, with 57 separations, followed by FEMA (HSCB) with 44 and ICE (HSBB) with 37. Across DHS the total was 273. These are counts, not rates: the senior executive headcount by component was not part of this query, so a large component may not have lost the largest share. Late reports keep arriving, so recent counts will grow. The count includes all separation categories and deferred resignation separations, and HSDA (3) is a code outside the review's twelve components. I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026; if you meant calendar 2026 or FY2026 to date, say so.

```sql
WITH `component_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `c`.`agency_subelement_code` AS `agency_subelement_code`,
    COUNT(`s`.`agency_subelement_code`) AS `separation_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`component` AS `c`
  LEFT JOIN `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation` AS `s`
    ON `c`.`agency_subelement_code` = `s`.`agency_subelement_code`
   AND `s`.`agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
   AND `s`.`effective_month` IS NOT NULL
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. For CBP Officers (CBP, series 1895), grades 13 to 15 separated at a rate of 0.0337 over the twelve months to August 2026, against 0.0352 for grades 05 to 12. The gap is negligible. Grade 12 carries most of the headcount, at 0.0317. Grade 15 (0.0663, 12 separations on about 181 staff) and grade 14 (0.0376) sit above it, but the grade 15 base is small. The rates use the mean of the August 2025 and August 2026 headcounts as the denominator. Headcount moved sharply in some grades (grade 05 went from 412 to 898), so treat the small grades as rough. No separation in this cell is flagged as part of the 2025 deferred resignation program, so the rates with and without that wave are the same. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly.

| Grade | Headcount Aug 2025 | Headcount Aug 2026 | Separations | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | 36 | 28 | 7 | 0.2188 |
| 05 | 412 | 898 | 67 | 0.1023 |
| 07 | 863 | 1,234 | 81 | 0.0773 |
| 09 | 1,429 | 1,661 | 61 | 0.0395 |
| 11 | 1,125 | 1,270 | 8 | 0.0067 |
| 12 | 17,520 | 17,130 | 550 | 0.0317 |
| 13 | 4,251 | 4,375 | 136 | 0.0315 |
| 14 | 834 | 866 | 32 | 0.0376 |
| 15 | 174 | 188 | 12 | 0.0663 |

Rate is separations divided by the mean of the two headcounts. Grade 13 to 15 combined: 180 / 5,344 = 0.0337. Grade 05 to 12 combined: 767 / 21,771 = 0.0352.

I read "higher-graded" as grades 13 to 15 against grades 05 to 12, over the trailing twelve months to August 2026, using the separation rate. If you meant a different grade cut, or the count of separations rather than the rate, say so.

Query that ran:

```sql
WITH `headcount_start` AS ( SELECT `grade`, COUNT(*) AS `headcount_start` FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot` WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2025-09-01' AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895' AND `grade` IS NOT NULL GROUP BY `grade` ), `headcount_end` AS ( SELECT `grade`, COUNT(*) AS `headcount_end` FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot` WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01' AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895' AND `grade` IS NOT NULL GROUP BY `grade` ), `seps` AS ( SELECT `grade`, COUNT(*) AS `separations_all`, SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS `separations_excl_drp` FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation` WHERE `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-09-01' AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-08-01' AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895' AND `grade` IS NOT NULL GROUP BY `grade` ), `grades` AS ( SELECT `grade` FROM `headcount_start` UNION SELECT `grade` FROM `headcount_end` UNION SELECT `grade` FROM `seps` ) SELECT `grades`.`grade` AS `grade`, COALESCE(`headcount_start`.`headcount_start`, 0) AS `headcount_start`, COALESCE(`headcount_end`.`headcount_end`, 0) AS `headcount_end`, COALESCE(`seps`.`separations_all`, 0) AS `separations_all`, COALESCE(`seps`.`separations_excl_drp`, 0) AS `separations_excl_drp` FROM `grades` LEFT JOIN `headcount_start` ON `grades`.`grade` = `headcount_start`.`grade` LEFT JOIN `headcount_end` ON `grades`.`grade` = `headcount_end`.`grade` LEFT JOIN `seps` ON `grades`.`grade` = `seps`.`grade` ORDER BY `grades`.`grade`
```

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

About 5,463 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) are in the retirement exposure pool over the next five years: aged 50 to 64 now with 20 or more years of service, as of the August 2026 snapshot. That is 2,483 aged 50-54, 2,130 aged 55-59, and 850 aged 60-64, out of 27,299 officers in total. This is an upper bound, not a forecast: the records do not hold retirement plan eligibility rules, and not everyone eligible retires. The counts are published OPM values, not estimated, and the snapshot shows no officers in the 65-or-more bracket. I read this as the August 2026 headcount in that age and service band; if you meant a count of actual retirements, the separation rate with its retirement categories is the nearest alternative.

Query run (CBP Officers, HSBD, series 1895, snapshot 2026-08-01):

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS ( SELECT `age_bracket`, CASE WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20' WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20 or more' END AS `service_bucket` FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot` WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01' AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895' AND `age_bracket` IS NOT NULL AND `length_of_service_years` IS NOT NULL AND `age_bracket` IN ('20-24', '25-29', '30-34', '35-39', '40-44', '45-49', '50-54', '55-59', '60-64', '65 or more') ), `grouped` AS ( SELECT `age_bracket`, `service_bucket`, COUNT(*) AS `employee_count` FROM `filtered` WHERE `service_bucket` IS NOT NULL GROUP BY `age_bracket`, `service_bucket` ) SELECT `age_bracket`, `service_bucket`, `employee_count`, SUM(`employee_count`) OVER () AS `total_headcount` FROM `grouped` ORDER BY CASE `age_bracket` WHEN '20-24' THEN 1 WHEN '25-29' THEN 2 WHEN '30-34' THEN 3 WHEN '35-39' THEN 4 WHEN '40-44' THEN 5 WHEN '45-49' THEN 6 WHEN '50-54' THEN 7 WHEN '55-59' THEN 8 WHEN '60-64' THEN 9 WHEN '65 or more' THEN 10 ELSE 11 END, CASE `service_bucket` WHEN 'under 1' THEN 1 WHEN '1-3' THEN 2 WHEN '3-5' THEN 3 WHEN '5-10' THEN 4 WHEN '10-20' THEN 5 WHEN '20 or more' THEN 6 ELSE 7 END
```

answer_text:
Verified
Assuming, as you state, that no one could be onboarded from October 1 to November 12, 2025, the plan scaled to the 49 days when hiring was possible is about 316.4 hires. The 475 actual accessions land 158.6 hires (50.1%) above that scaled plan, compared with 119 hires (20.0%) under the full plan of 594.

- Days in the quarter: October 1 to December 31, 2025 = 31 + 30 + 31 = 92
- Days hiring could not happen: October 1 to November 12 = 31 + 12 = 43
- Days hiring was possible: 92 - 43 = 49
- Scaled plan: 594 × 49 / 92 = 316.4
- Variance against the scaled plan: 475 - 316.4 = 158.6, or 158.6 / 316.4 = 50.1%

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory
OPM shows 1,041 separations of TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration (TSA), series 1802) in the two months October and November 2025: 541 effective in October and 500 in November. Of those, 702 were quits (372 in October and 330 in November), so quits were about 67% of the total (702 / 1,041). The 1,110 figure TSA gave Congress is 69 higher than this count (1,110 − 1,041 = 69), and I cannot tell from the data what population that figure covered. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly.

I read this as all separation categories for TSA screeners with effective months October and November 2025, with quits as the subset; if you meant only the count TSA reported to Congress, or a different period, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    separation.separation_category
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1802'
    AND separation.effective_month IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
    AND separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
),
month_category AS (
  SELECT
    base.effective_month,
    'MONTH' AS row_scope,
    base.separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    1 AS scope_sort,
    1 AS category_sort
  FROM base
  WHERE base.separation_category IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY base.effective_month, base.separation_category
),
month_total AS (
  SELECT
    base.effective_month,
    'MONTH' AS row_scope,
    'TOTAL' AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    1 AS scope_sort,
    2 AS category_sort
  FROM base
  GROUP BY base.effective_month
),
combined_category AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'TWO_MONTHS_COMBINED' AS row_scope,
    base.separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    2 AS scope_sort,
    1 AS category_sort
  FROM base
  WHERE base.separation_category IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY base.separation_category
),
combined_total AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'TWO_MONTHS_COMBINED' AS row_scope,
    'TOTAL' AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    2 AS scope_sort,
    2 AS category_sort
  FROM base
),
quit_counts AS (
  SELECT
    base.effective_month,
    'QUIT_ONLY' AS row_scope,
    'QUIT' AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    3 AS scope_sort,
    1 AS category_sort
  FROM base
  WHERE base.separation_category = 'QUIT'
  GROUP BY base.effective_month
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'QUIT_ONLY' AS row_scope,
    'QUIT' AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    3 AS scope_sort,
    1 AS category_sort
  FROM base
  WHERE base.separation_category = 'QUIT'
)
SELECT
  u.effective_month,
  u.row_scope,
  u.separation_category,
  u.separation_count
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM month_category
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM month_total
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM combined_category
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM combined_total
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM quit_counts
) u
ORDER BY
  u.scope_sort,
  u.effective_month ASC NULLS LAST,
  u.category_sort,
  u.separation_category
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory
OPM shows 94 accessions for FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency, HSCB), all occupations, from October 2025 through May 2026, against GAO's 134. The OPM count is 40 lower (94 is 70% of 134).

The OPM window includes all of May 2026, not just the first half. The monthly data cannot split May at mid-month, so the total runs slightly past GAO's period. Late OPM files will add accessions, so the gap may narrow. Three of the 94 accession rows carry estimated duty-station locations and two carry estimated pay. GAO may define a "hire" differently from an OPM accession, so the two figures may not be like-for-like.

Monthly accessions: October 2025, 1; November 2025, 8; December 2025, 1; January 2026, 5; February 2026, 0; March 2026, 2; April 2026, 1; May 2026, 76.

I read this as all FEMA accessions in all occupations, October 2025 through May 2026; if you meant only Emergency Management Specialists (series 0089), or a cut at May 15 exactly, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(`effective_month`) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE 'MONTH' END AS `row_type`,
  `effective_month`,
  `location_imputed`,
  `pay_imputed`,
  COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSCB'
  AND `effective_month` IS NOT NULL

  AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-05-15'

  (`location_imputed`, `pay_imputed`),
  (`effective_month`, `location_imputed`, `pay_imputed`)
)
ORDER BY

  `pay_imputed` ASC
```

question_text: Month by month, how many CBP Officers did we hire from September 2025 to August 2026?
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) recorded 2,456 accessions from September 2025 to August 2026, by effective month:

| Month | Accessions |
|---|---|
| 2025-09 | 224 |
| 2025-10 | 80 |
| 2025-11 | 236 |
| 2025-12 | 159 |
| 2026-01 | 232 |
| 2026-02 | 166 |
| 2026-03 | 243 |
| 2026-04 | 159 |
| 2026-05 | 319 |
| 2026-06 | 160 |
| 2026-07 | 242 |
| 2026-08 | 236 |

The total is the sum of the twelve months. The count covers every accession category in the OPM accession records, so it may include transfers in as well as new hires. Late OPM files keep adding accessions, so the most recent months will grow. I read "hire" as an accession by effective month; if you meant new hires only, say so and I will split out the category.

```sql
WITH `months` AS (
  SELECT explode(sequence(to_date('2025-09-01'), to_date('2026-08-01'), interval 1 month)) AS `effective_month`
), `accession_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= to_date('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= to_date('2026-08-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  date_format(`months`.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `month`,
  COALESCE(`accession_counts`.`accession_count`, 0) AS `accession_count`
FROM `months`
LEFT JOIN `accession_counts`
  ON `months`.`effective_month` = `accession_counts`.`effective_month`
ORDER BY `months`.`effective_month` ASC
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory
As of the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, 1802) average $74,762 in annual basic pay across 46,913 staff, and CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) average $104,656 across 27,650. CBP Officers therefore average about $29,893 (about 40%) more.

These averages are estimated. Pay was imputed from job postings for 42,225 of the 46,913 TSA screener rows (about 90%) and for all 27,650 CBP Officer rows, so neither average is a published OPM figure. The query also returned no average for the unimputed TSA rows, so I cannot yet say how far the published figures differ from the estimates.

I read "salary" as the mean annual basic pay (not total compensation) at the latest snapshot, August 2026. If you meant the median, or only the published pay figures, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `agency_subelement_code` AS `component_code`,
  `occupational_series_code` AS `series`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_annual_basic_pay`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `pay_imputed_row_count`,
  AVG(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = false OR `pay_imputed` IS NULL THEN `annualized_adjusted_basic_pay` END) AS `average_annual_basic_pay_non_imputed`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND `occupational_series_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND ((`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802')
    OR (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'))
GROUP BY `agency_subelement_code`, `occupational_series_code`
ORDER BY `agency_subelement_code`, `occupational_series_code`
```

question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory
The review found 889 USAJOBS postings that list Border Patrol Agent (series 1896) and opened between September 1, 2025 and October 31, 2026. All 889 are Customs and Border Protection announcements, and the count includes postings that also list other series. This is a count of announcements by open date, not of postings still open on a given day.

I read this as all of DHS, counting each posting once by open date across the full window; if you meant only postings open on one date, or only the Border Patrol component, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered_postings AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    job_posting.control_number,
    job_posting.agency_subelement
  FROM workforce.semantic.job_posting
  WHERE job_posting.open_date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2026-10-31')
    AND array_contains(job_posting.occupational_series_codes, '1896')
)
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS row_type,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS agency_subelement,
  COUNT(*) AS posting_count
FROM filtered_postings
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'BY_COMPONENT' AS row_type,
  filtered_postings.agency_subelement,
  COUNT(*) AS posting_count
FROM filtered_postings
WHERE filtered_postings.agency_subelement IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY filtered_postings.agency_subelement
ORDER BY row_type, posting_count DESC, agency_subelement
```

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. Higher-grade CBP Officer postings do not stay open longer. Across the 469 CBP Officer announcements opened September 2025 to October 2026, the median announced window was 6 days at minimum grades 11 to 15 (averages 5.8 to 7.7 days). The longest windows were at the lowest grades: a median of 30 days at grade 5 and 27 at grade 9 (averages 29.3 and 22.4 days). Grades 9 and 5 have few postings, and grade 00 (6 postings) is thin too. A window is the announced open-to-close span, not a record of how long a posting stayed open, and the data has no applicant records, so this does not measure time to fill.

I read "stay open longer" as the announced window from open date to close date for every CBP Officer posting; if you meant how many postings were still open on a given date, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered_postings AS (
  SELECT
    job_posting.minimum_grade,
    job_posting.open_date,
    job_posting.close_date,
    DATEDIFF(job_posting.close_date, job_posting.open_date) AS window_days,
    CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS location_imputed,
    CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS pay_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.job_posting
  WHERE job_posting.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND job_posting.open_date >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND job_posting.open_date <= DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND job_posting.open_date IS NOT NULL
    AND job_posting.close_date IS NOT NULL
    AND job_posting.minimum_grade IS NOT NULL
    AND array_contains(job_posting.occupational_series_codes, '1895')
), summary_by_grade AS (
  SELECT
    filtered_postings.minimum_grade,
    AVG(filtered_postings.window_days) AS avg_window_days,
    percentile_approx(filtered_postings.window_days, 0.5) AS median_window_days
  FROM filtered_postings
  WHERE filtered_postings.window_days IS NOT NULL
    AND filtered_postings.minimum_grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY filtered_postings.minimum_grade
)
SELECT
  'posting_detail' AS result_type,
  filtered_postings.minimum_grade,
  filtered_postings.open_date,
  filtered_postings.close_date,
  filtered_postings.window_days,
  filtered_postings.location_imputed,
  filtered_postings.pay_imputed,
  CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS avg_window_days,
  CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS median_window_days
FROM filtered_postings
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'summary_by_minimum_grade' AS result_type,
  summary_by_grade.minimum_grade,
  CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS open_date,
  CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS close_date,
  CAST(NULL AS INT) AS window_days,
  CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS location_imputed,
  CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS pay_imputed,
  summary_by_grade.avg_window_days,
  summary_by_grade.median_window_days
FROM summary_by_grade
ORDER BY result_type, minimum_grade, open_date, close_date
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) recorded 586 retirements in the twelve months from September 2025 to August 2026. December 2025 was the peak at 152, about three times the monthly average of 49, and every other month ran between 24 and 54. Late reports keep arriving, so the recent months, especially August 2026, will grow.

| Month | Retirements |
|---|---|
| 2025-09 | 54 |
| 2025-10 | 36 |
| 2025-11 | 24 |
| 2025-12 | 152 |
| 2026-01 | 44 |
| 2026-02 | 26 |
| 2026-03 | 31 |
| 2026-04 | 45 |
| 2026-05 | 52 |
| 2026-06 | 46 |
| 2026-07 | 45 |
| 2026-08 | 31 |

I read "retire" as the three retirement categories (voluntary, early out, and other) and "in the year" as the twelve effective months to August 2026. If you meant all separations, or the fiscal year, say so.

```sql
WITH `month_spine` AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS `effective_month`
), `retirement_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `retirement_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `separation_category` IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'RETIREMENT - OTHER')
    AND `effective_month` BETWEEN TO_DATE('2025-09-01') AND TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  DATE_FORMAT(`m`.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month`,
  COALESCE(`r`.`retirement_count`, 0) AS `retirement_count`,
  SUM(COALESCE(`r`.`retirement_count`, 0)) OVER () AS `total_across_twelve_months`
FROM `month_spine` `m`
LEFT JOIN `retirement_counts` `r`
  ON `m`.`effective_month` = `r`.`effective_month`
ORDER BY `m`.`effective_month`
```

question_text: How many CBP Officers who left this year had less than one year of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory
138 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) with less than one year of service separated from January through August 2026, out of 591 separations in that cell.
The count is a one-off result from the separation records, and it is right-censored: late reports keep arriving, so it will grow. Most of the short-service exits were quits (59) and "other separations" (63), and no voluntary retirements were under one year. question_text: Which DHS components lost the most senior executives this year?
answer_text:
Exploratory
DHS Headquarters (HSAA) lost the most senior executives in the trailing twelve months to August 2026, with 57 separations (42 excluding the 2025 deferred resignation program wave). FEMA (HSCB) was second with 44 (21 excluding that wave), and ICE (HSBB) third with 37. TSA (HSBC) recorded no senior executive separations. These are counts, not rates, because I did not pull senior executive headcount by component. Late reports keep arriving, so recent counts will grow.

| Component | Total separations | Excluding 2025 DRP wave |
|---|---|---|
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 57 | 42 |
| FEMA (HSCB) | 44 | 21 |
| ICE (HSBB) | 37 | 37 |
| CBP (HSBD) | 31 | 31 |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 30 | 21 |
| CISA (HSCA) | 27 | 20 |
| Secret Service (HSAD) | 23 | 23 |
| Science and Technology (HSFA) | 8 | 3 |
| Coast Guard civilian (HSAC) | 7 | 6 |
| FLETC (HSBE) | 4 | 4 |
| OIG (HSAE) | 2 | 1 |
| TSA (HSBC) | 0 | 0 |

Totals across all twelve components are 270 separations, or 209 excluding the deferred resignation wave (the rows sum to these figures).

I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026 (September 2025 to August 2026), with senior executives as the Senior Executive Service pay plan (ES) across any grade; if you meant the calendar year 2026 or a separation rate, say so.

The query that ran:

```sql
WITH `requested_components` AS (
  SELECT * FROM VALUES
    ('HSBD'), ('HSBC'), ('HSBB'), ('HSAB'), ('HSCB'), ('HSAD'),
    ('HSAC'), ('HSAA'), ('HSCA'), ('HSBE'), ('HSAE'), ('HSFA')
  AS `t`(`agency_subelement_code`)
),
`separation_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    COUNT(*) AS `total_separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS `separations_excluding_drp`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` IN ('HSBD','HSBC','HSBB','HSAB','HSCB','HSAD','HSAC','HSAA','HSCA','HSBE','HSAE','HSFA')
    AND `pay_plan_code` = 'ES'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
  GROUP BY `agency_subelement_code`
)
SELECT
  rc.`agency_subelement_code`,
  COALESCE(sc.`total_separations`, 0) AS `total_separations`,
  COALESCE(sc.`separations_excluding_drp`, 0) AS `separations_excluding_drp`
FROM `requested_components` rc
LEFT JOIN `separation_counts` sc
  ON rc.`agency_subelement_code` = sc.`agency_subelement_code`
ORDER BY rc.`agency_subelement_code`
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No, not in general. Across CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) over the trailing twelve months to August 2026, the separation rate falls as grade rises from 05 to 11, then sits at about 3 to 4 percent for grades 12 to 14. Grade 15 is higher at 6.6 percent, but that rests on only 12 separations. The highest rates are at grade 00 (21.9 percent, 7 separations from about 32 average headcount) and grade 05 (10.2 percent). The grade 00 figure is too small to quote alone.

Rates by grade, with and without the 2025 deferred resignation program: the two are identical for every grade, because this population has no deferred resignation separations in the window. Across all grades the cell total is 954 separations, a rate of 0.0351, which matches the review's standard calculation for the cell. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly. Some rows carry estimated location and pay values; those fields are not used in the grade rates.

I read this as the trailing twelve-month separation rate by grade, with "higher-graded" meaning grades 12 to 15; if you meant the count of separations or a different period, say so.

```sql
WITH sep_by_grade AS (
  SELECT
    separation.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.drp_indicator <> 'Y' OR separation.drp_indicator IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program,
    MAX(CASE WHEN separation.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sep_has_location_imputed,
    MAX(CASE WHEN separation.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sep_has_pay_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.effective_month >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND separation.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY separation.grade
),
start_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_2025_09_01,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS start_has_location_imputed,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS start_has_pay_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
end_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_2026_08_01,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS end_has_location_imputed,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS end_has_pay_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
grades AS (
  SELECT sep_by_grade.grade AS grade FROM sep_by_grade
  UNION
  SELECT start_hc.grade AS grade FROM start_hc
  UNION
  SELECT end_hc.grade AS grade FROM end_hc
)
SELECT
  grades.grade AS grade,
  COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations, 0) AS separations,
  COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program, 0) AS separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program,
  COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_2025_09_01, 0) AS headcount_2025_09_01,
  COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_2026_08_01, 0) AS headcount_2026_08_01,
  try_divide(
    100.0 * COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations, 0),
    try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_2025_09_01, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_2026_08_01, 0)),2.0)
  ) AS separation_rate,
  try_divide(
    100.0 * COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations_excluding_deferred_resignation_program, 0),
    try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_2025_09_01, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_2026_08_01, 0)),2.0)
  ) AS separation_rate_excluding_deferred_resignation_program,
  CASE
    WHEN GREATEST(
      COALESCE(sep_by_grade.sep_has_location_imputed, 0),
      COALESCE(start_hc.start_has_location_imputed, 0),
      COALESCE(end_hc.end_has_location_imputed, 0)
    ) = 1 THEN true ELSE false
  END AS has_location_imputed_rows,
  CASE
    WHEN GREATEST(
      COALESCE(sep_by_grade.sep_has_pay_imputed, 0),
      COALESCE(start_hc.start_has_pay_imputed, 0),
      COALESCE(end_hc.end_has_pay_imputed, 0)
    ) = 1 THEN true ELSE false
  END AS has_pay_imputed_rows
FROM grades
LEFT JOIN sep_by_grade
  ON grades.grade = sep_by_grade.grade
LEFT JOIN start_hc
  ON grades.grade = start_hc.grade
LEFT JOIN end_hc
  ON grades.grade = end_hc.grade
WHERE grades.grade IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY grades.grade
```

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

On the August 2026 snapshot, about 5,460 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) are in the age and service groups that could plausibly retire within five years: 2,980 are already 55 or older with 20 or more years of service, and 2,483 more are 50 to 54 with 20 or more years and reach 55 within the window. That is about 20% of the 27,299 officers on the snapshot. This is a proxy from age and years of service, not a retirement-eligibility determination, because the records here do not apply the retirement-plan rules. The count ignores departures that happen before retirement, so it is an upper bound on the group that could leave. Late reports keep arriving, so counts will shift slightly.

| Age bracket | 20+ years of service | Role in the five-year window |
|---|---|---|
| 55-59 | 2,130 | Already in the age range |
| 60-64 | 850 | Already in the age range |
| 65 or more | 0 | No officers in the snapshot |
| 50-54 | 2,483 | Reach 55 within five years |

I read "could retire in the next five years" as the age-and-service proxy on the August 2026 headcount, for CBP Officers only. If you meant a formal eligibility count under the retirement-plan rules, or the separation rate for retirements, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bracket`,
    CASE
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20 or more'
    END AS `service_bucket`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `age_bracket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `length_of_service_years` IS NOT NULL
    AND `age_bracket` IN ('20-24', '25-29', '30-34', '35-39', '40-44', '45-49', '50-54', '55-59', '60-64', '65 or more')
), agg AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bracket`,
    `service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`
  FROM base
  WHERE `service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `age_bracket`, `service_bucket`
), pivoted AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bracket`,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN `service_bucket` = 'under 1' THEN `headcount` END), 0) AS `under_1`,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN `service_bucket` = '1-3' THEN `headcount` END), 0) AS `1_3`,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN `service_bucket` = '3-5' THEN `headcount` END), 0) AS `3_5`,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN `service_bucket` = '5-10' THEN `headcount` END), 0) AS `5_10`,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN `service_bucket` = '10-20' THEN `headcount` END), 0) AS `10_20`,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN `service_bucket` = '20 or more' THEN `headcount` END), 0) AS `20_or_more`
  FROM agg
  GROUP BY `age_bracket`
)
SELECT
  `age_bracket`,
  `under_1`,
  `1_3`,
  `3_5`,
  `5_10`,
  `10_20`,
  `20_or_more`,
  (`under_1` + `1_3` + `3_5` + `5_10` + `10_20` + `20_or_more`) AS `total_headcount`
FROM pivoted
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'Total' AS `age_bracket`,
  SUM(`under_1`) AS `under_1`,
  SUM(`1_3`) AS `1_3`,
  SUM(`3_5`) AS `3_5`,
  SUM(`5_10`) AS `5_10`,
  SUM(`10_20`) AS `10_20`,
  SUM(`20_or_more`) AS `20_or_more`,
  SUM(`under_1` + `1_3` + `3_5` + `5_10` + `10_20` + `20_or_more`) AS `total_headcount`
FROM pivoted
ORDER BY CASE `age_bracket`
  WHEN '20-24' THEN 1
  WHEN '25-29' THEN 2
  WHEN '30-34' THEN 3
  WHEN '35-39' THEN 4
  WHEN '40-44' THEN 5
  WHEN '45-49' THEN 6
  WHEN '50-54' THEN 7
  WHEN '55-59' THEN 8
  WHEN '60-64' THEN 9
  WHEN '65 or more' THEN 10
  WHEN 'Total' THEN 11
END
```

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory

OPM records show 1,041 separations of TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, HSBC, series 1802) effective October and November 2025: 541 in October and 500 in November. Of those, 702 were quits (372 in October and 330 in November). That is 69 below the roughly 1,110 TSA reported to Congress. The records carry separation categories, not reasons, so they cannot show whether the shutdown caused any of these departures. These two months are nearly closed, so only small late restatements are likely to change the count. I read "left" as all separations in the October and November 2025 effective months; if you meant another measure, such as the separation rate, or a different period, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    CASE
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      WHEN separation.separation_category ILIKE 'RETIREMENT%' THEN separation.separation_category
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TERMINATION' THEN 'TERMINATION'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 'REDUCTION IN FORCE'
      ELSE 'OTHER SEPARATION'
    END AS separation_category_group,
    separation.drp_indicator
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation AS separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1802'
    AND separation.effective_month BETWEEN DATE '2025-10-01' AND DATE '2025-11-30'
    AND separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    'monthly_breakdown' AS row_type,
    base.effective_month,
    base.separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS drp_separations_count
  FROM base
  GROUP BY base.effective_month, base.separation_category_group
), totals AS (
  SELECT
    'two_month_total' AS row_type,
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'ALL SEPARATIONS' AS separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS drp_separations_count
  FROM base
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'two_month_quit_total' AS row_type,
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'QUIT' AS separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN base.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS drp_separations_count
  FROM base
  WHERE base.separation_category_group = 'QUIT'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'two_month_drp_total' AS row_type,
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'DRP (drp_indicator = Y)' AS separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations_count,
    COUNT(*) AS drp_separations_count
  FROM base
  WHERE base.drp_indicator = 'Y'
)
SELECT
  result.row_type,
  result.effective_month,
  result.separation_category_group,
  result.separations_count,
  result.drp_separations_count
FROM (
  SELECT
    monthly.row_type,
    monthly.effective_month,
    monthly.separation_category_group,
    monthly.separations_count,
    monthly.drp_separations_count
  FROM monthly
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    totals.row_type,
    totals.effective_month,
    totals.separation_category_group,
    totals.separations_count,
    totals.drp_separations_count
  FROM totals
) AS result
ORDER BY
  CASE result.row_type
    WHEN 'monthly_breakdown' THEN 1
    WHEN 'two_month_total' THEN 2
    WHEN 'two_month_quit_total' THEN 3
    WHEN 'two_month_drp_total' THEN 4
    ELSE 5
  END,
  result.effective_month,
  result.separation_category_group
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory

OPM records show 94 accessions into FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency, HSCB) across all occupational series for October 2025 through May 2026, 40 fewer than GAO's 134 (94 is 70% of 134). By month: October 1, November 8, December 1, January 5, February 0, March 2, April 1, May 76. Late reports keep arriving, so the OPM count will grow slightly. The query filtered on month start dates, so May is counted in full rather than only to mid-May; a mid-May cutoff would give 94 or fewer, which widens the gap. Three of the 94 rows carry estimated duty-station location or pay; they are included and do not change the total.

I read "hired" as all FEMA accessions by effective month, including any transfers in; if you meant new hires only, or a different cutoff, say so and I can rerun.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    accession.effective_month,
    accession.location_imputed,
    accession.pay_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.accession
  WHERE accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSCB'
    AND accession.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND accession.effective_month >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND accession.effective_month <= DATE '2026-05-15'
),
monthly AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_FORMAT(accession.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM') AS effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS accession_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS location_imputed_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pay_imputed_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.location_imputed = true OR accession.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS location_or_pay_imputed_rows,
    MIN(accession.effective_month) AS sort_month
  FROM base AS accession
  GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(accession.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM')
),
total AS (
  SELECT
    'TOTAL' AS effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS accession_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS location_imputed_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pay_imputed_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.location_imputed = true OR accession.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS location_or_pay_imputed_rows,
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS sort_month
  FROM base AS accession
)
SELECT
  result.effective_month,
  result.accession_count,
  result.location_imputed_rows,
  result.pay_imputed_rows,
  result.location_or_pay_imputed_rows
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM monthly
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM total
) AS result
ORDER BY CASE WHEN result.sort_month IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, result.sort_month
```

question_text: Month by month, how many CBP Officers did we hire from September 2025 to August 2026?
answer_text:
Exploratory
CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) had 2,456 accessions effective from September 2025 through August 2026. The monthly counts are below.

| Month | Accessions |
|---|---|
| 2025-09 | 224 |
| 2025-10 | 80 |
| 2025-11 | 236 |
| 2025-12 | 159 |
| 2026-01 | 232 |
| 2026-02 | 166 |
| 2026-03 | 243 |
| 2026-04 | 159 |
| 2026-05 | 319 |
| 2026-06 | 160 |
| 2026-07 | 242 |
| 2026-08 | 236 |

The total is the sum of the twelve months (224 + 80 + 236 + 159 + 232 + 166 + 243 + 159 + 319 + 160 + 242 + 236 = 2,456). Late OPM reports keep arriving, so the most recent months may still grow. I read "hired" as every accession action in the records for this series, which can include transfers in as well as new hires; the records do not separate them in this count, so if you need new hires only, say so and I can run that split.

```sql
WITH `months` AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS `effective_month`
), `counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= TO_DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  DATE_FORMAT(`months`.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month`,
  COALESCE(`counts`.`accession_count`, 0) AS `accession_count`
FROM `months`
LEFT JOIN `counts`
  ON `months`.`effective_month` = `counts`.`effective_month`
ORDER BY `months`.`effective_month` ASC;
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, series 1802) had an average annual basic pay of $74,762 across 46,913 staff, and CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) averaged $104,656 across 27,650 staff, about $29,893 more. Both averages are estimated: 42,225 of the TSA rows (about 90%) and all 27,650 CBP rows have pay estimated from job postings, not published by OPM. Each figure is a simple average across all grades and pay plans in the cell, so it reflects the mix of staff rather than a single grade's pay.

I read "salary" as annual basic pay in the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant a different month or a grade-level figure, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code AS component_code,
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement AS component,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code AS series_code,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series AS series,
  COUNT(*) AS headcount,
  AVG(workforce_snapshot.annualized_adjusted_basic_pay) AS average_annual_basic_pay,
  SUM(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS imputed_pay_row_count
FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND (
    (workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC' AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1802')
    OR (workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD' AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895')
  )
GROUP BY
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code,
  workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code,
  workforce_snapshot.occupational_series
ORDER BY workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code, workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code
```

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

The largest CBP Officer (1895) concentrations in the August 2026 snapshot are estimated at Washington, District of Columbia (1,920), Sterling, Virginia (751), Ashburn, Virginia (678), and El Paso, Texas (561), out of 27,650 officers in the cell. The top 15 cities hold 7,645 of them (27.6%).

All of these locations are imputed: OPM redacted the duty stations, so they were estimated from USAJOBS postings. Postings show where DHS hires, not where officers sit, so this is a distribution estimate. I did not run the masking test on this answer, and that test flatters the method for CBP, so treat the ranking as indicative. The Washington figure in particular likely reflects headquarters postings rather than officers posted there.

I read this as CBP Officers' duty-station cities in the August 2026 snapshot, the latest; if you meant a different snapshot or a count by state, say so.

```sql
WITH `cell_rows` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    `location_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
),
`total_cell` AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS `total_headcount`
  FROM `cell_rows`
),
`grouped` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city` AS `city`,
    `duty_station_state` AS `state`,
    `location_imputed`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`
  FROM `cell_rows`
  WHERE `duty_station_city` IS NOT NULL
    AND `duty_station_state` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    `location_imputed`
)
SELECT
  `grouped`.`city`,
  `grouped`.`state`,
  `grouped`.`headcount`,
  `grouped`.`location_imputed`,
  `total_cell`.`total_headcount`
FROM `grouped`
CROSS JOIN `total_cell`
ORDER BY
  `grouped`.`headcount` DESC,
  `grouped`.`city` ASC,
  `grouped`.`state` ASC,
  `grouped`.`location_imputed` ASC
LIMIT 15
```
