Sort by grade ascending. Include the imputed-location flag if any row used imputed values.

columns: separations in the twelve months (all categories)
separations in the twelve months excluding 2025 deferred resignation program separations
rate excluding deferred resignation program separations

genie_sql:
WITH start_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.pay_plan_code,
    workforce_snapshot.grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_start,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS start_any_location_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.pay_plan_code IS NOT NULL
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.pay_plan_code, workforce_snapshot.grade
),
end_hc AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.pay_plan_code,
    workforce_snapshot.grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_end,
    MAX(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS end_any_location_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.pay_plan_code IS NOT NULL
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.pay_plan_code, workforce_snapshot.grade
),
seps AS (
  SELECT
    separation.pay_plan_code,
    separation.grade,
    COUNT(*) AS separations_12m_all,
    SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(separation.drp_indicator, 'N') <> 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS separations_12m_excl_drp,
    MAX(CASE WHEN separation.location_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sep_any_location_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.pay_plan_code IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY separation.pay_plan_code, separation.grade
),
by_grade AS (
  SELECT
    CONCAT(COALESCE(start_hc.pay_plan_code, end_hc.pay_plan_code, seps.pay_plan_code), '-', COALESCE(start_hc.grade, end_hc.grade, seps.grade)) AS grade,
    COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) AS `headcount at 2025-09-01`,
    COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0) AS `headcount at 2026-08-01`,
    COALESCE(seps.separations_12m_all, 0) AS `separations in the twelve months (all categories)`,
    COALESCE(seps.separations_12m_excl_drp, 0) AS `separations in the twelve months excluding 2025 deferred resignation program separations`,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE try_divide(100.0 * COALESCE(seps.separations_12m_all, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0)),2.0)))
    END AS `rate with all separations`,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE try_divide(100.0 * COALESCE(seps.separations_12m_excl_drp, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(start_hc.headcount_start, 0) + COALESCE(end_hc.headcount_end, 0)),2.0)))
    END AS `rate excluding deferred resignation program separations`,
    CASE
      WHEN GREATEST(COALESCE(start_hc.start_any_location_imputed, 0), COALESCE(end_hc.end_any_location_imputed, 0), COALESCE(seps.sep_any_location_imputed, 0)) = 1 THEN true
      ELSE false
    END AS any_imputed_location_used,
    COALESCE(start_hc.pay_plan_code, end_hc.pay_plan_code, seps.pay_plan_code) AS sort_pay_plan_code,
    COALESCE(start_hc.grade, end_hc.grade, seps.grade) AS sort_grade,
    0 AS sort_total
  FROM start_hc
  FULL OUTER JOIN end_hc
    ON start_hc.pay_plan_code = end_hc.pay_plan_code
   AND start_hc.grade = end_hc.grade
  FULL OUTER JOIN seps
    ON COALESCE(start_hc.pay_plan_code, end_hc.pay_plan_code) = seps.pay_plan_code
   AND COALESCE(start_hc.grade, end_hc.grade) = seps.grade
),
total_row AS (
  SELECT
    'TOTAL' AS grade,
    SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2025-09-01`) AS `headcount at 2025-09-01`,
    SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2026-08-01`) AS `headcount at 2026-08-01`,
    SUM(by_grade.`separations in the twelve months (all categories)`) AS `separations in the twelve months (all categories)`,
    SUM(by_grade.`separations in the twelve months excluding 2025 deferred resignation program separations`) AS `separations in the twelve months excluding 2025 deferred resignation program separations`,
    CASE
      WHEN SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2025-09-01`) + SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2026-08-01`) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE try_divide(100.0 * SUM(by_grade.`separations in the twelve months (all categories)`),(try_divide((SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2025-09-01`) + SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2026-08-01`)),2.0)))
    END AS `rate with all separations`,
    CASE
      WHEN SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2025-09-01`) + SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2026-08-01`) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE try_divide(100.0 * SUM(by_grade.`separations in the twelve months excluding 2025 deferred resignation program separations`),(try_divide((SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2025-09-01`) + SUM(by_grade.`headcount at 2026-08-01`)),2.0)))
    END AS `rate excluding deferred resignation program separations`,
    CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN by_grade.any_imputed_location_used = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN true ELSE false END AS any_imputed_location_used,
    'ZZZ' AS sort_pay_plan_code,
    'ZZZ' AS sort_grade,
    1 AS sort_total
  FROM by_grade
)
SELECT
  result.grade,
  result.`headcount at 2025-09-01`,
  result.`headcount at 2026-08-01`,
  result.`separations in the twelve months (all categories)`,
  result.`separations in the twelve months excluding 2025 deferred resignation program separations`,
  result.`rate with all separations`,
  result.`rate excluding deferred resignation program separations`,
  result.any_imputed_location_used
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM by_grade
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM total_row
) result
ORDER BY result.sort_total, result.sort_pay_plan_code, result.sort_grade

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

About 7,700 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) could reach a common retirement-eligibility threshold within five years of the August 2026 snapshot. Of these, 5,463 are already 50 or older with 20 or more years of service, and another 2,245 aged 45 to 49 with 20 or more years will pass age 50 by August 2031. The total is 7,708 of 27,299 officers.

The records have no retirement-eligibility field, so the threshold (age 50 with 20 years of service, the federal law-enforcement early-retirement rule) is my assumption, not something the data states. The service buckets stop at 20 years, so officers under 50 with 25 years or more cannot be separated out, and some of the 1,877 aged 45 to 49 with 10 to 20 years will cross 20 years in the window. The count is therefore a floor. Every row carries the imputed-location flag, which does not change age or service. The 65-and-over bracket returned no rows.

I read "could retire" as age 50 or older with 20 or more years of service by August 2031 under that threshold; if you meant another eligibility rule or the count of actual retirements, say so.

```sql
WITH `base` AS (
  SELECT
    `ws`.`age_bracket`,
    CASE
      WHEN `ws`.`length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN '<1'
      WHEN `ws`.`length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `ws`.`length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN `ws`.`length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `ws`.`length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN `ws`.`length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `ws`.`length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN `ws`.`length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `ws`.`length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN `ws`.`length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20+'
    END AS `length_of_service_bucket`,
    `ws`.`location_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot` AS `ws`
  WHERE `ws`.`snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `ws`.`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `ws`.`occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `ws`.`age_bracket` IN ('20-24', '25-29', '30-34', '35-39', '40-44', '45-49', '50-54', '55-59', '60-64', '65 or more')
    AND `ws`.`age_bracket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `ws`.`length_of_service_years` IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  `age_bracket`,
  `length_of_service_bucket`,
  `location_imputed`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  COUNT(*) AS `total_headcount`
FROM `base`
WHERE `length_of_service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  `age_bracket`,
  `length_of_service_bucket`,
  `location_imputed`
ORDER BY
  CASE `age_bracket`
    WHEN '20-24' THEN 1
    WHEN '25-29' THEN 2
    WHEN '30-34' THEN 3
    WHEN '35-39' THEN 4
    WHEN '40-44' THEN 5
    WHEN '45-49' THEN 6
    WHEN '50-54' THEN 7
    WHEN '55-59' THEN 8
    WHEN '60-64' THEN 9
    WHEN '65 or more' THEN 10
    ELSE 99
  END,
  CASE `length_of_service_bucket`
    WHEN '<1' THEN 1
    WHEN '1-3' THEN 2
    WHEN '3-5' THEN 3
    WHEN '5-10' THEN 4
    WHEN '10-20' THEN 5
    WHEN '20+' THEN 6
    ELSE 99
  END,
  `location_imputed`
```

question_text:
The analyst supplies this fact, which the data does not contain: The government was shut down from October 1 to November 12, 2025.

Redo that with the shutdown taken out.
turn_1_answer_text:
Verified
CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) landed 475 accessions against a plan of 594 hires in FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025), a variance of -119 hires (-20.0% of plan). Later OPM files add accessions, so this gap will narrow as late actions are reported. I read this as the plan variance for the open cell, CBP Officers in FY2026 Q1; if you meant another measure, such as separations, say so.
answer_text:
Verified
Assuming, as you state, that no one could be onboarded from October 1 to November 12, 2025, the plan scaled to the days hiring was possible is about 316 hires. The 475 actual accessions would then be 158.6 hires (50.1%) above that scaled plan, compared with 119 hires (20.0%) below the full plan of 594. The shutdown is your assumption, not something the data records, so this comparison does not show that the shutdown caused the gap or its reversal.

- Days in the quarter: October 1 to December 31, 2025 = 31 + 30 + 31 = 92
- Days hiring could not happen: October 1 to November 12 = 31 + 12 = 43
- Days hiring was possible: 92 - 43 = 49

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory
The OPM data shows 1,041 separations of TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, 1802) with effective dates in October and November 2025, of which 702 were quits. That is 1,110 minus 1,041 = 69 fewer than the figure given to Congress; the data does not show what counting rule produced 1,110. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly. Only 4 of the 1,041 came through the 2025 deferred resignation program. Quits were 702 of 1,041, about 67 percent.

I read this as all separation categories for TSA screeners in effective months October and November 2025; if you meant only the 1,110 figure's definition or a different month range, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT
    separation.separation_category,
    separation.drp_indicator
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE '2025-11-30'
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1802'
    AND separation.separation_category IS NOT NULL
), counts AS (
  SELECT
    filtered.separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN filtered.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS drp_count,
    0 AS sort_order
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY filtered.separation_category
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'TOTAL' AS separation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS separation_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN filtered.drp_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS drp_count,
    1 AS sort_order
  FROM filtered
)
SELECT
  counts.separation_category,
  counts.separation_count,
  counts.drp_count
FROM counts
ORDER BY counts.sort_order, counts.separation_count DESC, counts.separation_category
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory

OPM records show 94 accessions for FEMA (HSCB), all occupational series, effective October 2025 through May 2026. That is 40 below GAO's 134 (94 is 70% of 134). Of the 94, 92 are new hire appointments (78 excepted service, 9 competitive service, 5 Senior Executive Service) and 2 are transfers in. Counting new hires only gives 92, still 42 below GAO's figure.

The monthly file records effective months, not days, so the cutoff at May 15 could not be applied. The 94 therefore covers all of May 2026, and the count through mid-May is at most 94, so the gap to GAO is at least 40. May alone holds 76 of the 94 (81%), and late reports keep arriving, so recent counts will grow. February 2026 has no recorded accessions. GAO's counting method is not in the data, so I cannot say why the figures differ.

I read "hired" as all accession records for FEMA, all series, from October 2025 through mid-May 2026; if you meant new hire appointments only, that is 92. Monthly counts: October 2025 1, November 8, December 1, January 2026 5, February 0, March 2, April 1, May 76.

The first query's new-hire split (0) was wrong because its category labels did not match the stored text; the second query corrects it.

First query:
```sql
WITH filtered_accessions AS (
  SELECT
    accession.effective_month,
    accession.accession_category
  FROM workforce.semantic.accession
  WHERE accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSCB'
    AND accession.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND accession.effective_month >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND accession.effective_month <= DATE '2026-05-15'
),
monthly AS (
  SELECT
    date_format(accession.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM') AS effective_month_yyyy_mm,
    COUNT(*) AS total_accessions,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.accession_category IN ('NEW HIRE - COMPETITIVE SERVICE', 'NEW HIRE - EXCEPTED SERVICE') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS new_hire_accessions,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.accession_category IN ('NEW HIRE - COMPETITIVE SERVICE', 'NEW HIRE - EXCEPTED SERVICE') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS other_accessions,
    MIN(accession.effective_month) AS month_sort_date
  FROM filtered_accessions AS accession
  GROUP BY date_format(accession.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM')
),
period_total AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_accessions,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.accession_category IN ('NEW HIRE - COMPETITIVE SERVICE', 'NEW HIRE - EXCEPTED SERVICE') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS new_hire_accessions,
    SUM(CASE WHEN accession.accession_category IN ('NEW HIRE - COMPETITIVE SERVICE', 'NEW HIRE - EXCEPTED SERVICE') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS other_accessions
  FROM filtered_accessions AS accession
)
SELECT
  monthly.effective_month_yyyy_mm,
  monthly.total_accessions,
  monthly.new_hire_accessions,
  monthly.other_accessions,
  'MONTH' AS row_type
FROM monthly
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS effective_month_yyyy_mm,
  period_total.total_accessions,
  period_total.new_hire_accessions,
  period_total.other_accessions,
  'TOTAL' AS row_type
FROM period_total
ORDER BY CASE WHEN row_type = 'TOTAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, effective_month_yyyy_mm
```

Second query:
```sql
SELECT
  accession.accession_category,
  COUNT(*) AS accession_record_count
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession` AS accession
WHERE accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSCB'
  AND accession.effective_month IS NOT NULL
  AND accession.accession_category IS NOT NULL
  AND accession.effective_month >= DATE '2025-10-01'
  AND accession.effective_month <= DATE '2026-05-15'
GROUP BY accession.accession_category
ORDER BY accession_record_count DESC, accession.accession_category ASC
```

```sql
WITH `months` AS (

), `accession_counts` AS (

FROM `months`
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration (HSBC), series 1802) had an average annual basic pay of $74,762.38 on the August 2026 snapshot, against $104,655.83 for CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection (HSBD), series 1895), a gap of $29,893.45 (CBP about 40% higher). Pay is estimated for most rows: 42,225 of the 46,913 TSA screener rows and all 27,650 CBP Officer rows had pay filled in from job postings because OPM redacted it, so both averages are estimates. The averages cover all employees in each series on the snapshot, not the plan or the trailing year. I read "salary" as annual basic pay and the average as the mean across all staff in each series; if you meant median pay or pay by grade, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_annual_basic_pay`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `pay_imputed_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND `occupational_series_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND ((`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802')
    OR (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'))
GROUP BY
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`
ORDER BY `agency_subelement_code`, `occupational_series_code`
```

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory
As of the August 2026 snapshot, the ten duty-station cities with the most CBP Officers (customs and border protection, series 1895) are led by Washington, DC (1,920), then Sterling and Ashburn, Virginia, and El Paso, Texas, out of 27,650 officers in total.

| City | CBP Officers |
|---|---|
| Washington, District of Columbia | 1,920 |
| Sterling, Virginia | 751 |
| Ashburn, Virginia | 678 |
| El Paso, Texas | 561 |
| Detroit, Michigan | 440 |
| New Orleans, Louisiana | 375 |
| Houston, Texas | 368 |
| Blaine, Washington | 362 |
| Miami, Florida | 338 |
| Derby Line, Vermont | 321 |

All 27,650 location rows are estimated (imputed from USAJOBS postings), not published by OPM. These counts show where DHS advertises and hires, not necessarily where officers sit. The standard masking test covers FEMA and CISA only, not CBP. It gave a state match share of 0.1174 for FEMA and 0.2817 for CISA, and it flatters the method for CBP and TSA, whose staff spread across many ports and airports. I read this as the August 2026 headcount by city; if you meant the FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025) picture or the count for all CBP occupations, say so.

```sql
WITH `base` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    `location_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
),
`totals` AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS `total_headcount`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `imputed_location_rows`
  FROM `base`
),
`city_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    COUNT(*) AS `employee_count`
  FROM `base`
  WHERE `duty_station_city` IS NOT NULL
    AND `duty_station_state` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `duty_station_city`, `duty_station_state`
),
`ranked` AS (
  SELECT
    `duty_station_city`,
    `duty_station_state`,
    `employee_count`,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY `employee_count` DESC, `duty_station_city` ASC, `duty_station_state` ASC) AS `city_rank`
  FROM `city_counts`
)
SELECT
  `r`.`duty_station_city`,
  `r`.`duty_station_state`,
  `r`.`employee_count`,
  `t`.`imputed_location_rows`,
  `t`.`total_headcount`
FROM `ranked` AS `r`
CROSS JOIN `totals` AS `t`
WHERE `r`.`city_rank` <= 10
ORDER BY `r`.`employee_count` DESC, `r`.`duty_station_city` ASC, `r`.`duty_station_state` ASC
```

question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory

889 USAJOBS postings across all of DHS listed series 1896 (Border Patrol Agent) and opened between September 1, 2025 and October 31, 2026, counting postings that list several series once each. Monthly counts ran from 43 (December 2025) to 92 (August 2026), and the monthly figures sum to the 889 total. Postings are announcements, not hires, and the count can only be read as an upper bound on what was open, since postings filled or cancelled early are not visible. I read this as postings by open date within that window; if you meant postings still open at some date, or a count of hires, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT
    `control_number`,
    `open_date`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `open_date` <= DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND `occupational_series_codes` IS NOT NULL
    AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1896')
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    date_format(DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', `open_date`), 'yyyy-MM') AS `open_month`,
    COUNT(DISTINCT `control_number`) AS `posting_count`
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', `open_date`)
)
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS `open_month`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT `control_number`) AS `posting_count`
FROM filtered
UNION ALL
SELECT
  `open_month`,
  `posting_count`
FROM monthly
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `open_month` = 'TOTAL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, `open_month`
```

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory
No. Higher-grade CBP Officer postings (grades 12 to 15) close faster, with a median of about 6 days each, while the lower grades 5 and 9 stay open about 28 to 30 days at the median. This covers CBP Officer (series 1895, Customs and Border Protection) announcements opened from September 1, 2025 to October 31, 2026, measured as the announced close date minus the open date. Grades 5 and 9 are small groups (14 and 22 postings), so those medians are less firm than the grade 12 to 13 figures (57 and 211 postings).

I read this as the announced posting length by minimum grade; if you meant how many postings are still open on a given date, or how long postings took to fill, say so, since filled-early postings are not visible in the data.

```sql
SELECT
  `minimum_grade` AS `minimum_grade`,
  COUNT(*) AS `posting_count`,
  AVG(DATEDIFF(`close_date`, `open_date`)) AS `average_days_open`,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY DATEDIFF(`close_date`, `open_date`)) AS `median_days_open`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
  AND (`series` = '1895' OR array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1895'))
  AND `open_date` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
  AND `open_date` <= DATE '2026-10-31'
  AND `minimum_grade` IS NOT NULL
  AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
  AND `close_date` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `minimum_grade`
ORDER BY `minimum_grade`
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory
CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) had 586 retirement separations in the twelve months from September 2025 to August 2026. December 2025 was the peak at 152, and November 2025 the low at 24. Late reports keep arriving, so the recent months, especially August 2026, will grow slightly. I read "retire" as all three retirement categories (voluntary, early out, and other) over the trailing twelve months to August 2026; if you meant only voluntary retirements or a different window, say so.

Query run:
```sql
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `retirement_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `separation_category` IN (
      'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY',
      'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT',
      'RETIREMENT - OTHER'
    )
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month`, `retirement_count`
FROM monthly
UNION ALL
SELECT 'TOTAL' AS `effective_month`, SUM(`retirement_count`) AS `retirement_count`
FROM monthly
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `effective_month` = 'TOTAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, `effective_month`
```

question_text: How many CBP Officers who left this year had less than one year of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory
170 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) with less than one year of service separated in the twelve months to August 2026 (September 2025 to August 2026). The breakdown is 78 other separations, 76 quits, 14 terminations (expired appointments or other), and 2 individual transfers out. None came through the 2025 deferred resignation wave, so the count is the same with and without it. Late reports keep arriving, so this count will grow.

I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026, the latest period available. If you meant calendar 2026 to date (January to August 2026), or the open quarter of FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025), say so and I will rerun it.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT
    `separation_category`,
    `drp_indicator`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `length_of_service_years` IS NOT NULL
    AND `length_of_service_years` < 1
), `category_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `separation_category` AS `breakdown`,
    COUNT(*) AS `count_including_drp`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` <> 'Y' OR `drp_indicator` IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `count_excluding_drp`
  FROM `filtered`
  WHERE `separation_category` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `separation_category`
), `total_count` AS (
  SELECT
    'TOTAL' AS `breakdown`,
    COUNT(*) AS `count_including_drp`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` <> 'Y' OR `drp_indicator` IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `count_excluding_drp`
  FROM `filtered`
)
SELECT
  `breakdown`,
  `count_including_drp`,
  `count_excluding_drp`
FROM `total_count`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  `breakdown`,
  `count_including_drp`,
  `count_excluding_drp`
FROM `category_counts`
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `breakdown` = 'TOTAL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, `breakdown`
```

Grade 12 alone, the largest group, separated at 0.032. The overall rate for the cell is 0.035 (954 separations), and no separations in this cell are flagged as deferred resignation program, so the rate excluding that wave is also 0.035. question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

About 11,400 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895), roughly 41% of the 27,650 on the August 2026 snapshot, reach law-enforcement retirement eligibility by August 2031. About 6,200 of them are already eligible. Eligibility is not retirement: it is the pool that could leave, not a forecast of how many will.

The eligibility rule is my assumption, not something the data contains: age 50 with 20 years of service, or 25 years at any age. The buckets are five-year age brackets and service bands, so the counts are approximate at the edges. Already eligible (August 2026): age 50 and over with 20+ years, 5,760 (50-54: 2,483; 55-59: 2,130; 60-64: 850; 65+: 297); age 45-49 with 25+ years, 407; age 40-44 with 25+ years, 26. Total 6,193. Becoming eligible by August 2031: age 50 and over with 15-19 years, 1,325 (767 + 333 + 176 + 49); age 45-49 with 15-24 years, 3,168 (1,330 + 1,838); age 40-44 with 20-24 years, 673; age 35-39 with 20-24 years, 28. Total 5,194. Sum: 6,193 + 5,194 = 11,387. The location flags on these rows are estimated, but the age and service counts do not depend on location.

I read "could retire" as eligibility under the law-enforcement rule above, within five years of the August 2026 snapshot. If you meant the general federal retirement rules or expected separations, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.age_bracket,
    CASE
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 0 AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 5 THEN '0-4'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 5 AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 10 THEN '5-9'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 10 AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 15 THEN '10-14'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 15 AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 20 THEN '15-19'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 20 AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years < 25 THEN '20-24'
      WHEN workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years >= 25 THEN '25 or more'
    END AS service_group,
    workforce_snapshot.location_imputed
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.age_bracket IS NOT NULL
    AND workforce_snapshot.age_bracket IN ('20-24', '25-29', '30-34', '35-39', '40-44', '45-49', '50-54', '55-59', '60-64', '65 or more', '65 OR MORE')
    AND workforce_snapshot.length_of_service_years IS NOT NULL
), normalized AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN filtered.age_bracket = '65 OR MORE' THEN '65 or more'
      ELSE filtered.age_bracket
    END AS age_bracket,
    filtered.service_group,
    filtered.location_imputed
  FROM filtered
  WHERE filtered.service_group IS NOT NULL
), grouped AS (
  SELECT
    normalized.age_bracket,
    normalized.service_group,
    normalized.location_imputed,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount
  FROM normalized
  GROUP BY
    normalized.age_bracket,
```

answer_text:
Verified
Assuming, as you state, that no one could be onboarded from October 1 to November 12, 2025, the plan scaled to the days hiring was possible is about 316 hires. The 475 actual accessions then land 159 hires (50.1%) above that scaled plan, compared with 119 hires (20.0%) below the full plan of 594 for CBP Officers in FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025).

- Days in the quarter: October 1 to December 31, 2025 = 31 + 30 + 31 = 92
- Days hiring could not happen: October 1 to November 12 = 31 + 12 = 43
- Days hiring was possible: 92 − 43 = 49
- Scaled plan: 594 × 49 / 92 = 316.4
- Variance against the scaled plan: 475 − 316.4 = +158.6, about +159 hires, or 158.6 / 316.4 = 50.1%

This comparison does not show that the shutdown explains the gap; it only shows where the actuals fall under your assumption. Late OPM files can still add accessions. Accessions by month for October to December 2025 would test the assumption directly, and a one-off query can produce them if you want that.

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory

TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration (TSA), series 1802) recorded 1,041 separations of all kinds effective in October and November 2025 in the OPM data: 541 in October and 500 in November. Of those, 702 were quits (372 in October and 330 in November). That is 69 below the figure of about 1,110 that TSA gave Congress, and the data does not show why the two differ. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow. Only 2 of the quits carried the 2025 deferred resignation program flag, both in October.

I read "those" as all TSA screener separations effective in October and November 2025, and "quits" as the QUIT category; if you meant separations by the month they were reported, or a different count, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    `separation_category`,
    `drp_indicator`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802'
    AND `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `separation_category` IS NOT NULL
), detailed AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    `separation_category`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `drp_separation_count`,
    'detail' AS `row_type`
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY `effective_month`, `separation_category`
), totals AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS `effective_month`,
    `separation_category`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `drp_separation_count`,
    'two_month_total' AS `row_type`
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY `separation_category`
)
SELECT
  `effective_month`,
  `separation_category`,
  `separation_count`,
  `drp_separation_count`,
  `row_type`
FROM detailed
UNION ALL
SELECT
  `effective_month`,
  `separation_category`,
  `separation_count`,
  `drp_separation_count`,
  `row_type`
FROM totals
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN `row_type` = 'detail' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
  `effective_month`,
  `separation_category`
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory

OPM's accession records show 94 accessions at FEMA (HSCB) with effective dates from October 2025 through May 2026, 40 fewer than GAO's 134 (about 30 percent below). Of the 94, 78 are excepted service appointments, 9 competitive service appointments, 5 Senior Executive Service appointments, and 2 transfers in. The monthly records carry only the first day of each month, so the mid-May cutoff could not be applied and the 94 includes all of May 2026. May alone accounts for 76 of the 94, including 74 excepted service appointments. October 2025 through April 2026 totals 18, so a true mid-May figure would fall between 18 and 94, and the data cannot narrow it. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts may grow slightly. I cannot tell from the data what GAO counted.

I read "hired" as all accessions, new hires plus transfers in, for October 2025 through May 2026. If you meant new hires only, the count is 87 (9 competitive plus 78 excepted service, excluding SES appointments and transfers in). Excluding only the 2 transfers in gives 92.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT
    `a`.`effective_month`,
    `a`.`accession_category`,
    `a`.`source_file`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession` AS `a`
  WHERE `a`.`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSCB'
    AND `a`.`effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `a`.`effective_month` >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND `a`.`effective_month` <= DATE '2026-05-15'
), `all_source_files` AS (
  SELECT
    array_join(sort_array(collect_set(`f`.`source_file`)), ', ') AS `source_files`
  FROM `filtered` AS `f`
  WHERE `f`.`source_file` IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS `row_type`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `effective_month_yyyy_mm`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `accession_category`,
  COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`,
  (SELECT `source_files` FROM `all_source_files`) AS `source_files`
FROM `filtered`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'DETAIL' AS `row_type`,
  date_format(`f`.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month_yyyy_mm`,
  `f`.`accession_category`,
  COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`,
  (SELECT `source_files` FROM `all_source_files`) AS `source_files`
FROM `filtered` AS `f`
WHERE `f`.`accession_category` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  date_format(`f`.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM'),
  `f`.`accession_category`
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN `row_type` = 'TOTAL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
  `effective_month_yyyy_mm`,
  `accession_category`
```

question_text: Month by month, how many CBP Officers did we hire from September 2025 to August 2026?
answer_text:
Exploratory
CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) had 2,456 accessions from September 2025 to August 2026, by month: 224, 80, 236, 159, 232, 166, 243, 159, 319, 160, 242 and 236 (the sum of the twelve monthly counts). The low was October 2025 (80) and the high was May 2026 (319). Later OPM files can still add accessions, so the most recent months will grow. The location and pay fields on these rows are estimated from job postings, but the counts do not depend on them. I read this as all accession categories, counted by effective month, for the twelve months to August 2026; if you meant the quarterly plan variance, say so.

```sql
WITH `months` AS (
  SELECT explode(sequence(to_date('2025-09-01'), to_date('2026-08-01'), interval 1 month)) AS `effective_month`
), `agg` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS `any_location_imputed`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS `any_pay_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= to_date('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= to_date('2026-08-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  date_format(`months`.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month`,
  COALESCE(`agg`.`accession_count`, 0) AS `accession_count`,
  COALESCE(`agg`.`any_location_imputed`, false) AS `any_location_imputed`,
  COALESCE(`agg`.`any_pay_imputed`, false) AS `any_pay_imputed`
FROM `months`
LEFT JOIN `agg`
  ON `months`.`effective_month` = `agg`.`effective_month`
ORDER BY `months`.`effective_month` ASC
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration (HSBC), 1802) averaged $74,762 in annual basic pay across 46,913 staff, about $29,893 (roughly 29%) below CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection (HSBD), 1895), who averaged $104,656 across 27,650 staff. Both averages are estimated: 42,225 of the TSA rows (about 90%) and all 27,650 CBP rows had pay filled in from job postings because OPM redacted it, so treat these as estimates. I read "average salary" as the mean annualized basic pay across all grades for each cell in the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant the median or a different month, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_annual_basic_pay`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `pay_imputed_row_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND (
    (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802')
    OR
    (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895')
  )
GROUP BY
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`
```

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory
Washington, District of Columbia (1,920) leads the CBP Officer headcount in the August 2026 snapshot, followed by Sterling, Virginia (751), Ashburn, Virginia (678), and El Paso, Texas (561). The top ten are in the block below.
All of these city figures are estimated, not published: every row was filled in from job postings, which show where DHS hires rather than where officers sit. On the masking test, the state match was 0.1174 for FEMA and 0.2817 for CISA, and the test flatters the method for CBP, whose staff spread across many ports. Rows without a city or state were left out of the ranking.
I read this as CBP Officer headcount by duty station city at the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant FY2026 Q1 or a state-level count, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `duty_station_city`,
  `duty_station_state`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `location_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `location_imputed_rows`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
  AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
  AND `duty_station_city` IS NOT NULL
  AND `duty_station_state` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  `duty_station_city`,
  `duty_station_state`
ORDER BY `headcount` DESC, `duty_station_city` ASC, `duty_station_state` ASC
```

question_text: Add up the first three quarters of FY2026: how far behind plan is each component on hiring?
answer_text:
**Verified**
Eight of the twelve components are behind plan on hiring across FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (October 2025 to June 2026). FEMA is furthest behind, at 1,896 hires short (92.8% of plan), and TSA is 1,032 short (43.6%). DHS as a whole landed 17,370 accessions against 15,064 planned, 2,306 hires (15.3%) ahead.

| Component | Planned hires | Actual accessions | Variance (hires) | Variance (% of plan) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FEMA (HSCB) | 2,043 | 147 | −1,896 | −92.8% |
| TSA (HSBC) | 2,368 | 1,336 | −1,032 | −43.6% |
| Coast Guard (HSAC) | 567 | 198 | −369 | −65.1% |
| CISA (HSCA) | 303 | 18 | −285 | −94.1% |
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 441 | 228 | −213 | −48.3% |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 1,203 | 1,053 | −150 | −12.5% |
| OIG (HSAE) | 36 | 5 | −31 | −86.1% |
| S&T (HSFA) | 18 | 1 | −17 | −94.4% |
| ICE (HSBB) | 3,186 | 7,573 | +4,387 | +137.7% |
| CBP (HSBD) | 4,182 | 5,734 | +1,552 | +37.1% |
| Secret Service (HSAD) | 627 | 884 | +257 | +41.0% |
| FLETC (HSBE) | 90 | 193 | +103 | +114.4% |

Late OPM files keep adding accessions, so the shortfalls will narrow. ICE's lead rests mostly on FY2026 Q1 (6,185 accessions against 1,062 planned); it was behind plan in Q2 (−39) and Q3 (−697), so check that first quarter before this goes to OPM.

I read "behind plan" as the variance in hires summed over the three quarters, with the percentage of plan alongside; if you meant a single quarter or the count of components behind in each quarter, say so.

question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory
889 USAJOBS announcements listed Border Patrol Agent (series 1896) among their occupational series, counting all of DHS and postings that list several series, with an open date from September 1, 2025 through October 31, 2026. The one-off query returned no location or pay imputation flags for these postings, so no estimated figures apply. Postings are counted by open date, so a posting opened late in the window is included even if it closed after it. I read this as all announcements opened in that window across every component; if you meant only the postings open on a given date, or only one component, say so.

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. Among the 469 CBP Officer (1895) postings opened from September 1, 2025 to October 31, 2026, the higher-grade announcements (minimum grade 12 to 15) stayed open about 6 to 8 days on average. The lower-grade announcements stayed open longest: GS-5 averaged 29.3 days and GS-9 averaged 22.4 days.

By minimum grade: grade 12 averaged 7.7 days (median 6, 57 postings), grade 13 averaged 7.4 (median 6, 211), grade 14 averaged 5.8 (median 6, 126), and grade 15 averaged 6.4 (median 6, 32). The long GS-5 and GS-9 windows come from the monthly "CBPO" announcements, which stay open 25 to 32 days. Days open is the announced close date minus the open date. It measures the advertised window, not time to fill, because the records hold no applicants or hire links. Some postings close after the data ends, so their windows are as announced, and the median is unaffected by the longest one (181 days).

I read "higher-grade" as minimum grade and "CBP Officer postings" as all series 1895 announcements, including the Office of Field Operations listings, opened September 1, 2025 to October 31, 2026. If you meant maximum grade or a single opening month, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered_postings AS (
  SELECT
    job_posting.control_number,
    job_posting.announcement_number,
    job_posting.open_date,
    job_posting.close_date,
    job_posting.minimum_grade,
    job_posting.maximum_grade,
    datediff(job_posting.close_date, job_posting.open_date) AS days_open,
    CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS location_imputed,
    CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS pay_imputed
  FROM workforce.semantic.job_posting
  WHERE job_posting.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND (job_posting.series = '1895' OR array_contains(job_posting.occupational_series_codes, '1895'))
    AND job_posting.open_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-01' AND DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND job_posting.open_date IS NOT NULL
    AND job_posting.close_date IS NOT NULL
),
summary_by_grade AS (
  SELECT
    filtered_postings.minimum_grade,
    AVG(filtered_postings.days_open) AS avg_days_open,
    percentile_approx(filtered_postings.days_open, 0.5) AS median_days_open,
    COUNT(*) AS posting_count
  FROM filtered_postings
  WHERE filtered_postings.minimum_grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY filtered_postings.minimum_grade
)
SELECT
  'posting_detail' AS result_type,
  filtered_postings.control_number,
  filtered_postings.announcement_number,
  filtered_postings.open_date,
  filtered_postings.close_date,
  filtered_postings.minimum_grade,
  filtered_postings.maximum_grade,
  filtered_postings.days_open,
  CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS avg_days_open,
  CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS median_days_open,
  CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS posting_count,
  filtered_postings.location_imputed,
  filtered_postings.pay_imputed
FROM filtered_postings
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'grade_summary' AS result_type,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS control_number,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS announcement_number,
  CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS open_date,
  CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS close_date,
  summary_by_grade.minimum_grade,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS maximum_grade,
  CAST(NULL AS INT) AS days_open,
  summary_by_grade.avg_days_open,
  summary_by_grade.median_days_open,
  summary_by_grade.posting_count,
  CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS location_imputed,
  CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS pay_imputed
FROM summary_by_grade
ORDER BY result_type, open_date, minimum_grade
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) had 586 retirements over the twelve effective months September 2025 to August 2026. December 2025 was the peak at 152, about 26% of the total, and November 2025 was the low at 24. Retirements ran between 26 and 54 a month in the other months, with a second rise to 44 to 52 a month from January to July 2026. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months, July and August 2026, will grow. The count includes voluntary, early-out and other retirements; I read "retire" that way over the trailing twelve months to August 2026. If you meant a single calendar year, or retirements alone within the separation rate, say so.

```sql
WITH month_spine AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS `effective_month`
), retirement_counts AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `retirement_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `separation_category` IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT', 'RETIREMENT - OTHER')
    AND `effective_month` >= TO_DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  DATE_FORMAT(m.`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month`,
  COALESCE(r.`retirement_count`, 0) AS `retirement_count`,
  SUM(COALESCE(r.`retirement_count`, 0)) OVER () AS `twelve_month_total`
FROM `month_spine` m
LEFT JOIN `retirement_counts` r
  ON m.`effective_month` = r.`effective_month`
ORDER BY m.`effective_month`
```

question_text: Which DHS components lost the most senior executives this year?
answer_text:
Exploratory

DHS Headquarters (HSAA) lost the most senior executives (pay plan ES) over the twelve months to August 2026, with 57 separations, followed by FEMA (HSCB) with 44 and ICE (HSBB) with 37. Counts are not scaled to size: FEMA's 44 separations against 57 senior executives on the August 2026 snapshot is a much heavier loss than HQ's 57 against 107. The counts include both deferred resignation program and other separations, and I did not split them. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow. The senior executive population is small, so single-digit differences are noise.

| Component | Separations, Sep 2025 to Aug 2026 | Senior executives, Aug 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 57 | 107 |
| FEMA (HSCB) | 44 | 57 |
| ICE (HSBB) | 37 | 90 |
| CBP (HSBD) | 31 | 122 |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 30 | 62 |
| CISA (HSCA) | 27 | 24 |
| Secret Service (HSAD) | 23 | 54 |
| S&T (HSFA) | 8 | 13 |
| Coast Guard civilian (HSAC) | 7 | 18 |
| FLETC (HSBE) | 4 | 8 |
| Domestic Nuclear Detection Office (HSDA) | 3 | 0 |
| OIG (HSAE) | 2 | 16 |

TSA (HSBC) does not appear in the result, so it recorded no senior executive separations or headcount. The total across the rows is 273 separations. The Domestic Nuclear Detection Office is not one of the twelve components in the code list, but it is in the records and I have kept it.

I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026 and "senior executives" as pay plan ES. If you meant calendar 2026, or a rate against headcount rather than a count, say so.

```sql
WITH `sep` AS (
  SELECT
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    `agency_subelement`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `pay_plan_code` = 'ES'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `agency_subelement_code`, `agency_subelement`
),
`hc` AS (
  SELECT
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    `agency_subelement`,
    COUNT(*) AS `es_headcount_2026_08_01`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `pay_plan_code` = 'ES'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
    AND `agency_subelement` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `agency_subelement_code`, `agency_subelement`
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(`sep`.`agency_subelement_code`, `hc`.`agency_subelement_code`) AS `agency_subelement_code`,
  COALESCE(`sep`.`agency_subelement`, `hc`.`agency_subelement`) AS `agency_subelement`,
  COALESCE(`hc`.`es_headcount_2026_08_01`, 0) AS `es_headcount_2026_08_01`,
  COALESCE(`sep`.`separation_count`, 0) AS `separation_count`
FROM `sep`
FULL OUTER JOIN `hc`
  ON `sep`.`agency_subelement_code` = `hc`.`agency_subelement_code`
 AND `sep`.`agency_subelement` = `hc`.`agency_subelement`
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

Higher-graded CBP Officers (grades 12 to 15) did not leave at a higher rate than the middle grades. Across the twelve months to August 2026, grades 12 to 15 separated at about 3.2%, while grades 05 to 11 separated at about 4.9%. The pattern is not monotonic: grade 05 was 10.2% and grade 07 was 7.7%, grade 11 was 0.7%, and grade 15 was 6.6% on a small base of about 180 staff. The 2025 deferred resignation wave does not appear in this window, so the rates with and without it are the same. Grade 00 (21.9%) rests on about 32 staff and is too small to read. Headcount in grades 05 and 07 rose sharply between the two snapshots, so averaging the start and end counts is rough for those grades. Grade is the grade on the separation record and on each snapshot.

I read this as the trailing twelve-month separation rate by grade for CBP Officers, September 2025 to August 2026; if you meant the count of separations by grade, or the rate for a single grade band, say so.

```sql
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separations`,

    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`headcount_start_by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_start`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`headcount_end_by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_end`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`grade_rows` AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(s.`grade`, hs.`grade`, he.`grade`) AS `grade`,
    COALESCE(s.`separations`, 0) AS `separations`,
    COALESCE(hs.`headcount_start`, 0) AS `headcount_start`,
    COALESCE(he.`headcount_end`, 0) AS `headcount_end`,
    CASE
      WHEN (COALESCE(hs.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(he.`headcount_end`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE try_divide(COALESCE(s.`separations`, 0),((try_divide((COALESCE(hs.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(he.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0))))
    END AS `rate`,
    CASE
      WHEN (COALESCE(hs.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(he.`headcount_end`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE try_divide(COALESCE(s.`separations_excluding_drp`, 0),((try_divide((COALESCE(hs.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(he.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0))))
    END AS `rate_excluding_drp`
  FROM `separations_by_grade` s
  FULL OUTER JOIN `headcount_start_by_grade` hs
    ON s.`grade` = hs.`grade`
  FULL OUTER JOIN `headcount_end_by_grade` he
    ON COALESCE(s.`grade`, hs.`grade`) = he.`grade`
),
`total_separations` AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS `separations`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` <> 'Y' OR `drp_indicator` IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `separations_excluding_drp`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-08-01'
),
`total_headcount_start` AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS `headcount_start`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE '2025-09-01'
),
`total_headcount_end` AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS `headcount_end`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
),
`total_row` AS (
  SELECT
    'ALL' AS `grade`,
    ts.`separations` AS `separations`,
    ths.`headcount_start` AS `headcount_start`,
    the.`headcount_end` AS `headcount_end`,
    CASE
      WHEN (ths.`headcount_start` + the.`headcount_end`) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE try_divide(ts.`separations`,((try_divide((ths.`headcount_start` + the.`headcount_end`),2.0))))
    END AS `rate`,
    CASE
      WHEN (ths.`headcount_start` + the.`headcount_end`) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE try_divide(ts.`separations_excluding_drp`,((try_divide((ths.`headcount_start` + the.`headcount_end`),2.0))))
    END AS `rate_excluding_drp`
  FROM `total_separations` ts
  CROSS JOIN `total_headcount_start` ths
  CROSS JOIN `total_headcount_end` the
)
SELECT
  `grade`,
  `separations`,
  `headcount_start`,
  `headcount_end`,
  `rate`,
  `rate_excluding_drp`
FROM `grade_rows`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  `grade`,
  `separations`,
  `headcount_start`,
  `headcount_end`,
  `rate`,
  `rate_excluding_drp`
FROM `total_row`
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `grade` = 'ALL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, `grade`
```

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

About 5,760 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) could reach retirement eligibility in the next five years, going by the August 2026 snapshot. That is 3,277 already aged 55 or older with 20 or more years of service, plus 2,483 aged 50 to 54 with 20 or more years who would turn 55 inside the window. That is about 21% of the 27,650 officers on the snapshot.

| Age bracket | Officers with 20+ years | All officers in bracket |
|---|---|---|
| 50-54 (reach 55 within five years) | 2,483 | 3,447 |
| 55-59 | 2,130 | 2,540 |
| 60-64 | 850 | 1,047 |
| 65 or more | 297 | 351 |

This is a count of people at the age and service levels where retirement is common, not a forecast of who will leave. The records hold no retirement-eligibility date or rule, so age 55 with 20 years is my proxy. Not everyone who is eligible retires. I read "could retire" as that proxy and the five-year window; if you meant a different age or service threshold, say so.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%20-24%' THEN '20-24'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%25-29%' THEN '25-29'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%30-34%' THEN '30-34'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%35-39%' THEN '35-39'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%40-44%' THEN '40-44'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%45-49%' THEN '45-49'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%50-54%' THEN '50-54'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%55-59%' THEN '55-59'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%60-64%' THEN '60-64'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%65%' THEN '65 or more'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS `age_bucket`,
    CASE
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20 or more'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS `service_bucket`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `age_bracket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `length_of_service_years` IS NOT NULL
), counts AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bucket`,
    `service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`
  FROM base
  WHERE `age_bucket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `age_bucket`, `service_bucket`
), row_totals AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bucket`,
    'Total' AS `service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount`
  FROM base
  WHERE `age_bucket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `age_bucket`
)
SELECT `age_bucket`, `service_bucket`, `headcount`
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM counts
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM row_totals
) t
ORDER BY
  CASE `age_bucket`
    WHEN '20-24' THEN 1
    WHEN '25-29' THEN 2
    WHEN '30-34' THEN 3
    WHEN '35-39' THEN 4
    WHEN '40-44' THEN 5
    WHEN '45-49' THEN 6
    WHEN '50-54' THEN 7
    WHEN '55-59' THEN 8
    WHEN '60-64' THEN 9
    WHEN '65 or more' THEN 10
    ELSE 11
  END,
  CASE `service_bucket`
    WHEN 'under 1' THEN 1
    WHEN '1-3' THEN 2
    WHEN '3-5' THEN 3
    WHEN '5-10' THEN 4
    WHEN '10-20' THEN 5
    WHEN '20 or more' THEN 6
    WHEN 'Total' THEN 7
    ELSE 8
  END
```

question_text: Which components missed their hiring plan by the most in the first quarter of FY2026?
answer_text:
Verified
FEMA (HSCB) missed its FY2026 Q1 plan (October to December 2025) by the most, at 671 hires short (10 actual accessions against 681 planned, 98.5% below plan). Eight components finished the quarter below plan, and the other four were above it.

| Component | Planned hires | Actual accessions | Shortfall (hires) | % of plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FEMA (HSCB) | 681 | 10 | -671 | -98.5% |
| TSA (HSBC) | 533 | 223 | -310 | -58.2% |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 401 | 200 | -201 | -50.1% |
| Coast Guard (HSAC) | 189 | 76 | -113 | -59.8% |
| CISA (HSCA) | 101 | 4 | -97 | -96.0% |
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 147 | 55 | -92 | -62.6% |
| OIG (HSAE) | 12 | 2 | -10 | -83.3% |
| S&T (HSFA) | 6 | 1 | -5 | -83.3% |

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory
The OPM data shows 1,041 TSA screener (1802) separations with effective dates in October and November 2025, not 1,110. Of those, 702 were quits (about two-thirds): 372 in October and 330 in November. The other 339 were retirements (136) and other separations (203). The records hold no termination, transfer-out, or reduction-in-force rows for this group in those months.

The 69-separation gap from TSA's figure cannot be explained from these records, since they do not show what basis TSA used. Late reports and restatements (about 0.8%) can shift these counts slightly.

I read "left" as all separation categories for TSA screeners, effective October and November 2025, counted by effective month. If you meant the twelve-month separation rate, I can pull that to August 2026.

The one-off query that ran:

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    workforce.semantic.separation.effective_month,
    CASE
      WHEN workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      WHEN workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category ILIKE '%RETIREMENT%' THEN 'RETIREMENT'
      WHEN workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category = 'TERMINATION' THEN 'TERMINATION'
      WHEN workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT'
      WHEN workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category = 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 'REDUCTION IN FORCE'
      ELSE 'OTHER SEPARATION'
    END AS separation_category_group
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE workforce.semantic.separation.effective_month IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
    AND workforce.semantic.separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category IS NOT NULL
    AND workforce.semantic.separation.occupational_series_code = '1802'
    AND (
      workforce.semantic.separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC'
      OR workforce.semantic.separation.agency_subelement ILIKE '%Transportation Security Administration%'
    )
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    base.effective_month,
    base.separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    1 AS sort_group
  FROM base
  GROUP BY base.effective_month, base.separation_category_group
), summary AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'COMBINED TOTAL (ALL CATEGORIES, OCT+NOV 2025)' AS separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    2 AS sort_group
  FROM base
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'COMBINED TOTAL (QUIT ONLY, OCT+NOV 2025)' AS separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations,
    3 AS sort_group
  FROM base
  WHERE base.separation_category_group = 'QUIT'
)
SELECT result.effective_month, result.separation_category_group, result.separations
FROM (
  SELECT monthly.effective_month, monthly.separation_category_group, monthly.separations, monthly.sort_group
  FROM monthly
  UNION ALL
  SELECT summary.effective_month, summary.separation_category_group, summary.separations, summary.sort_group
  FROM summary
) AS result
ORDER BY
  result.sort_group,
  result.effective_month,
  CASE result.separation_category_group
    WHEN 'QUIT' THEN 1
    WHEN 'RETIREMENT' THEN 2
    WHEN 'TERMINATION' THEN 3
    WHEN 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 4
    WHEN 'REDUCTION IN FORCE' THEN 5
    WHEN 'OTHER SEPARATION' THEN 6
    WHEN 'COMBINED TOTAL (ALL CATEGORIES, OCT+NOV 2025)' THEN 7
    WHEN 'COMBINED TOTAL (QUIT ONLY, OCT+NOV 2025)' THEN 8
    ELSE 9
  END
```

question_text: GAO says FEMA hired 134 people from October 2025 to mid-May 2026. What do the OPM numbers show for the same period?
answer_text:
Exploratory
OPM shows 94 accessions for FEMA (HSCB), all occupational series, with effective months from October 2025 through May 2026. That is 40 fewer than GAO's 134. The accession records carry only an effective month, so I could not cut at May 15. The 94 therefore includes all of May (76 of the 94 fall in May 2026), and the true count to May 15 is at most 94. By month: October 2025 1, November 8, December 1, January 2026 5, February 0, March 2, April 1, May 76. Later OPM files can add accessions, so the figure may grow slightly. The gap may also reflect a different definition of "hired" on GAO's side; the data here cannot reconcile it. I read "hired" as OPM accession records (new hires, transfers in, and SES appointments); if you meant another measure, such as hires by announcement date, say so. A second check I ran filtered on accession categories and returned zero for May, which conflicts with the first query, so I have not relied on it.

```sql
WITH `monthly` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `accession_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSCB'
    AND `effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-05-15'
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  `effective_month`,
  DATE_FORMAT(`effective_month`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `effective_month_yyyy_mm`,
  `accession_count`,
  SUM(`accession_count`) OVER () AS `total_accessions`
FROM `monthly`
ORDER BY `effective_month` ASC;
```

```sql
WITH `month_spine` AS (
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration (TSA) (HSBC), series 1802) had an average annual basic pay of $74,762 across 46,913 staff, and CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection (CBP) (HSBD), series 1895) averaged $104,656 across 27,650. The CBP average is about $29,893 (40%) higher. Both figures are estimated: pay was imputed from job postings for 90% of TSA screener rows (42,225 of 46,913) and for every CBP Officer row, because OPM redacted them. I read this as average annual basic pay across all staff in each cell at the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant pay by grade or the FY2026 Q1 pay, say so.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS headcount, AVG(workforce_snapshot.annualized_adjusted_basic_pay) AS average_annual_basic_pay, SUM(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS imputed_pay_rows, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN workforce_snapshot.pay_imputed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN true ELSE false END AS any_pay_imputed FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot` WHERE workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01' AND workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC' AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1802'
```

question_text: Which cities have the most CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

The cities with the most CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) as of the August 2026 snapshot are Washington, DC (1,920), Sterling, Virginia (751), Ashburn, Virginia (678), El Paso, Texas (561), and Detroit, Michigan (440). The top 25 cities together hold 10,220 of the 27,650 officers, about 37%.

Every city figure is estimated: OPM redacted these duty stations, so they were imputed from job postings, which show where DHS hires rather than where officers sit. On the masking test, the imputed state matched the true state 12% of the time for FEMA and 28% for CISA. That test flatters the method for CBP, whose officers are spread across many ports of entry, so these city counts are a rough distribution at best. I read this as the headcount at the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant the open cell's FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025) or the full list of 25 cities, say so.

```sql
WITH population AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_headcount
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `workforce_snapshot`.`snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `workforce_snapshot`.`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `workforce_snapshot`.`occupational_series_code` = '1895'
),
city_counts AS (
  SELECT
    `workforce_snapshot`.`duty_station_city` AS duty_station_city,
    `workforce_snapshot`.`duty_station_state` AS duty_station_state,
    `workforce_snapshot`.`location_imputed` AS location_imputed,
    COUNT(*) AS city_headcount
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `workforce_snapshot`.`snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `workforce_snapshot`.`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `workforce_snapshot`.`occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `workforce_snapshot`.`duty_station_city` IS NOT NULL
    AND `workforce_snapshot`.`duty_station_state` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    `workforce_snapshot`.`duty_station_city`,
    `workforce_snapshot`.`duty_station_state`,
    `workforce_snapshot`.`location_imputed`
)
SELECT
  `city_counts`.`duty_station_city`,
  `city_counts`.`duty_station_state`,
  `city_counts`.`location_imputed`,
  `city_counts`.`city_headcount`,
  `population`.`total_headcount`
FROM city_counts
CROSS JOIN population
ORDER BY `city_counts`.`city_headcount` DESC, `city_counts`.`duty_station_city` ASC, `city_counts`.`duty_station_state` ASC
LIMIT 25
```

question_text: Add up the first three quarters of FY2026: how far behind plan is each component on hiring?
answer_text:
Verified

Across FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (October 2025 to June 2026), eight of the twelve components are behind plan on hiring. FEMA is furthest behind at 1,896 hires short (-92.8% of plan), then TSA at 1,032 short (-43.6%). ICE, CBP, the Secret Service, and FLETC are ahead. Each row sums the three quarterly plan variances, with planned hires and accessions summed separately.

| Component | Planned hires | Actual accessions | Variance (hires) | Variance % of plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FEMA (HSCB) | 2,043 | 147 | -1,896 | -92.8% |
| TSA (HSBC) | 2,368 | 1,336 | -1,032 | -43.6% |
| Coast Guard (HSAC) | 567 | 198 | -369 | -65.1% |
| CISA (HSCA) | 303 | 18 | -285 | -94.1% |
| DHS Headquarters (HSAA) | 441 | 228 | -213 | -48.3% |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 1,203 | 1,053 | -150 | -12.5% |
| OIG (HSAE) | 36 | 5 | -31 | -86.1% |
| S&T (HSFA) | 18 | 1 | -17 | -94.4% |
| ICE (HSBB) | 3,186 | 7,573 | +4,387 | +137.7% |
| CBP (HSBD) | 4,182 | 5,734 | +1,552 | +37.1% |
| Secret Service (HSAD) | 627 | 884 | +257 | +41.0% |
| FLETC (HSBE) | 90 | 193 | +103 | +114.4% |
| DHS total | 15,064 | 17,370 | +2,306 | +15.3% |

The DHS total rests on ICE's 6,185 accessions in FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025) against 1,062 planned, far above its later quarters (1,023 and 365). Check that figure before quoting ICE. Without ICE, DHS is 2,081 short of plan (9,797 accessions against 11,878 planned, -17.5%). Later OPM files keep adding accessions, so these shortfalls will narrow. question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory
889 USAJOBS postings that listed Border Patrol Agent (series 1896) among their series opened between September 1, 2025 and October 31, 2026. Each posting is counted once even when it lists several series. All 889 sit under Customs and Border Protection (CBP) in the returned breakdown. I read "between September 2025 and October 2026" as the posting open date falling in that window, inclusive; if you meant the posting close dates or the open-on-a-date count, say so.

```sql
SELECT 'ALL_DHS' AS `component`, COUNT(DISTINCT `control_number`) AS `posting_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
WHERE `open_date` BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2026-10-31')
  AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1896')
UNION ALL
SELECT `agency_subelement` AS `component`, COUNT(DISTINCT `control_number`) AS `posting_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
WHERE `open_date` BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2026-10-31')
  AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1896')
  AND `agency_subelement` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `agency_subelement`
ORDER BY `component`
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) retired 586 times in the twelve effective months from September 2025 to August 2026. December 2025 is the peak at 152, about three times the monthly average of 49 (586 ÷ 12 ≈ 48.8). The lowest month was November 2025 at 24. Late reports keep arriving, so the recent months will grow slightly.

I read "in the year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026, counting retirements of all three retirement categories, and not as a rate. If you meant a different twelve-month window, or the count with the 2025 deferred resignation wave separated out, say so.

```sql
WITH monthly_counts AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS retirement_count
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.separation_category IN (
      'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY',
      'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT',
      'RETIREMENT - OTHER'
    )
    AND separation.effective_month >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
  GROUP BY separation.effective_month
)
SELECT
  DATE_FORMAT(monthly_counts.effective_month, 'yyyy-MM') AS effective_month,
  monthly_counts.retirement_count
FROM monthly_counts
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS effective_month,
  SUM(monthly_counts.retirement_count) AS retirement_count
FROM monthly_counts
ORDER BY CASE WHEN effective_month = 'TOTAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, effective_month
```

question_text: Which DHS components lost the most senior executives this year?
answer_text:
Exploratory

DHS Headquarters (HSAA) lost the most senior executives: 57 of the 270 senior executive separations across DHS in the twelve months from September 2025 to August 2026. FEMA (HSCB) followed with 44, ICE (HSBB) with 37, and CBP (HSBD) with 31. TSA (HSBC) recorded none. These are counts, not rates. The 270 includes deferred resignation program separations, and I did not split them out. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly.

I read "this year" as the twelve effective months ending August 2026, and "senior executives" as the Senior Executive Service pay plan (ES). If you meant calendar 2026 or the fiscal year, say so.

```sql
WITH `components` AS (
  SELECT * FROM VALUES
    ('HSBD'), ('HSBC'), ('HSBB'), ('HSAB'), ('HSCB'), ('HSAD'),
    ('HSAC'), ('HSAA'), ('HSCA'), ('HSBE'), ('HSAE'), ('HSFA')
  AS `t`(`agency_subelement_code`)
),
`sep` AS (
  SELECT
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
    AND `pay_plan_code` = 'ES'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` IN ('HSBD', 'HSBC', 'HSBB', 'HSAB', 'HSCB', 'HSAD', 'HSAC', 'HSAA', 'HSCA', 'HSBE', 'HSAE', 'HSFA')
  GROUP BY `agency_subelement_code`
),
`hc` AS (
  SELECT
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    COUNT(*) AS `senior_executive_headcount_2026_08_01`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND `pay_plan_code` = 'ES'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` IN ('HSBD', 'HSBC', 'HSBB', 'HSAB', 'HSCB', 'HSAD', 'HSAC', 'HSAA', 'HSCA', 'HSBE', 'HSAE', 'HSFA')
  GROUP BY `agency_subelement_code`
)
SELECT
  `components`.`agency_subelement_code` AS `component_code`,
  COALESCE(`sep`.`separation_count`, 0) AS `separation_count`,
  SUM(COALESCE(`sep`.`separation_count`, 0)) OVER () AS `total_across_all_components`,
  COALESCE(`hc`.`senior_executive_headcount_2026_08_01`, 0) AS `senior_executive_headcount_2026_08_01`
FROM `components`
LEFT JOIN `sep`
  ON `components`.`agency_subelement_code` = `sep`.`agency_subelement_code`
LEFT JOIN `hc`
  ON `components`.`agency_subelement_code` = `hc`.`agency_subelement_code`
ORDER BY `separation_count` DESC, `component_code` ASC
```
